**Traced the 5 signed-URL calls to their real consequence, not assumed from the shape** (`company/registrations/page.tsx:59`, `company/properties/page.tsx:42`, `company/principals/page.tsx:54`, `admin/page.tsx:209`, `experience/[id]/page.tsx:110`) - all four vault-document pages share the identical pattern: `const { data: signed } = await supabase.storage...createSignedUrls(...); for (const s of signed ?? []) ...`. Read every downstream consumer (`HeldRow`/`DocumentLine` in `registrations/page.tsx`/`principals/page.tsx`) - on a failed batch, `urls[path]` is falsy and the UI falls back to showing the filename as **plain text instead of a link**, never to "No copy uploaded" - the compliance status itself (`expiryStatus()`/`path` presence) is computed entirely independently of `urls`, so a failed signed-URL fetch can only break a download link, never flip a compliance read. Confirmed safe, not fixed. Also traced `admin/layout.tsx:23`'s `is_platform_admin()` RPC gate (every `/admin/*` page's own access control) - `if (!isAdmin) notFound()` is fail-closed by construction: a failed RPC read makes `isAdmin` falsy, denying access, never granting it. Confirmed safe, not fixed.

**The real finding: `tender-readiness.ts`'s `computeTenderReadiness()` - traced from `pack-review-data.ts:116/134/232/236/297`'s own untraced hits, three levels deep to where it actually bites.** `pack-review-data.ts` (`loadPackReviewSnapshot()`, the "what will go into this SANRAL pack" preview) wraps each of its 6 sections in its own try/catch, and a failed read inside one (`company`, `key_positions`, `form_answers`, `signature`, `documents`, `form_b7`) already correctly renders as `{ error: "Couldn't load this section: ...", items: [] }` rather than fabricating data - that part is fine. The bug is one level up, in `tender-readiness.ts`'s own `computeTenderReadiness(sections)`, the shared pure function (used by BOTH SANRAL's `pack-review-data.ts` and the general family's `general-pack-review-data.ts`) that flattens those sections into the Verify/Provide/Fix split: its own header comment explicitly argued `section.error` sections should "contribute nothing... silently treating a read failure as '0 items, fully ready' would be worse than leaving it out of the count" - but leaving a failed section's items out of `fix`/`totalCount` has the EXACT SAME effect, at every call site, as if that section really did have 0 Fix items: `fix.length` and `score` can't tell "genuinely nothing to fix" apart from "a section holding a real Fix item just failed to load this render." The existing test file (`tender-readiness.test.ts`, pre-fix) literally codified this as intended behavior (`"a section that failed to load contributes nothing to the count"`, asserting `score: 100`).

**Where this actually bites.** `submission-pack.tsx:169` (SANRAL) and `general-workspace.tsx:259` (general family) both compute their own Submit-button `disabledReason` as `fixCount > 0 ? "Fix N items..." : ...` straight off this function - so a transient read failure in any one Pack Review section could make the button render as enabled/not-blocked when a real, disqualifying Fix item exists but just didn't load this render. Checked `requestSubmissionPack()` (`actions.ts`) on current `main` to see what's actually enforced server-side today: `unfilledPositions` (independently re-verified by the engine, already confirmed safe in a prior pass), `missingTemplates`, `b7.blocker`, the already-queued dedupe, and the pack-review-confirmation gate - but **nothing that re-checks `computeTenderReadiness(...).fix` at all**. That's exactly the gap PR #178 (open, unmerged, "the Fix-item server-side gate") is meant to close - and its own diff adds that check by calling this exact same `computeTenderReadiness()` function in both `actions.ts` and `general-actions.ts`. So today this is "only" a client-rendered-attribute cosmetic gap (a direct POST already bypasses the UI gate regardless, a separate thing PR #178 itself names); but once #178 merges, its new server-side check would inherit this identical blind spot, silently, unless it's also addressed. Also checked `pipeline/page.tsx:331/337`'s own "Pack Ready" board badge (`packHealthStatusFromReadiness(score, fix.length)`) - same shape, cosmetic-only (a dashboard card, not a gate), but a visible false-"ready" signal on Sarel's own Bids board.

**Fixed, on `main`, opened as PR #180 (not pushed directly - gate-adjacent).** `computeTenderReadiness()` now also returns `hasUnreadSection: boolean`. `submission-pack.tsx`/`general-workspace.tsx`'s own `disabledReason` now fails closed ("Couldn't check compliance readiness just now - refresh and try again") when `hasUnreadSection` is true - the pre-existing `packReviewSnapshot.mapped === false`/`!generalReviewSnapshot.mapped` fallback (already its own separate, already-PR'd-for gap) was deliberately left untouched, to keep this PR's diff scoped to the genuinely new finding and not duplicate #178's own change. `packHealthStatusFromReadiness()` (`pipelineCardHelpers.ts`) takes a new optional third `hasUnreadSection` param, returning `"in_progress"` instead of `"ready"` when true even at a 100% score; `pipeline/page.tsx`'s both call sites updated to pass it through. **Left a PR comment on #178** (not an edit to it) explaining the interaction, so whoever reviews #178 for merge knows to pull in #180's fix (or an equivalent check) first or shortly after.

**A second, smaller instance of the same bug class, same PR: `ImpersonationBanner.tsx`.** Found while sweeping the same grep list (`ImpersonationBanner.tsx:33`). A failed `impersonation_audit_logs` read fell through to the exact same `if (!row) return null` branch as a genuinely-ended/stale impersonation session - silently hiding the one reminder this banner exists to give (guardrail 2, its own header comment: "an admin forgetting which account they're acting as"), exactly while a real, still-open impersonation session needs it most. The underlying impersonation session itself is unaffected (enforced by the cookie/RLS, not by whether this banner renders) - this is a safety-reminder gap, not a permission bypass - but it's the same root shape. Fixed: now shows a cautious "Admin Support Mode may still be active - couldn't confirm details just now" banner (with the Exit button still present) on a read error, instead of silently showing nothing. No target name/email available to show on this path (not in the cookie, and the failed read is what would have supplied them) - acceptable, the point is the reminder and the exit path, not the detail.

**Verification, run myself, real exit codes.** `npm run typecheck` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings (caught and fixed one new one along the way - an unescaped apostrophe in the new `ImpersonationBanner.tsx` copy, `react/no-unescaped-entities` - before this entry was written, not after). `npx vitest run` - **453/453 passed, 56/56 test files** (up from 450/56: +3 new `pipelineCardHelpers.spec.ts` assertions). The corrected per-file `*.test.ts` loop (no `--test` flag) - **27 files, 303 tests, 0 failures** (up from 301/27: +2 new `tender-readiness.test.ts` assertions). `npx next build` - **compiled successfully**, same route table, `Proxy (Middleware)` present.

**Did not re-trace the remaining ~25 of 49 hits exhaustively.** Traced to a real consequence: the 5 signed-URL calls (safe), `admin/layout.tsx:23` (safe), `pack-review-data.ts`'s 5 untraced hits (the real finding, above), `ImpersonationBanner.tsx:33` (the second finding, above). ## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): took the immediately-preceding pass's own "stop refining the grep, read files from scratch" suggestion literally - picked 5 representative Server Action/data-loading files never previously reviewed by name, read each genuinely end-to-end with no grep filter at all, and it surfaced a real (if low-severity) instance of the false-all-clear shape in 1 of the 5 that EVERY prior grep pass would have missed structurally, not just by an exclusion-rule gap - fixed with a behavior change; the other 4 came back genuinely clean. Also confirms, as data, that the from-scratch-read approach is worth continuing over one more grep-pattern refinement.

Oriented from `5727cff` (immediately-preceding pass's own push, `829dbb9`). `git fetch origin main` found zero sibling-session commits, both before starting and again right before this entry's own push - pushed as a clean fast-forward (`5727cff..6424df6`). Re-checked PR #176/#177/#178/#179 (and #164/#165) myself via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open`: all six unchanged from the prior pass's own record - `#179`/`#178`/`#176` `draft: false`, `#177` `draft: true`, `#164`/`#165` both still draft, stale since 2026-10-26. None touched, commented on, or merged this pass.

**Why this angle, and how the 5 files were picked.** The immediately-preceding pass's own entry explicitly named the risk: four consecutive passes each found a new grep EXCLUSION-RULE gap (camelCase guard files, hyphenated `*-actions.ts` files, bare writes, array/tuple destructures) rather than ever asking whether the grep's whole target shape - "find a `data`/`rows` destructure with no `error:` alongside it" - was itself too narrow a model of the bug class. Took that literally: picked files that had genuinely never been named in this doc before (confirmed by grepping every `.ts` filename in `app/app`/`app/lib` against the whole of `System-Status.md` and keeping only 0-mention or peripheral-mention hits), favouring small, varied files over another big Server Action: `app/app/company/digestActions.ts` (32 lines, 0 mentions), `app/app/_components/search-tenders.ts` (34 lines, 0 mentions), `app/app/tenders/[id]/bid-task-status.ts` (75 lines, 0 mentions), `app/app/tenders/[id]/update-actions.ts` (43 lines, mentioned twice before but only inside a grep-output file list, never itself read), `app/app/_components/document-intake/uploadBatch.ts` (94 lines, mentioned 3 times before but only for file-validation/header-comment context, never read for this specific bug shape).

**The finding: `app/app/_components/search-tenders.ts`'s `searchTenders()` - real, low-severity, fixed with a behavior change, and structurally invisible to every version of the TS-sweep's grep.** This one DID capture its error (`const { data, error } = await supabase.from("tenders")...`, `if (error) { console.error(...); return []; }`) - every grep this sweep has ever run (looking for a MISSING `error:` capture) would walk straight past it as already-safe. But the function's own return value on that captured-error branch was a bare `[]`, byte-identical to the genuine "no tender matches this query" result one line below (`return data ?? [];` when `data` is an empty array). Its one caller, `CommandPalette.tsx` (the Cmd/Ctrl+K "jump to a tender by contract number" search), rendered the exact same `<CommandEmpty>Nothing found.</CommandEmpty>` for both - a transient read failure told the user their tender doesn't exist, not that the search itself broke. This is a genuinely distinct dimension of the same root bug class this whole doc has been tracking: not "the error was never captured" (the thing every grep pass has looked for) but "the error was captured and logged, then discarded by collapsing it into the same return shape as a genuine empty result" - no literal-substring grep for `"const { data"` or a missing `error:` token could ever have found this, because there's nothing missing to grep for. Severity is low (a command-palette search convenience, not a compliance gate, hard stop or money path - the realistic consequence is a confused user retyping a contract number, not a disqualification risk or a lost write), consistent with this doc's own established severity calibration for a UI-only false-empty state.

**Fixed.** `searchTenders()` now returns `{ results, error }` instead of a bare array; `CommandPalette.tsx` tracks a `searchFailed` state (reset on close and derived-away, same pattern as the existing `displayedResults` staleness guard, once the query drops back under 2 characters) and shows "Tender search failed - try again." instead of "Nothing found." when the read itself failed. New `app/app/_components/search-tenders.spec.ts` (4 tests), using this repo's own established `vi.mock("@/lib/supabase/server", ...)` convention (copied from `company/actions.spec.ts`) since this file calls `createClient()` internally rather than taking it as a parameter.

**The other 4 files, read in full, genuinely clean:**
- `app/app/company/digestActions.ts` - `setDailyDigestOptIn()`'s one RPC call already captures `error` and redirects with a visible error message on failure; the happy-path `redirect()` after it is unreached code on the error branch (Next.js's `redirect()` throws internally), the same convention used throughout this codebase. No gap.
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/bid-task-status.ts` - pure synchronous classification logic (`classifyComplianceItem()`), no Supabase call, no I/O of any kind. Out of scope for this bug class entirely; read anyway per the directive (no filter), confirmed genuinely nothing to find.
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/update-actions.ts` - `acceptTenderUpdateDate()`'s one RPC call already captures `error` and redirects with a visible error message; same "redirect() throws, nothing after it runs" shape as `digestActions.ts`. No gap.
- `app/app/_components/document-intake/uploadBatch.ts` - per-file upload state machine (`markUploading`/`applyUploadResult`/`partitionBatch`); each file's own storage-upload error is captured, logged, and recorded in that file's own `{ status: "failed", error }` slot - never silently merged into another file's outcome or dropped. Already correctly handles the exact "one failure must not discard others" shape its own header comment documents. No gap.

**Verification, run myself, real exit codes.** `npm run typecheck` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings. `npx vitest run` - **450/450 passed, 56/56 test files** (up from 446/55: +4 tests, +1 file, exactly the new `search-tenders.spec.ts`). The corrected per-file `*.test.ts` loop (no `--test` flag) - **27 files, 301 tests, 0 failures, standing baseline exactly unchanged** (no `.test.ts` file touched - the new coverage went into a `.spec.ts` file). `npx next build` - **compiled successfully**, same route table, `Proxy (Middleware)` present.

**Genuine red-then-green, run myself.** `git stash push -- app/app/_components/search-tenders.ts` (keeping the new spec file in place), reran: 2 of the 4 new tests failed exactly as predicted (`expected undefined to deeply equal [...]` - destructuring `{ results, error }` off the pre-fix bare-array return gives `undefined` for both fields), the other 2 (query-too-short, genuine-no-match) still passed since their expected shape happened to coincide. `git stash pop` restored the fix; all 4 passed again, confirmed.

**Does this confirm the hypothesis?** Yes, with an honest caveat on magnitude. A from-scratch read of 5 small/medium files (representative size for this codebase's Server Action layer) found 1 real, previously-undiscoverable-by-grep instance of the bug class in roughly 20 minutes of reading - a similar hit rate to several of the recent grep-refinement passes, but the KIND of finding is qualitatively different: it is in the grep's blind spot by construction (captured-but-discarded error), not by an exclusion-rule accident, meaning no amount of further grep-pattern refinement on the existing `"const { data"`/missing-`error:` model could ever have found it. That said, the severity this time is genuinely low (UI convenience, not a gate/money/RLS finding) - unlike several recent grep-pass findings (`loadDocumentExpiryOverview()`, `getNotifications()`, `syncWonProjectToTeam()`) which were compliance-adjacent and behaviorally dangerous. One data point is not enough to conclude from-scratch reading strictly dominates grep refinement for THIS codebase's remaining surface, but it is enough to say the grep's fundamental target shape (missing error capture) is provably narrower than the full bug class (error capture discarded into an ambiguous return value), and a future pass should treat "error captured but not meaningfully propagated to the caller" as its own distinct thing to look for - genuinely ungreppable by any literal-substring method tried so far, since the signal is in what the function DOES with a value it already has, not in what syntax is present or absent.

**Backlog status.** 1 real finding fixed with a behavior change, pushed directly to `main` (`6424df6`, no PR) - low severity, additive, no RLS/security-boundary or money-path change, same risk tier as this doc's many prior direct-push fixes. The original standing 43-hit read-grep and the 33-hyphenated-file surface remain untouched this pass (this pass's whole budget went to the from-scratch-read angle instead, per the directive). The 6 standing judgment-call items (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-integrity gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap in `proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, the zero-recipients batched-send sub-case, the live `RESEND_API_KEY` validity question, PR #176/#177/#178/#179 all awaiting Sarel's own merge decision) remain exactly as described - not touched, not resolved. Migrations `0117`-`0120` still on `main`, still not applied to production - untouched this pass. **For a future pass:** either continue the from-scratch-read approach on a fresh batch of never-named files (this pass only covered 5 of the ~150-file `app/app`/`app/lib` surface - plenty left), go back to the two oldest untouched grep threads, or pick a different angle entirely (a fresh `engine/` Python subsystem read, or revisiting a standing judgment-call item) - this pass's own data point is suggestive but not conclusive enough to mandate one over the other.

## Prior pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): a FOURTH systematic blind spot in the TS-sweep's own grep - array/tuple-destructured `Promise.all()` reads never matched the sweep's literal `"const { data"` grep either (a `[` sits between `const` and `{`, or the whole tuple sits on its own line, or several `{ data: x }` members share one long single-line destructure with only ONE `const` at the very start) - found and fixed 24 instances across 15 files, including one genuine hard-stop-adjacent gate finding (traced safe) and two genuine silent-false-"all clear" UI bugs (fixed with real behavior changes, not just logging)

Oriented from `968feaa` (immediately-preceding pass, docs-only "clean sweep" entry, no code touched). `git fetch origin main` found that one sibling-session commit in flight when this pass started; re-fetched and fast-forward-merged it (`b2c1b23..968feaa`) before finishing, confirmed no overlap (it only appended to this doc), then pushed this pass's own work on top. PR #176/#177/#178/#179 (and #164/#165) re-checked via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls` at the start of this pass: unchanged, all still open/draft exactly as the prior entry recorded. Not touched, not merged.

**How this was found.** Took the standing directive's own suggestion literally: picked a plausible "other shape the `const { data` grep could miss" and grepped for it directly rather than reasoning about it. `grep -rn "Promise.all" --include="*.ts" app/app app/lib | grep -v "\.spec\.\|\.test\."` surfaced every call site; checking each by hand against `grep -n "const { data"` on the same file showed the array-destructure form (`const [{ data: x }, { data: y }] = await Promise.all([...])`) never matches - the literal 13-character substring `"const { data"` requires `const` immediately followed by `{ data`, and a `[`, a line break, or several unrelated tokens (another destructured member, `readiness`, `notifications`, etc.) sitting between them all defeat it. This is a cousin of the 3rd blind spot the immediately-preceding-but-one pass found (bare writes with no destructuring) - same root cause (the grep's literal-substring method, not any particular exclusion rule, was too narrow), one more shape of it.

**Full list of the 24 fixed instances, by file:**
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/compliance-data.ts` (3 Promise.all groups, 15 reads total: the top 9-way `company/pack/requirementRows/financial/briefing/roleRows/tagRows/officeRows/letterRows` read, plus the conditional `prov/asg` and `ppl/prj/cvs/gen` reads) - **the one real gate-adjacent finding, traced carefully, concluded safe.** `loadTenderCompliance()` feeds `packReadiness()`, which `requestSubmissionPack()` (`actions.ts:139-142`) uses as a genuine server-side hard stop (`if (readiness.unfilledPositions.length > 0) fail(...)`) - and `request_submission_pack_checked()` (migration 0115) does NOT independently re-verify unfilled positions, it only checks the billing quota and inserts the job row with the client-supplied `readiness_snapshot` verbatim. So a failed `requirementRows` read COULD, in principle, make a required-but-unconfirmed position vanish from `positionRows` (if it also has no `tender_pack_assignments` row yet, e.g. on a first-ever pack request) and let `unfilledPositions` wrongly come back empty - the TS gate passing when it shouldn't. Read `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py` directly (~line 505) to check whether this is actually exploitable: it is NOT - the engine re-derives `required` straight from the uploaded Technical workbook's own SETUP sheet (`read_required_positions(Workbook(technical))`) and `unassigned` from a fresh `tender_pack_assignments` read, completely independent of the TS-side `readiness_snapshot`, and raises `ValueError` (job marked `'failed'` with a visible `error_message`, confirmed at `process_pack_jobs.py:751`) if any required position is still unconfirmed. Same defense-in-depth shape already documented for `confirmPositionPerson()`'s own writes in the immediately-preceding-but-two pass. A TS-side bypass here just means the job gets queued and then fails loudly at the engine instead of being caught a step earlier - self-correcting on retry, not a real disqualification-risk bypass. Logged (9 + 2 + 4 `console.error` lines), not gated. Also checked `b7-data.ts`'s own `loadB7State()` (feeds the identical kind of hard stop, `b7.blocker` at `actions.ts:154`) for the same reason - same conclusion, same engine-level `sanral_b7.applicability()` re-derivation from the real workbook, logged there too.
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/actions.ts` (`syncWonProjectToTeam()`, lines ~561-610) - **the one other real finding fixed with a behavior change.** The `[{ data: assignmentRows }, { data: tenderRow }, { data: reqRows }]` read had no error captured at all. `assignmentRows` is what `confirmed` (the list of positions to sync into each person's `projects` row, feeding their next generated CV) is filtered from - a failed read silently made `confirmed = []`, skipped the whole upsert block, and the action still redirected to `#won-project` with no `error=` param, reporting success while nothing was actually synced. Fixed with the same `fail()` pattern this exact function already uses for every other read in it (`packErr`/`updErr`/`staleErr`/`syncErr`) - `asgErr` now fails loudly; `tenderErr`/`reqErr` (display text only) and a separate `existingSynced` read (stale-row cleanup only, safe direction) are logged, not gated.
- `app/lib/documentExpiry.ts` (`loadDocumentExpiryOverview()`) - **real finding, fixed with a behavior change.** All 4 reads (`companyRow/heldRows/typeRows/peopleRows`) had no error captured. Every caller used `rows.length === 0` to mean "nothing tracked, 100% compliant" - `dashboard/page.tsx`'s own `vaultCompliancePct = vaultRows.length === 0 ? 100 : ...` and `DocumentExpiryOverview.tsx`'s own "Every tracked document is valid - nothing needs attention right now." message both took a FAILED read (which also empties `rows`) for that exact same genuine-empty case. This is the dangerous direction the sweep looks for, not a logging gap: the one widget whose whole job (Sarel's own ask, "2 documents need attention before your next bid") is catching real compliance gaps could show a false "100% compliant"/"all valid" on a transient Supabase failure. Fixed by changing the return shape to `{ rows, error }` (same precedent as `fetchSavingsCounterSummary()`'s own earlier-today fix) and updating both callers: `dashboard/page.tsx` now shows "Couldn't check right now" instead of a percentage, never defaults to 100% on error; `DocumentExpiryOverview.tsx` shows a destructive "Couldn't check document expiry right now - try refreshing." banner instead of either message. New tests in `documentExpiry.spec.ts` (4 new, 15 total).
- `app/lib/notifications.ts` (`getNotifications()`, the topbar bell + dashboard's "Documents expiring" stat card) - **real finding, fixed with a behavior change.** All 5 reads had no error captured, same false-all-clear shape as the document-expiry finding above - a failed read fell through to the same `?? **Angle chosen.** Continued the directive's own standing TS-side unprotected-read sweep: re-ran `grep -rn "const { data" --include="*.tsx" --include="*.ts" . | grep -v "actions.ts" | grep -v "\.spec\." | grep -v "\.test\." | grep -v "error"` from scratch inside `app/app` - **45 hits, same count as every prior pass**, confirming the grep itself still hasn't drifted. Before tracing individual hits, re-read the sweep's own stated exclusion rule literally: "excluding `actions.ts` Server Actions... a failed read there surfaces as the action's own error return, not a silent false page-render state." That rule is about files *named* `actions.ts` (the `grep -v "actions.ts"` is a literal substring match, case-sensitive) - it does NOT touch `officeActions.ts`, `preferencesActions.ts`, or any other differently-named Server Action file, and two of the 45 raw hits (`company/officeActions.ts:19`, `discovery/preferencesActions.ts:22`) are exactly that: `company_members` membership-guard reads inside Server Action files whose name just doesn't literally contain the six characters "actions.ts" in that exact case. Traced both rather than assuming the sweep's own rule obviously covers them.

**What tracing them actually showed, and why the exclusion's own stated reason doesn't hold for this specific helper shape.** Both `officeActions.ts`'s `requireCompanyId()` and `preferencesActions.ts`'s `requireCompanyId()` read the signed-in user's own `company_members` row with no `error` captured, then `if (!membership) redirect("/onboarding")`. A `redirect()` is a hard Next.js navigation (throws `NEXT_REDIRECT`, intercepted by the framework to produce a real HTTP redirect) - it is NOT "the action's own error return" the exclusion rule describes (an `{ok:false, error}` value the caller can distinguish from success). On a transient `company_members` read failure (network blip, not a genuine "no row" result - confirmed again, as this doc has confirmed many times before, that Supabase-js resolves `{data: null, error}` on a query failure rather than throwing), an already-linked company member saving an office location or toggling an opportunity preference would be silently bounced to `/onboarding`, the exact "misleading a correctly-linked person" consequence `9fddd8f` already fixed for `my-cv/page.tsx`/`onboarding/page.tsx`'s own page-level reads, and PR #177 is fixing for `proxy.ts`'s own middleware-level read - just never fixed here. **Checked whether the prior exclusion's literal "actions.ts" scoping was itself the oversight** by running the sweep's own separate standing convention, `grep -rn "company_members" app/app --include="*.tsx" --include="*.ts" | grep -v spec`, and reading every multi-line (chained `.from(...).select(...).eq(...)`) hit the single-line grep above couldn't catch on its own - this is how the other 21 instances (every genuine `actions.ts`-named file, plus `tenders/new/actions.ts`, `pipeline/actions.ts` x3, etc.) surfaced. All 23 are the exact same 3-line, copy-pasted `requireCompanyId()`/`requireMember()`/`requireCompanyAdmin()` body (one file's own comment literally says "each actions.ts file keeps its own copy rather than a shared lib, matching the rest of this codebase's convention") - confirmed by reading every one of the 23, not assumed from the shape matching once.

**One real exception found and deliberately left alone, confirmed safe by tracing its own consumer**: `tenders/[id]/vault-quick-fix-actions.ts`'s own narrower `requireCompanyId(companyId): Promise<string | null>` does NOT redirect on failure - it `return membership ? companyId : null`, and its one caller, `saveVaultQuickFields()`, turns a null into `{ok: false, error: "Not signed in to this company."}` - a real `{ok,error}` return value the calling drawer component shows inline, never a navigation away from the page. This is genuinely the safe-direction shape the exclusion rule describes (a transient blip here just makes one save attempt fail with a retry-able, if slightly mis-worded, error - it does not redirect the whole page or imply the company doesn't exist). Traced this one all the way through before ruling it out, not assumed from the function's name alone - left unchanged.

**Fixed, all 23 files, one uniform, minimal change each**: `company/bank-accounts/actions.ts`, `company/document-scan/actions.ts`, `company/officeActions.ts`, `company/principals/actions.ts`, `company/properties/actions.ts`, `company/registrations/actions.ts`, `company/team/actions.ts`, `discovery/preferencesActions.ts`, `experience/actions.ts`, `my-cv/actions.ts`, `people/actions.ts`, `pipeline/actions.ts` (3 separate inline copies, not a shared helper: `moveTenderStage`, `saveTenderEconomics`, `recordOutcomeAndMoveStage`), `tenders/[id]/actions.ts`, `tenders/[id]/b7-actions.ts`, `tenders/[id]/comment-actions.ts`, `tenders/[id]/general-actions.ts`, `tenders/[id]/general-pack-review-actions.ts`, `tenders/[id]/logistics-actions.ts`, `tenders/[id]/narrative-actions.ts`, `tenders/[id]/pack-inputs-actions.ts`, `tenders/[id]/pack-review-actions.ts`, `tenders/[id]/reuse-actions.ts`, `tenders/new/actions.ts`. Each guard now captures `error: membershipError` on the same `company_members` read and adds `if (membershipError) throw new Error("Couldn't verify your company - try again.")` immediately before the pre-existing `if (!membership) redirect("/onboarding")` line - nothing else in any of the 23 files was touched (confirmed by `git diff`: every file's diff is exactly 3 lines added, 1 modified, rest byte-identical). A thrown error inside a Next.js Server Action (whether invoked via a plain `<form action>` or a client component's `useTransition`, both styles are used across these 23 callers - confirmed by reading `discovery/OpportunityPreferencesPanel.tsx`'s own `startTransition(async () => { const result = await setOpportunityPreferences(...) ... })`, which has no surrounding try/catch of its own) is caught by this app's own root `app/app/error.tsx` ("Something went wrong - Try again", added 2026-10-20 per its own header comment specifically for this kind of unhandled-error case) rather than silently redirecting to `/onboarding` and implying the company needs re-onboarding. The happy path (`membershipError` null, the only reachable value on any currently-passing test or live request) is unchanged byte-for-byte in every file.

**Verification, run myself, real exit codes, on the complete working tree**: `npm run typecheck` (`next typegen && tsc --noEmit`) - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings unchanged (`Logo.tsx` x2 `no-img-element`, `analytics/page.tsx` 1 unused `STAGE_META`). `npx vitest run` - **434/434 passed, 54/54 files** (none of the 23 touched files has a `.spec.ts`). The corrected per-file `*.test.ts` loop (no `--test` flag, looping `node --experimental-strip-types`, summing each file's own TAP `# tests`/`# fail` lines) - **27 files, 301 tests, 0 failures**, standing baseline unchanged (none of the 23 touched files has a `.test.ts` either). `npx next build` - **compiled successfully**, same route table, `/tenders/[id]` still `◐` Partial Prerender, `Proxy (Middleware)` line present.

**No red-then-green manual revert-and-confirm for this one, flagged plainly rather than skipped past silently** - every one of the 23 touched files is a `"use server"` Server Action file importing `next/navigation`/`next/cache` at module scope and calling the real Supabase server client (`next/headers` cookies), the identical "unsafe to import directly into a `.test.ts`/`.spec.ts` file" situation this doc's own history already documents for this exact file category (PR #178's own entry, this doc's prompt-9-part-0/1 entries). Correctness here rests on: (a) `npm run typecheck` passing, which confirms `membershipError`'s type (`PostgrestError | null`, from the Supabase client's own generated types) and every call site's shape are consistent; (b) the change being a single, mechanical, syntactically-verified-by-script insertion applied identically to all 23 files (confirmed via `git diff` that every file's diff is the same 3-line shape, not hand-edited per file with room for a typo to diverge); (c) the underlying behavioral claim (Supabase-js resolves `{data, error}` rather than throwing on a query-level failure, and Next.js routes a thrown Server Action error to the nearest `error.tsx`) being the same two facts this doc has already independently confirmed and relied on repeatedly across many prior passes, not a new claim introduced here - not asserted as equivalent to an actual red/green cycle.

**Pivoted to the TS-side sweep, re-grepped `const { data` with no nearby `error` capture from scratch** (same command as prior passes: `app/app/**/*.tsx`/`*.ts`, excluding `actions.ts`/`.spec.`/`.test.` files) - same 45 hits as the immediately-preceding pass's own count, confirming the grep itself hasn't drifted. Traced `app/tenders/[id]/compliance-data.ts:41`'s unprotected `tenders` row read (`loadTenderCompliance`'s own entry point - `const { data: tender } = ...; if (!tender) return null;`) all the way through its 4 real call sites (`compliance-report.tsx`, `disqualification-guard.tsx`, `submission-pack.tsx`, `pack-review-data.ts`) rather than stopping at "returns null, looks safe."

**The real finding, bigger than the read-failure framing it started from.** `submission-pack.tsx`'s and `general-workspace.tsx`'s own "Generate/Fill pack" buttons both compute `fixCount = snapshot.mapped ? computeTenderReadiness(snapshot.sections).fix.length : 0` and disable the button when `fixCount > 0` - this is prompt 9 part 2's own "Submit button: disabled while any Fix item is open" feature (app/AGENTS.md). Followed the button's own form `action` into `requestSubmissionPack()` (`actions.ts`) and `requestJob()`'s `generate_pack` branch (`general-actions.ts`), and from there into `request_submission_pack_checked()`/`request_general_job_checked()` (migration 0115, read in full): **neither Server Action nor either Postgres RPC ever re-checks `computeTenderReadiness(...).fix` at all** - only `unfilledPositions`, missing blank templates, Form B7, the pack-review confirmation, billing quota, and "already queued". The Fix-item gate is a `disabled` HTML attribute and nothing else. An HTML `disabled` attribute is purely client-rendered; it does not stop a direct POST to the Server Action (devtools, a saved/replayed form, any client that doesn't re-render the button's state) - so a tender with a real, disqualifying Fix item open (a mandatory compliance document never confirmed, an unconfirmed key person, etc.) could still have its submission pack requested and built, with nothing on the server ever having checked. This is the same dominant bug class this review loop has mined all week (a safeguard that exists in exactly one place and silently isn't the real gate), just found in the newer Fix/Provide/Verify gating feature rather than an old unprotected read.

**A second, narrower instance of the classic shape, found while fixing the first.** Both buttons' own `snapshot.mapped ? ... : 0` fallback treats "not mapped" as "zero Fix items" - but since `submission-pack.tsx` only ever mounts for a tender page.tsx has already confirmed is SANRAL-family, and `general-workspace.tsx` only reaches this line after its own earlier, separate read already confirmed a requirements manifest exists, `!mapped` at this specific point in either file can only mean *this* request's own fresh read of `loadTenderCompliance`/`loadGeneralPackReviewSnapshot` failed transiently - never a genuine "not applicable" case. On a transient blip, after a tender had already been reviewed once (`reviewed=true` persists from an earlier visit), the old code would silently re-enable the button with the Fix check never having actually run that render - "a failed read looks falsely ready," reached through the new Fix-gate instead of an old field.

**Fixed, 4 files** (not yet pushed to `main` - see below): `actions.ts`'s `requestSubmissionPack()` and `general-actions.ts`'s `requestJob()` (`generate_pack` branch) both now re-read the same cached Pack Review snapshot and fail closed (`fail()`/`redirect()` with the same "Fix N items first" wording the button already shows) when `fixCount > 0`, and fail closed with a "couldn't check readiness" message when `!mapped` too (never silently proceeding on an unreadable snapshot). `submission-pack.tsx` and `general-workspace.tsx` themselves: `!mapped` now produces its own distinct "Couldn't check compliance readiness - refresh and try again" disabled reason instead of being folded into "0 fix items". `general-workspace.tsx`'s own `badges.generalFixCount` (a separate, purely cosmetic tab-badge count, same already-accepted tier as every other count this review loop has left alone) deliberately keeps the old 0-on-unmapped number - only the button's own gate needed the stricter tri-state. Every previously-passing path (`mapped=true`) is unchanged byte-for-byte in all 4 files; the new branches are reachable only when `mapped` is false, which is unreachable on the happy path for either component by construction.

**Verification, run myself, real exit codes**: `npm run typecheck` (`next typegen && tsc --noEmit`) - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings unchanged (`Logo.tsx` x2 `no-img-element`, `analytics/page.tsx` 1 unused `STAGE_META`). `npx vitest run` - **434/434 passed, 54/54 files**. The corrected per-file `*.test.ts` loop (no `--test` flag, looping `node --experimental-strip-types`) - **27 files, 301 tests, 0 failures**, standing baseline unchanged. `npx next build` - **compiled successfully**, same route table, `/tenders/[id]` still `◐` Partial Prerender, `Proxy (Middleware)` line present.

**No new automated test, and no red-then-green manual revert-and-confirm for this one** - flagging plainly rather than quietly skipping past it: both Server Action changes are thin compositions of already-tested logic (`computeTenderReadiness` has its own 5-case `tender-readiness.test.ts`; `loadPackReviewSnapshot`/`loadGeneralPackReviewSnapshot` are the exact same cached snapshots the already-shipped button gate reads) inside files that import `next/navigation` and the Supabase server client at module scope - the identical "unsafe to import directly into a `.test.ts` file" situation this doc's own history already documents for this exact file category (`general-workspace.tsx`, `pack-review-data.ts`, prompt 9 part 0's own entry above). Correctness here rests on the composed, already-tested functions plus the full QA suite above, same standard that entry set - not asserted as equivalent to an actual red/green cycle.

**Why opened as PR #178, not pushed directly to `main`.** This is a genuine behavior change to the real hard-stop gate on the core submission-pack generation pipeline, for both tender families at once - unlike this review loop's usual "additive, narrowly-gated, unreachable on any currently-passing path" dashboard/report fixes, a company currently relying (even unknowingly, e.g. if their own browser's JS failed to apply the disabled state, or if they genuinely have an open Fix item right now) on the previously-missing server-side check would be newly, correctly blocked by this fix where they weren't before. That is exactly the intended effect, but it is a different risk tier from this loop's usual direct-push fixes and touches money-path logic (`requestSubmissionPack`/`requestJob`) this session cannot exercise against a live Supabase project - it should get a look before merging, per the standing guardrail ("for anything larger, open a PR and stop there"). Not merged by this session. PR: https://github.com/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pull/178 (branch `fix/submission-pack-fix-gate-server-side`, commit `465507e` on top of `12de22a`).

## Prior pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): continued the "built, tested, wired into ONE consumer but not a structurally identical sibling" angle into `engine/pack/` - found and fixed a genuinely significant instance: SANRAL submission packs, this product's original flagship pack engine, never fired the "Bid Pack Compilation Complete" email at all, while the general-family pack engine has sent it on every ready pack since 2026-10-27

Oriented from `bc60b7c` (immediately-preceding pass). `git fetch origin main` found zero sibling-session commits before this pass started, and the same emptiness held immediately before this pass's own push (`git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` / `HEAD..origin/main` both checked right before `git push`) - pushed as a clean fast-forward (`bc60b7c..b50069f`).

So `ecsa_expiry`/`sacpcmp_expiry`'s absence here is NOT a bug - the SANRAL Excel pack genuinely has nowhere to put it - and (separately, not fixed or touched this pass, just noted) the existing `sacnasp`/`sagc` plumbing in this same adapter appears to be dead data by the same test: present in the adapter dict and tested, but with no confirmed consumer anywhere in the actual pack output I could find. **The real finding.** `process_general_jobs.py` (engine=`'general'`) and `process_pack_jobs.py` (engine=`'sanral'`) both poll the exact same `pack_generation_jobs` table (confirmed: `general/process_general_jobs.py:89` `JOBS_TABLE = "pack_generation_jobs"`, `pack/process_pack_jobs.py` passes the literal table name the same way), both mark a completed job `'ready'` the same way - but only `process_general_jobs.py` ever called `send_pack_ready_email()` (`engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py`, notification-engine item B12, built 2026-10-27 and confirmed live-tested that same window against a real DBSA pack for Reviewer Civils & Consulting - see this doc's own 2026-10-28 entry). The consequence: every company that has ever generated a SANRAL submission pack - this product's original, flagship pack-generation path, not a secondary feature - has had NO "your pack is ready" email at all since B12 shipped, while a general-family pack customer has gotten one on every ready pack for the same 10 days.

**Angle chosen for the rest of the pass.** The directive's own suggestions: `engine/**/*.py` unchecked-write-then-irreversible-consequence shapes, or a different frequently-read table across pages (`people`, `tender_packs`, etc., not `company_members`/`companies`). Checked mention-count-in-this-doc as a rough proxy for "already mined" across `engine/**/*.py` (every job-processor/notify/discovery file sits at 20-140+ mentions; `run_discovery.py`/`download_documents.py` are low but already flagged elsewhere in this doc as "operator/QA tools run by hand, not wired" - read both anyway; found a real but low-severity design gap - `run_discovery.py` unconditionally `save_state()`s a tender's new detail metadata regardless of whether `--attempt-automated-download` actually succeeded, so a failed automated download is indistinguishable from a successful manual one on the next run's diff - but this path is documented elsewhere in this same file as reliably rejected by SANRAL's reCAPTCHA and kept only as an opt-in, and the whole script is a by-hand operator tool Sarel watches directly, not a scheduled job - judged not worth a fix this pass, noted here instead of silently dropped). **Read all 9 named files.** 7 of the 9 are already correct or genuinely low-severity, confirmed by reading (not assumed): `cover-page-preview.tsx` and `reuse-past-submission.tsx`'s own `people`/`tenders`/`tender_packs` reads are cosmetic (a display-name fallback, or hiding an optional "start from a previous submission" widget) - same tier this doc already accepts elsewhere. `pipeline/page.tsx` and `pipeline/pricing/page.tsx` (both newer pages) already wrap their whole render in try/catch with a real `ErrorState` fallback AND already surface their main `tenders`/`tender_packs` read's own `error` as a visible banner (`{(error || actionError/sp.error) && ...}`) - checked the actual banner-gating code, not just that an `error` variable exists. `market-comparison.tsx` already surfaces `loadOutcomesForTenders()`'s own error; its unprotected `companies` read only degrades name-matching accuracy, the same already-accepted tier. `company/registrations/page.tsx` already captures and bannerss its two main reads; its unprotected `people`/`company_principals` reads only narrow a dropdown's own options list.

**The real finding, in the 2 large remaining files (`general-workspace.tsx`, `general-pack-review-data.ts` - both part of the general/non-SANRAL tender-workspace family).** Both files' own "Company experience evidence" check is gated `if (evidenceRules.length > 0 && company?.id)`, where `company` comes from a `companies` read earlier in each file with no error captured at all (destructured as bare `{ data: companyRow }`). Supabase client calls never throw on a query-level error - a failed read returns `{data: null, error: {...}}`, it does not raise - so a transient `companies` read failure makes `company?.id` falsy via the exact same code path as "this tender genuinely needs no experience evidence," with nothing to tell them apart. Traced the real consequence in each file rather than assuming it from the shape alone:
- **`general-pack-review-data.ts`**: this section is one of several whose items feed `tender-readiness.ts`'s `computeTenderReadiness()`, which in turn is `general-workspace.tsx`'s own `generalFixCount` - the ONLY thing gating `disabled={!!generalDisabledReason}` on the "Generate a new pack"/"Generate submission pack" button (checked the actual JSX call site, not inferred). `computeTenderReadiness()`'s own doc comment already states the intended safeguard explicitly: "A section whose own data failed to load (`section.error`) contributes nothing... silently treating a read failure as '0 items, fully ready' would be worse than leaving it out of the count" - but that safeguard only works for a section that sets `section.error` via its own `catch` block, and this section's `catch` is never reached here because nothing actually throws. The result is exactly the thing the comment says is worse than omitting the section: on a `companies` (or the separate `experience_matches` RPC, same no-throw shape) read failure, this section silently pushes ZERO items - not a `missing`/Fix item, not `section.error` - so a tender that genuinely still needs its qualifying-experience evidence confirmed could have that one remaining gap vanish from the count on a blip, letting `generalFixCount` read 0 and wrongly enable pack generation. Compared directly against the SANRAL sibling (`compliance-data.ts`'s B6 check in `tenderCompliance.ts`) to confirm this is a real divergence, not an intentional design: the SANRAL side already has an explicit `else if (!input.experienceAvailable)` branch that pushes an honest "The Experience Library couldn't be read for this check..." item with status `check` - the general-family side never got the equivalent branch.
- **`general-workspace.tsx`**: the same `company?.id`-gated `experience` read feeds only a display block ("Company experience this tender accepts") - confirmed this one does NOT feed `peopleGaps` (`peopleGaps = regGaps + roleGaps`, computed from a separate, correctly-fail-safe pair of counts), so this instance is display-only, not a gating bug. Its own sibling `experience?.error` branch already shows a warning for the OTHER failure mode (`findMatchingExperience()`'s own RPC error) - but `company?.id` being falsy makes `experience` itself `null`, which that existing branch can't catch, so the read failure silently renders as if the tender simply had no evidence requirement at all (no warning, no chip, same look as "nothing to show").

**The finding, read end to end before touching anything.** Inside the page's `if (tenderPack)` block (reached once a tender has a pack - i.e. every tender actually being worked, not just browsed), 5 reads were destructured as just `{ data }` with no error captured: a `Promise.all()` of `tender_requirements`/`person_role_eligibility`/`tender_roles`, plus separate `tender_pack_assignments` and `generated_cvs` reads. A 6th, the page's own `people` roster read (`assignablePeopleRows`, used for the task-assignee and key-position-confirmation dropdowns), also lacked error capture. Two concrete, reachable consequences, re-confirmed by reading every downstream consumer rather than assumed from the pattern:
1. **Cosmetic-but-familiar instance**: `positions.length === 0` already rendered "No positions listed yet..." (the exact established false-empty-state claim) on a silent `tender_requirements`/`tender_pack_assignments` failure; `assignablePeople.length === 0 && positions.length > 0` rendered "No one is captured on the People page yet..." on a silent `people` failure - both in the "Key positions" section, both indistinguishable from the genuine case.
2. **New, higher-severity instance, specific to this page**: `openPositionsCount` (computed from `requirementRows`/`assignments`, both from the unprotected reads) feeds directly into `PrimaryPackActionLink`'s `ready` prop at line ~780 (`ready={!!tenderPack && (!tenderReadiness || tenderReadiness.thingsLeft === 0) && openPositionsCount === 0}`), which gates whether the "Generate submission pack" primary action is enabled. Traced the failure mode concretely: if `tender_requirements` fails (returns `null` -> `requirementRows = []`) while `tender_pack_assignments` either also fails or genuinely has no rows yet for a position that was never confirmed, the computed `positions` set can lose a real, still-open position entirely - `openPositionsCount` reads `0` on a tender that still has an unconfirmed key person, and the pack-generation action is wrongly enabled. This is not a display-only mis-render; it is a readiness/submission-gating value computed from an unprotected read, on the one page in the app whose job is deciding whether a bid is actually ready to go out.

**Fixed**: all 6 reads now capture their own `error`, each logged via `console.error` with a distinct, page-specific message (matching this file's and this doc's existing convention). The 5 position/CV-related reads combine into one `keyPositionsError` boolean; the `people` roster read gets its own `peopleLoadError` (kept separate since it also affects the already-existing "no one captured" message independently of positions failing). `keyPositionsError` now also gates `ready` directly (`ready={!!tenderPack && !keyPositionsError && ...}`, never just the derived count) and is checked first in `disabledReason` ("Couldn't load this tender's key positions - try refreshing before the pack can be generated."), so a failed read can never silently enable pack generation, only ever block it (the always-safe direction). The "Key positions" section's render gate was widened from `positions.length > 0 || isSanralPackFamily` to also include `|| keyPositionsError`, so the new error banner is reachable even for a general-family tender whose positions list would otherwise be empty and the whole section would previously have disappeared rather than shown anything. Both existing false-empty-state messages ("No positions listed yet", "No one is captured on the People page yet") are now gated on `!keyPositionsError`/`!peopleLoadError` respectively, with a new destructive-tone inline banner (same `bg-destructive/10 text-destructive` treatment this file already uses for `ErrorBanner`, inlined here since this is inside a section body, not the page-level banner slot) shown instead whenever the real cause is a failed read. The non-error path is unchanged byte-for-byte - `keyPositionsError`/`peopleLoadError` are both `false` whenever every read succeeds, which is the entire pre-existing passing-case behaviour for `positions`/`assignments`/`generatedCvs`/`openPositionsCount`/`ready`/`disabledReason`.

The membership read is the most consequential: on a transient failure, `membership` is `null`, so `isAdmin` becomes `false` and `companyId` becomes `undefined` - every one of the 4 parallel reads then short-circuits to its own `Promise.resolve({ data: [] })` branch (not because they failed, but because `companyId`/`isAdmin` are falsy), and the whole page renders "No members yet.", hides "Pending invites" and "Invite someone" entirely, and shows the real owner/admin as neither an admin nor able to manage their own team - indistinguishable from a brand-new, member-only account. Even when the membership read succeeds, any one of the 4 parallel reads failing independently shows the same "No members yet."/"No pending invites." false-empty text. Exactly the established bug class, here with an unusually wide blast radius (one failed read on a team-management page hides the entire admin UI, not just a display count).

**Fixed**: all 5 reads now capture their own `error`, each logged via `console.error` with a distinct, page-specific message (matching this file's and this doc's existing convention). One combined `loadError` boolean (true if any of the 5 failed) gates a single new destructive-tone `Banner` ("Couldn't load your team - try refreshing. If it keeps happening, let us know.") rendered above the existing `Current team` card, additively - imported `Banner` from `../_components/shared` (already used internally by `SubPage`'s own save-error banner, just not previously re-exported for a page to use directly). The non-error path is unchanged byte-for-byte: `Promise.resolve({ data: [], error: null })` replaces the old `Promise.resolve({ data: [] })` placeholders (same shape the real Supabase client returns on its own skipped-branch equivalent), so every currently-passing code path computes the exact same `members`/`invites`/`people`/`labelByUser` values as before.

**Finding 2 - `app/people/[id]/page.tsx`**: read end to end (989 lines). Its primary `people` read for the person itself already correctly captures `{ data, error }` and renders a distinct "Couldn't load this person" vs. "Person not found" not-found screen (already correct, not touched - confirmed by reading, not assumed). But 5 secondary reads inside the same `if (!isNew)` block - `projects`, `cv_uploads`, `cv_extraction_results` (pending CV extractions), `generated_cvs`, `signatory_scopes` - were all destructured as just `{ data }`, no error captured on any. A failed read on any of them is indistinguishable from the genuine empty case: `projects.length === 0` renders the explicit sentence "No project history on file yet for {name}" (a real false-empty-state claim on a Supabase failure, the exact established bug shape), and `cvUploads`/`generatedCvs`/`pendingExtractions`/`signatoryScopes` all silently render nothing at all (no section, no message) rather than their real, non-empty content - on a page whose whole job is assembling a person's CV/registration record for bid submission.

**Fixed**: all 5 reads now capture their own `error`, each logged via `console.error` with a distinct, page-specific message. One combined `secondaryLoadError` boolean (true if any of the 5 failed) gates a single new destructive-tone banner ("Some of this person's details (projects, CVs or registrations) couldn't be loaded - the sections below may be incomplete. Try refreshing."), placed directly after the existing `errorParam` banner slot and before the `cvApplied` success banner - the same additive-banner-above-content pattern `app/company/page.tsx`'s own secondary-reads fix (`6a6fc5b`) just used, reused here rather than inventing a new shape. `secondaryLoadError` defaults `false` (declared alongside the other per-page `let` state) and is only ever set inside the `!isNew` branch, so the `isNew` ("Add person") render path - which does none of these reads - is untouched. The non-error path is unchanged: every one of the 5 arrays is set to exactly the same value as before whenever its read succeeds.

**Verification - why this stops short of a red-then-green test, consistent with this doc's own established standard for this case**: both fixes are page-level Server Component changes (no `lib/*.ts` pure-function logic touched), and this codebase's test convention (`*.test.ts`/`*.spec.ts`) has no page-rendering harness - the same situation `615a124`'s briefing-attendance fix and `bc1e7b5`'s bulk-cv fix both documented, verified the same way here: (1) read every new branch carefully against the unchanged surrounding code to confirm each is reachable only when its own error flag is truthy and changes nothing else; (2) the full QA gate below.

The genuine "no company row yet, no error" case still returns `{ summary: null, error: false }` unchanged. `SavingsCounterCard` (`components/tt/savings-counter-card.tsx`) gained a new `error` prop, checked FIRST, ahead of the existing empty-state check - on `error`, it now renders the already-imported-elsewhere `ErrorState` component ("Couldn't load your savings") instead of the encouraging "Finish your first bid" `EmptyState`, same pattern `615a124`'s own briefing-attendance fix just used. Both call sites (`app/dashboard/page.tsx`, `app/analytics/page.tsx` - confirmed via grep these are the ONLY two callers of either `fetchSavingsCounterSummary()` or `SavingsCounterCard`) updated to destructure `{ summary, error }` and pass both through. The non-error path is unchanged on both pages and in the card - `error` is `false`/absent on every currently-passing code path, so the new branch is unreachable whenever both reads succeed, which is the entire rest of this function and component's existing behaviour.

## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): `pricePoints()`'s PPR 2022 price-points formula had no floor at 0, so the public `/tools/bee-preference-points` lead-magnet calculator rendered negative "preference points" for any realistic high-price input

Oriented from `9582a87` (own immediately-preceding pass, independently re-verified by the orchestrating session before this pass started per its own instruction - not re-verified again here). `git fetch origin main` found zero sibling-session commits - `HEAD` was already `origin/main`. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, unchanged - `#164`/`#165` (draft, stale since 2026-10-26, untouched) and `#176` (open, not draft, not merged, still awaiting Sarel's own go-ahead - not reviewed, not commented on, not touched this pass).

**Angle chosen, and what came up dry first.** The directive's own first-choice angle - other `.github/workflows/*.yml` multi-step Python pipelines with the same "claim/write in an earlier step, gated on a later step's unconfirmed outcome" shape `9582a87` just fixed in `daily-digest.yml` - was checked across every workflow in `.github/workflows/` and came back exhausted, not just assumed clean: `daily-discovery.yml` is the only other workflow that splits a Python "build" step (`watch_new_tenders.py`, writes `discovered_opportunities`/`discovery_seen_releases`) from a later, separate send step (`send-discovered-tenders.ts`, Node) - but read end to end, that send script's own `claim_notification` RPC call happens entirely WITHIN itself, in the same step, never in the earlier Python step. If the Node step never runs at all (an `npm ci` failure, a crash before `claim_notification` is ever called), nothing is marked claimed, and the next day's run picks the same `discovered_opportunities` rows back up automatically (its own `sinceIso` bounds to "last 2 days", confirmed by reading `send-discovered-tenders.ts` directly) - correctly decoupled already, not the same bug. Every other notify workflow (`compliance-alerts`, `corrigendum-alerts`, `deadline-reminders`, `founder-digest`, `onboarding-nudges`, `operational-alerts`, `returnables-digest`, `scout-alerts`) runs its own claim-and-send in one single Node step, confirmed by grepping each workflow file for its `run:` lines - no second script, no cross-step gap possible. This vein is genuinely exhausted now, not just this pass's own guess - every multi-step pipeline in the repo was actually read, not inferred from the one instance already fixed.

Also spot-checked the API-route-vs-Server-Action auth-parity angle: `app/app/api/**/route.ts` is only 3 files total (`billing/checkout`, `billing/payfast/itn`, `unsubscribe`) - read all 3. `checkout` requires `supabase.auth.getUser()` and redirects to `/login` if absent, same as a Server Action would gate. `payfast/itn` and `unsubscribe` are deliberately session-less webhook/one-click endpoints (PayFast's own server, and RFC 8058 mail-client auto-POSTs respectively) with their own already-documented, already-reviewed bearer-token/signature-based checks in place of a session - not a gap, by design, already commented as such in the files themselves. Nothing to fix here; too small a surface for a dedicated finding.

**The finding, from the "ZAR rounding/financial-calculation" angle.** `app/lib/preferencePoints.ts`'s `pricePoints()` implements the PPR 2022 reg 4/reg 5 price-points formula, `Ps = system-max x (1 - (Pt - Pmin) / Pmin)`, and its own comment already shows awareness that the result needs capping on the HIGH side ("never above the system's max... capped rather than allowed to exceed the max point by a rounding fluke") - but the function only ever did `Math.min(raw, maxPricePoints)`, with no floor on the LOW side. The raw formula goes negative for any `tenderPriceZar` more than double `lowestAcceptablePriceZar` (e.g. Pmin = R1,000,000, Pt = R2,500,000 -> `80 * (1 - 1.5) = -40`) - a real, reachable input on the public `/tools/bee-preference-points` calculator: read `BeePreferencePointsClient.tsx` directly and confirmed there is no upper-bound validation on the "Your tendered price" field at all, and the result card renders `{result.data.pricePoints} / {result.data.maxPricePoints}` verbatim, so a user who simply typed a price more than 2x the lowest bidder's would see "-40 / 80" and a correspondingly negative `totalPoints / 100`. A negative "preference points" figure is not how the PPR 2022 scoring is ever practically applied or presented - SBD 6.1's own Preference Points Claim Form has no box for a negative score, and no SCM practice note or worked example (including this repo's own `docs/specs/Tender-Regulatory-Compliance-Review.md` §2.1, re-read before concluding this) treats an over-priced bid as anything other than 0 price points, not an increasingly negative one. This is a UI/UX correctness bug on a public lead-magnet tool, not a judgment call to leave open - fixed by clamping the same way the high side already is.

**Fixed**: `pricePoints()` now does `Math.min(Math.max(raw, 0), maxPricePoints)` - clamped to `[0, maxPricePoints]` instead of only capped above. `calculatePreferencePoints()`'s `totalPoints` (which sums `pricePoints` + `beeGoalsPoints`) is unaffected in shape, just never fed a negative `pricePoints` input any more. Comment rewritten to document both bounds and why the low side matters here specifically (a real, unvalidated input on this exact page).

**Verified red-then-green.** Added 2 new tests to `app/lib/preferencePoints.test.ts`: the exact `Pt = 2 x Pmin` zero boundary (0 both with and without the fix - confirms the fix doesn't change the boundary itself), and a `Pt > 2 x Pmin` case (`Pt = 2,500,000`, and a further `Pt = 10,000,000` to confirm it stays at 0, not increasingly negative) asserting `pricePoints` returns exactly `0`. **Red confirmed directly**: `git stash push -- app/lib/preferencePoints.ts` (reverting only the implementation, keeping the new tests) and reran - `12 tests, 11 pass, 1 fail`, the failing one showing exactly the predicted pre-fix value (`AssertionError: -40 !== 0` at the `Pt = 2,500,000` case). `git stash pop` restored the fix, reran: **12/12 passed** (the file's own test count went from 10 to 12; the 2 new ones are additions, not replacements - every pre-existing case, including the Pt=Pmin/10%-above/rounding/throws/BEE-table/full-breakdown cases, is untouched and still green).

**Full suite, run after restoring the fix (not before)**: `npx tsc --noEmit` from `app/` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings this doc's own baseline already documents (`_components/Logo.tsx` x2 `no-img-element`, `analytics/page.tsx` 1 unused var), confirmed unchanged. `npx vitest run` - **427/427 passed, 52/52 files**, unchanged (no `.spec.ts` file touched). `node --experimental-strip-types --test` over all 27 `*.test.ts` files in `app/` - **240/240 passed** (238 baseline + the 2 new `preferencePoints.test.ts` cases; every other file's own count unchanged). `npx next build` - **compiled successfully**, same route shapes as `9582a87`'s own baseline including `/tools/bee-preference-points` and `/toolkit/bee-preference-points` (run out of caution since this lib file feeds that page, even though no page/route file itself was touched). Also re-ran `lib/sanralScoring.test.ts` + `lib/tenderCompliance.test.ts` directly (adjacent scoring logic, neither touched) - **13/13 passed**, confirming no regression nearby. No Python file touched this pass - no `py_compile`/`pytest` run needed.

**Why committed directly to `main`, not a draft PR**: pure function change in one file plus its own test file, no schema/RLS/migration/workflow touched, strictly a correctness fix in one direction (clamping an already-known-to-need-clamping formula at the other end it was missing), and the kind of small/well-verified fix the standing guardrails call for committing directly rather than opening a PR.

**Context for whoever picks this up next.** Migrations `0117`-`0120` still on `main`, still not applied to production - untouched this pass. PR `#176` still open, awaiting Sarel's own go-ahead - not touched. The 4 standing judgment-call items (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-before-ITN gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, the zero-recipients batched-send sub-case) remain exactly as described - not touched, not resolved. The two veins flagged as exhausted (membership-revoked-mid-request, `AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md`) were correctly left alone this pass. The frontend empty-state/error-boundary systematic sweep flagged as still-open by 2 passes ago was **not touched this pass either** (a genuinely different angle was picked instead, per the directive's own menu of options) - still a real next-pass candidate. The multi-step-workflow angle this pass's directive highlighted is now genuinely exhausted (see above) - a future pass re-opening it needs a new workflow or script to have been added since this one, not a re-read of what's already here. Also worth a future pass's attention, not chased further here: `app/lib/dealEconomics.ts`'s `commissionRand()` (`Math.round(price * pct) / 100`) and `app/lib/billing.ts`'s PayFast amount formatting (`toFixed(2)` on integer Rand prices) were both read as part of this pass's ZAR-rounding angle and look correct (whole-Rand plan prices, cent-precise commission rounding) - not a finding, just confirming they were actually checked, not skipped.

Committed and pushed directly to `main`:
- `app/lib/preferencePoints.ts`
- `app/lib/preferencePoints.test.ts`
- `docs/specs/System-Status.md`

`git status --short` confirmed clean before and after (only the files listed above).

To verify independently: `node --experimental-strip-types --test app/lib/preferencePoints.test.ts` (12 tests, 0 failures); revert `app/lib/preferencePoints.ts` to `git show 9582a87:app/lib/preferencePoints.ts` and rerun to see the 2 new tests fail with the `-40 !== 0` assertion described above. Or just evaluate `80 * (1 - (2_500_000 - 1_000_000) / 1_000_000)` by hand against the pre-fix code's `Math.min(raw, maxPricePoints)` to see the uncapped negative result directly.
