## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): a fresh angle - the "claim the one-time digested-mark before confirming the send" bug class, already fixed for every OTHER notification type in this codebase (pack_ready, deadline reminders, operational alerts, returnables/compliance/discovered-tenders/scout-alert digests), had two unswept instances left in `engine/notify/daily_digest.py` - and they were the worst-case shape of this whole bug class, since "claim" and "send" here aren't two lines in one function but two DIFFERENT SCRIPTS in two DIFFERENT GitHub Actions steps. Fixed by moving the marking write to `send_digest_emails.py`, gated on a confirmed `sent` status; also corrected a now-demonstrably-false claim in the workflow's own header comment. 4 new tests, red-then-green confirmed. Committed and pushed directly to `main` - no PR (no schema/RLS/migration touched, same established fix pattern as every prior instance of this exact bug class, all of which were also committed directly).

Oriented from `4049d82` (own immediately-preceding pass, independently re-verified by the orchestrating session before this pass started per its own instruction - not re-verified again here). `git fetch origin main` found zero sibling-session commits, checked both before starting and again immediately before this commit - `HEAD` was already `origin/main` both times. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, unchanged - `#164`/`#165` (draft, stale since 2026-10-26) and `#176` (open, not draft, not merged, still awaiting Sarel's own go-ahead - not reviewed, not commented on, not touched this pass).

**Angle chosen**: the directive flagged both the "membership-revoked-mid-request" vein and the `AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md` cross-check as exhausted - explicitly not re-mined. Rather than the frontend empty-state/error-boundary angle (also offered, genuinely open, but a broader, shallower sweep), picked a line-by-line read of `engine/notify/daily_digest.py`/`send_digest_emails.py` end to end, looking specifically for the SAME "claimed a one-time token before the send was confirmed" shape the `fdeab92`/prior passes already found and fixed everywhere else in this codebase (the TS cron scripts, the pack-ready email) - checking whether that sweep, which the `fdeab92` pass's own entry explicitly scoped to `claim_notification`/`record_deadline_reminder_sent`/`record_operational_alert_sent` callers, had actually reached every real instance.

**The finding.** `daily_digest.py --mode live`'s `main()` called `discovery_downgrades.mark_digested()` and `watch_tender_updates.mark_digested()` - both real `PATCH` writes against `discovered_opportunities.downgrade_digested_at` and `tender_update_notifications.digested_at` - unconditionally, the moment a digest was merely BUILT (an item present in at least one person's assembled digest JSON), never gated on whether that digest was ever actually delivered. The real send is `send_digest_emails.py`, a SEPARATE script reading the `--out` JSON this one writes, run as its OWN later step in `.github/workflows/daily-digest.yml` with its OWN separate secrets (only `RESEND_API_KEY`/`DIGEST_FROM_ADDRESS` - confirmed by reading the workflow file, `send_digest_emails.py` has never had Supabase credentials in production at all). This is the identical bug class `fdeab92`'s pass fixed 4 instances of (and `send-returnables-digest.ts` before that) - but a WORSE-CASE shape of it: every other instance claimed its one-time token and attempted the send in the same function, so the gap was a few lines/milliseconds wide; here the "claim" (build step, writes to Supabase) and the real "send" (a wholly separate process, possibly minutes later, over its own network calls to Resend) are decoupled across a GitHub Actions step boundary. Concretely, before this fix, ANY of the following silently and permanently lost that day's re-assessed-tender-downgrade/tender-update content, with zero retry, ever: the "Send via Resend" step crashing, timing out, or being cancelled after the build step already succeeded; a Resend outage or bad/expired `RESEND_API_KEY` (which currently degrades gracefully, per that script's own design, by sending nothing and exiting 0 - a documented "safe" path that was nonetheless marking everything digested regardless); or even just ONE person's e-mail failing transiently (`send_one()`'s own `"failed"` status, which already exists and is exercised in this file's own tests) - that specific person's `tender_updates`/`reassessed_tenders` content for that day was marked delivered and never carried again, even though their inbox never received it. Confirmed by reading `daily_digest.py`'s `main()` (the two `mark_digested()` call sites, both gated only on "did this item appear in a built digest", never on send outcome) and `send_digest_emails.py` end to end (confirmed zero Supabase imports/env-var reads anywhere in it before this pass) and the workflow file (confirmed the "Send via Resend" step's `env:` block only ever had the two Resend secrets). Also caught, incidentally: the workflow's own header comment claimed "daily_digest.py's own --mode live is read-only against Supabase... this workflow cannot write or delete anything in the real database" - demonstrably false even before this pass's own finding (that step already writes `deadline_reminders_seen`/`digest_readiness_seen` seen-store rows every run via `watch_deadlines.save_seen_db()`/`save_readiness_seen_db()`), corrected alongside the real fix rather than left to mislead a future reader.

**Fixed**, moving the responsibility to where the actual send outcome is known rather than adding a check in place (the two scripts' separation means there's nowhere in `daily_digest.py` itself where "confirmed sent" could ever be known):
- `daily_digest.py`'s `build_digest_for_person()`: the `tender_updates` section now also tracks `_delivered_tender_updates` (a list of `{company_id, watched_document_id}`) regardless of role - including the `viewer` role's own summarized `{count, most_urgent}` rendering, which previously dropped the raw ids entirely. `reassessed_tenders`' existing `_delivered_downgrades` tracking (added for the OLD build-time marking) is kept, just no longer popped/consumed here.
- `daily_digest.py`'s `main()`: removed both `mark_digested()` calls (and the `delivered_downgrades` aggregation) outright. The `_delivered_*` keys now simply ride along, unconsumed, in the `--out` JSON - harmless extra fields `send_digest_emails.py`'s own `render_text()`/`has_content()` already ignore (both iterate a fixed, named `SECTION_LABELS` list, confirmed by reading both functions).
- `send_digest_emails.py`: new `mark_delivered_items(sent_digests)`, called from `main()` with exactly the digests whose `send_one()` call returned `"sent"` this run (never `"failed"`/`"skipped_*"`/`"dry_run"`) - collects the union of `_delivered_downgrades`/`_delivered_tender_updates` across only those, and calls the same two `mark_digested()` functions (now imported here instead) with a real `company_profiles.RestClient.from_env()`. If that client is `None` (Supabase credentials not present in this step - the exact gap this pass also closes in the workflow, see below), it logs and raises ONE `system_alerts` warning rather than crashing or guessing - the safe default on a missing-credential day is "carry it again tomorrow" (a harmless duplicate line in an already-opted-in person's digest), never the silent, permanent loss this whole fix exists to close. A per-table write failure (a real RPC/network error) is caught and alerted the same way, same "don't flood Sarel, don't crash the batch" convention this module's `send_one()` loop already uses.
- `.github/workflows/daily-digest.yml`: added `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` to the "Send via Resend" step's `env:` block (the same two secrets the build step already uses - no new secret needed, confirmed these are real, already-configured repository secrets per this doc's own 2026-10-25 entry) and rewrote the header comment that incorrectly claimed this workflow never writes to Supabase.

**Verified red-then-green, with 4 new tests** in `engine/notify/test_send_digest_emails.py` (`test_mark_delivered_items_marks_nothing_for_a_run_with_no_sent_digests`, `test_mark_delivered_items_only_marks_ids_from_confirmed_sent_digests`, `test_mark_delivered_items_degrades_safely_with_no_supabase_credentials`, `test_main_only_marks_the_digest_that_actually_sent_not_a_skipped_one` - the last is a full `main()`-level integration test with one digest that sends successfully and one with no e-mail on file, asserting only the SENT one's downgrade id gets marked). **Red confirmed directly, not assumed**: `git stash push -- engine/notify/send_digest_emails.py` (back to the exact pre-fix content) and reran the new test file - crashed immediately with `AttributeError: module 'send_digest_emails' has no attribute 'company_profiles'` on the very first new test, since the pre-fix module has no Supabase integration or `mark_delivered_items()` at all - the plainest possible demonstration that this safety net did not previously exist. `git stash pop` restored the fix, reran: **13/13 passed** (9 pre-existing + 4 new).

**Full suite, run after restoring the fix (not before)**: `npx tsc --noEmit` from `app/` - **0 errors** (this pass touched no TypeScript at all - run anyway, per the standing QA gate). `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings (`_components/Logo.tsx` x2 `no-img-element`, `analytics/page.tsx` 1 unused var) every prior pass's own baseline already documents, confirmed unchanged. `npx vitest run` - **427/427 passed, 52/52 files**, unchanged (no `.spec.ts` file touched). `node --experimental-strip-types --test` over all 27 `*.test.ts` files - **238/238 passed**, unchanged. `npx next build` - compiled successfully, same route shapes as `4049d82`'s own baseline (run out of caution, even though no page/route file was touched). `python3 -m py_compile` on all 3 touched/new Python files - clean. `python3 engine/notify/test_send_digest_emails.py` - **13/13 passed, 0 failures**. `python3 engine/notify/test_digest_live.py` (the `main()`-level live-mode integration test, confirms the build step no longer prints any "marked ... as digested" line and still builds all 4 roster digests correctly, including the `viewer`-role person) - **0 failures**. `python3 engine/notify/test_digest_opt_in.py`, `python3 engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py`, `python3 engine/discovery/test_discovery_downgrades.py`, `python3 engine/discovery/test_tender_updates.py` (all read or adjacent to the touched code, none of them modified) - all re-run directly, **all pass, 0 failures**, confirming no regression in anything this pass didn't touch. `git diff --stat`: `.github/workflows/daily-digest.yml` (+27/-4), `engine/notify/daily_digest.py` (+71/-26... net additions are mostly comment/rationale, the real logic change is small: 2 call sites removed, ~10 lines of tracking added), `engine/notify/send_digest_emails.py` (+71, new function + imports), `engine/notify/test_send_digest_emails.py` (+115, 4 new tests).

**Why committed directly to `main`, not a draft PR**: no schema/migration/RLS boundary touched; the fix is strictly safety-improving in one direction only (a missing-credential or any other failure mode now degrades to "carried again tomorrow", never a worse outcome than before); and it is the exact same fix pattern - and, per this doc's own history, the exact same "commit directly" precedent - every other instance of this specific bug class already received (`send-returnables-digest.ts`, `send-deadline-reminders.ts`, `send-operational-alerts.ts`, the pack-ready email's `RESEND_API_KEY`-ordering fix). The one real production-reaching change is additive-only to the workflow (two secret references added to an existing step, both already real, already-configured secrets - no new secret needed, nothing removed that was relied on).

**Not re-opening `send-compliance-digest.ts`/`send-discovered-tenders.ts`/`send-scout-alerts.ts`'s own "claim-many-before-a-batched-send" tradeoff** (standing judgment-call item #4) - that remains exactly as described by prior passes, untouched, not overridden. This pass's finding is a different file family (Python, not the TS cron scripts), a different, more clear-cut shape (no batching semantics to preserve - there is no reason at all for the mark to happen before the send is confirmed, once the send step has its own Supabase credentials), and was fixed outright rather than left as a judgment call.

**Context for whoever picks this up next**: migrations `0117`-`0120` still on `main`, still not applied to production - untouched this pass. PR `#176` still open, still awaiting Sarel's own go-ahead - not touched. The 4 standing judgment-call items (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-before-ITN gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, the zero-recipients batched-send sub-case) remain exactly as described - not touched, not resolved. The two veins flagged as exhausted (membership-revoked-mid-request, `AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md`) were correctly left alone this pass, per the directive. The frontend empty-state/error-boundary angle flagged as genuinely open by the immediately-preceding pass is **still open, not touched this pass either** - spot-checked a handful of admin pages (`admin/telemetry`, `admin/notifications`) for empty-state handling while orienting, found nothing worth a dedicated writeup (an empty `<tbody>` with just column headers, not a crash or a misleading display), but did not do the systematic sweep the prior pass described - a genuine next-pass candidate, not exhausted by this spot-check.

**One more thing worth a human decision, not resolved here**: whether the `daily-digest` workflow's "Build today's digests" step still needs `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` write-equivalent access documented more honestly in its own comment going forward - done this pass - but also whether `RESEND_API_KEY` is CURRENTLY a real, valid, working key in the live repository secrets (this doc's own 2026-10-25 entry says Sarel set real env vars including it "mid-session", but this sandbox cannot read GitHub Actions secret values or confirm a real scheduled run's own logs) - if it has since expired, lapsed, or Resend's own sending domain verification has lapsed, today's live runs would already be silently losing `tender_updates`/`reassessed_tenders` content under the OLD code (now fixed going forward) with no way for this session to directly confirm either way. Flagging rather than guessing.

## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): the "membership-revoked-mid-request" meta-sweep's own "exhausted across the 8 named files" claim (`3aa470a`) held for the WRITE that each file's own fix targeted, but missed a second, later write inside one of those already-"fixed" functions - `app/app/company/registrations/actions.ts`'s own `saveHeldRegistration()`, fixed for its row-update write by `23b43b4`. Found and fixed the gap, verified red-then-green with 2 new tests, committed and pushed directly to `main`.

Oriented from `b764cf2` (own immediately-preceding pass, independently re-verified by the orchestrating session before this pass started - not re-verified again here, per instruction). `git fetch origin main` found zero sibling-session commits, both before starting and again immediately before this commit - `HEAD` was already `origin/main` both times. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, as expected - `#164`/`#165` (both draft, stale, untouched since 2026-10-26) and `#176` (open, NOT draft, NOT merged - left exactly as is, re-checked again after this pass's own push, still unchanged).

**The quick spot-check the directive asked for, done first**: re-grepped every `app/app/**/actions.ts` for `.update(`/`.delete(` not already chained with a `.select(...).maybeSingle()`/`.single()` gate. Most hits were either already-covered (just not matched by the crude single-line grep, because the `.select()` sits on a later line of the same chain) or genuinely low-severity (a plain UI-state `.update()` with no file/destructive consequence and no existing check at all, e.g. `tenders/[id]/actions.ts`'s `reassignTenderTask()`/`advanceTaskStatus()` - inline tap-to-update task fields, no error check, no destructive write, judged not worth fixing on the same proportionality basis prior passes have used for similar no-consequence cases). One hit stood out: `company/registrations/actions.ts` line 86, inside `saveHeldRegistration()` - a file this bug class's meta-sweep explicitly lists as already fully covered.

**The actual finding - read `saveHeldRegistration()` end to end again rather than trusting "this file is done" from the file-level list.** The function has TWO separate writes to `held_registrations`, not one: (1) the row's own field update (`.update(row).eq("id", id)`), fixed by `23b43b4` with `.select("id").maybeSingle()` plus a real "no longer there" error path; and (2), only reached when a certificate file is attached, a SECOND, later update that records the just-uploaded file's path (`.update({storage_path, original_filename}).eq("id", heldId)`) - still checking only `error`, exactly the pre-`23b43b4` shape, never touched by that fix or by any later meta-sweep pass (both of which evidently read only as far as the first write in this function before moving on). The two writes have two independent timing windows: fixing (1) does nothing to protect (2) - a membership-revoked-mid-request race (another admin's `removeMember()`, 0114) landing specifically between the row write succeeding and this second write still hits RLS's own `using (is_company_member(company_id))` (0050), re-evaluated against the then-current row, and PostgREST returns the same `error: null`/zero-rows-affected 2xx this whole bug class is built on. Pre-fix, the code: uploads the new certificate to storage (succeeds, since storage RLS is a separate, already-correct check), then this second update silently no-ops, then - checking only `error`, which is null - goes on to delete `existing.storage_path`, the OLD file, which the row STILL actually references since the attach write never took effect. Net result, worse than a plain orphan: the row ends up pointing at a file that no longer exists at all, while the real new file sits permanently unreferenced in storage - and the page reports "Registration saved".

**Fixed** with the same established pattern used throughout this bug class - chained `.select("id").maybeSingle()` onto the attach write, gated on the returned row (not just `error`); on a zero-row match, the newly-uploaded (now-orphaned) file is removed and the action fails with a clear error, and - critically - the OLD file is left alone (never reached, since the gate `fail()`s before that line).

**Verified with 2 new tests** in the existing `app/app/company/registrations/actions.spec.ts` (same sequential-response-queue mocking convention already established in this file): one for the race (real row-write match, then zero-row attach-write match) asserting the old file is NOT removed and the new orphaned file IS removed, one confirming the ordinary success path (both writes match) still attaches the new file and removes the old one as before. **Red-then-green confirmed directly, not assumed**: `git stash push` on the just-fixed `actions.ts` (back to its exact pre-fix, `b764cf2` content) and reran against the pre-fix code - **1 of 7 failed exactly as predicted**: the new race test (`expected '.../company/registrations?saved=1#r-...' not to contain 'saved=1'` - i.e. pre-fix it reports success for a write that silently no-opped), while all 6 others (including the new success-path test, which exercises the same two-write sequence but with both writes genuinely matching, so it passes identically whether or not the fix is present - it's a general correctness check for the ordinary case, not itself a regression test for this bug) stayed green throughout, confirming the race test is a genuine reproduction and not a tautology. `git stash pop` restored the real fix, reran: **7/7 passed** (5 pre-existing + 2 new).

**Full suite, run after restoring the fix (not before)**: `npx tsc --noEmit` from `app/` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings (`_components/Logo.tsx` x2 `no-img-element`, `analytics/page.tsx` 1 unused var) every prior pass's own baseline already documents, confirmed unchanged. `npx vitest run` - **422/422 passed, 52/52 files** (420 baseline + this pass's 2 new tests, no regression anywhere). `node --experimental-strip-types --test` over all 27 `*.test.ts` files (the separate suite) - **238/238 passed**, identical baseline, unaffected (none of the 27 touch `registrations/actions.ts`). `git diff --stat`: `app/app/company/registrations/actions.ts` (+25/-3), `app/app/company/registrations/actions.spec.ts` (+74).

**Other angles tried this pass, found genuinely clean or low-severity, not written up at length**: `company/actions.ts`, `company/document-scan/actions.ts`, `people/actions.ts`, `experience/actions.ts`, `onboarding/actions.ts`, `admin/actions.ts`, `admin/taxonomy/actions.ts`, `pipeline/actions.ts`, `company/team/actions.ts` were all re-grepped for the same shape; nothing else with a destructive-consequence write turned up unguarded - the remaining unguarded `.update()`/`.delete()` calls found were all either plain, no-file UI-state writes (task reassignment/status, admin moderation actions) with no destructive consequence, or already correctly gated and just missed by the crude single-line grep pattern.

**On the meta-sweep's own "exhausted" claim, again**: this pass doesn't reopen it for the 8 named files' PRIMARY writes - those are still correctly fixed. It does show the claim was (reasonably) read at the granularity of "one write per function," when at least one function in that list had two. A future pass treating a file as "done" for this bug class should specifically check whether any already-fixed function has a SECOND write after the one that got fixed (storage-attach writes, two-step "insert then backfill a generated field" patterns, etc.) before assuming nothing more is there - this specific vein (two-writes-in-one-already-fixed-function) has now produced exactly one real finding and may or may not have more; worth a fast targeted check (grep each of the 8 files for a second `.update(`/`.delete(` after the one already fixed) before a future pass invests more time in it, but not worth a dedicated open-ended re-read of all 8 again from scratch.

**The `deletePerson()` re-assessment is the significant correction here.** The prior pass's own words: "a microseconds-wide window between two consecutive awaited calls, no destructive consequence... the window is narrower by orders of magnitude than every instance actually fixed above." Reading the function end to end rather than taking that characterization on trust: it is backwards. `deletePerson()`'s real order was (1) confirm the person exists, (2) read every CV-upload/generated-CV/held-registration storage path this person owns (two parallel `select`s, two storage `list()` calls), (3) remove the CV/generated-CV files from the `cv-documents` bucket (checked by `error`), (4) remove the held-registration certificate files from the `company-documents` bucket (**not checked by anything at all** - the prior pass's own claim that "its own storage-file removals already correctly check their own error" was true for step 3 but not step 4, an oversight in that pass's own read), THEN (5) `supabase.from("people").delete().eq("id", id).eq("company_id", companyId)`, checked only by `error`. The real race window for step 5 is the ENTIRE span from step 1 to step 5 - every read, every listing, both storage removals - not "two consecutive awaited calls." And the consequence is not "none": if another admin's `removeMember()` (0114) revokes this user's own `company_members` row anywhere in that window, RLS's own `using (is_company_member(company_id))` (0001, re-evaluated against the OLD row) on the final delete silently matches zero rows - but by that point every one of this person's real CV files, generated CVs and registration certificates has ALREADY been permanently destroyed from storage, unconditionally, while the `people` row (and everything that would have cascaded with it) survives, now with every `storage_path` column on its cascading rows pointing at nothing. This is the same shape as every other instance this bug class has already fixed (destructive storage removal unconditional on a write that might not have matched), just with the write at the END of the function instead of in the middle of it - arguably the single widest window of any instance found in this entire bug class to date, not the narrowest.

**Fixed by reordering, not by adding a check in place**: the person row's own delete now runs FIRST (right after gathering every storage path - itself all read-only, so safe to do in any order), gated by `.select("id").maybeSingle()`, and ALL storage removal (both buckets) is deferred until that delete is confirmed to have actually matched a row. This fully closes the window rather than narrowing it - once the delete is confirmed, the two storage removals are now best-effort cleanup (logged on failure, not blocking the user-facing success) rather than a precondition for a user-facing "deleted" message, since the real, irreversible delete has by then genuinely happened.

1. *RESTRICTIVE policies with the same "revoke from public doesn't touch anon" blind spot.* That blind spot is specific to `revoke ... from function ... from public` on a GRANT; a RESTRICTIVE policy is a completely different mechanism (it narrows what a PERMISSIVE policy already allows, it doesn't grant anything itself), so there's no equivalent gap to find - confirmed by reading every RESTRICTIVE policy in the schema (`0032`, `0077`, `0117`, `0118`): every one is scoped `to authenticated`, same as every PERMISSIVE policy.
2. *Leftover table-level `anon` grants independent of RLS.* Queried `pg_policies` directly against the replayed schema: every single policy in the schema (exactly as `0120`'s own entry already found for functions) is scoped `to {authenticated}` - zero target `anon`/`public`. Queried `pg_class.relrowsecurity` for every one of the 67 real tables in `public`: **all 67 have RLS enabled**, none missing it (ruling out the much worse "no RLS at all, so the default-privilege table grant is the only thing governing the table" shape). Grepped every migration for a table-level `revoke ... from public` (as opposed to the function-level pattern 0120 fixed): found exactly 3 (`0022`, `0042`, `0043`), and all 3 already correctly name `anon` directly (`revoke ... from authenticated, anon`), not the bare `from public` shape that has the blind spot - so this angle, unlike the function one, was never actually broken. Also checked the schema's two views (`company_ownership_breakdown`, `tender_engine_jobs`) for the classic "a view silently runs as its owner, bypassing the querying role's RLS" PG<15 gotcha - both already carry `security_invoker=true` (confirmed via `pg_class.reloptions`), so this is clean too. ## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): continued `fdf51d7`'s own "other anon-granted SECURITY DEFINER functions" suggestion - found the explicit-grant angle already fully covered, but a different, broader mechanism behind it was not: ~46 functions' `revoke all ... from public` (the near-universal pattern across 0003-0115) never actually removed `anon`'s own execute privilege, because this project's roles are provisioned the real-Supabase way (a direct, named-role default-privilege grant to `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role`, separate from and untouched by revoking the generic `public` pseudo-role); fixed with a new migration revoking `anon` explicitly for all of them, verified red-then-green against a real scratch Postgres 16 instance for the privilege change AND a functional sample, confirmed zero regression for `authenticated` (grant-level and business-logic-level), pushed to `main` as a new migration awaiting Sarel's own application to production, same batch as `0117`-`0119`

**Context for whoever picks this up next, restated, unchanged**: migrations `0117`-`0119` were already on `main` but not yet applied to production; this pass adds a fourth, `0120`, to that same pending batch (SQL-only, also not yet applied). The 4 standing judgment-call items (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-before-ITN gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap in `app/proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, the zero-recipients batched-send sub-case) remain exactly as described in prior entries - not touched, not resolved. `start_payfast_checkout()` specifically is discussed below (it DID match this pass's own bug pattern) and was deliberately left out of the fix so this grant-table cleanup can't be read as touching that open judgment call.

Oriented from `fdf51d7` (own immediately-preceding pass, independently re-verified by the orchestrating session before this pass started - not re-verified again here, per instruction). `git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only` confirmed clean both before starting and again immediately before this commit - `HEAD` was still a direct ancestor of `origin/main` with zero divergence, no sibling-session work landed mid-pass. Open PRs re-checked via `gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`: exactly three - `#164`/`#165` (draft, stale, untouched) and `#176` (open, not draft, not merged, left exactly as is).

**Angle chosen**: the orchestrator's own directive explicitly named this as "a promising, not-yet-fully-swept variant" of `fdf51d7`'s angle - other `SECURITY DEFINER` functions that are `anon`-granted without a genuine `anon` caller. Grepping migrations for literal `grant execute ... to anon` found only the 11 lines already known and accounted for in `fdf51d7`'s own entry (`apply_payfast_itn`, `signups_enabled`, `claim_notification`, `record_notification_sent`, `lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for`, `unsubscribe_lifecycle_email`, `record_deadline_reminder_sent` x2, `invite_preview` - the 4 already fixed by `0119` plus the 4 already-confirmed-genuine callers, `lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for` already `service_role`-only since `0108`) - that literal angle really is exhausted, exactly as the directive guessed it might be.

Rather than stop there, re-read the question as "which functions actually END UP anon-executable in the live schema, by ANY mechanism" rather than "which migrations say the word `anon`" - because a SECURITY DEFINER function's privileges aren't fully described by what a migration's own `grant`/`revoke` lines say; Postgres's own default behaviour matters too. Built a real scratch Postgres 16 instance (reusing this session's own `engine/security/scratch_supabase_stub.sql`, a prior pass's own tenant-isolation-test harness, which deliberately replicates the real Supabase platform's own role/default-privilege setup, not a bare vanilla Postgres), replayed all 109 real migration files verbatim in order (clean, no manual fixture, no error), then queried `has_function_privilege('anon', <oid>, 'EXECUTE')` directly against the resulting catalog for every `security definer` function in `public` (56 total, minus pure trigger functions, which PostgREST can never expose as an RPC call regardless of grants).

**The finding**: 52 non-trigger `security definer` functions came back `anon`-executable in the real, current schema (pre-`0120`) - not 8 (the literal-`anon`-grep count), not the ~11 either. Root cause, confirmed by reading `engine/security/scratch_supabase_stub.sql`'s own header (itself documenting a prior pass's own hard-won 2026-10-17/18 lesson) and then reproducing it directly: this project's Postgres roles carry `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on functions to anon, authenticated, service_role` - a DIRECT, NAMED-role grant to `anon` applied automatically to every function at creation time, completely separate from and untouched by the generic `public`-pseudo-role default every vanilla Postgres function also gets. The near-universal migration convention (`revoke all on function X from public; grant execute on function X to authenticated;`, used in essentially every migration from `0003` onward) only ever undoes the SECOND, generic grant - it has never actually removed `anon`'s own direct one. The handful of migrations that DO work correctly (`0055`, `0089`, `0094`/`0095`, `0099`, `0108`, and now `0119`) all happen to spell it `revoke all ... from public, anon` (or a separate explicit `revoke ... from anon`) - confirmed by grepping for the literal string `from anon` across every migration and finding exactly those files, nothing else.

**Not a live, exploitable vulnerability on its own** (checked individually, not assumed, via `pg_get_functiondef()` read for every one of the 52, then verified by direct `set role anon` calls against the scratch database): 4 are the genuine, already-known anon callers (`apply_payfast_itn`, `invite_preview`, `signups_enabled`, `unsubscribe_lifecycle_email` - untouched); `start_payfast_checkout` also matched the bug pattern but was deliberately excluded from the fix below, specifically so this cleanup can't be read as touching its own still-open revenue-integrity judgment call; of the remaining 47, 3 (`tt_pack_company`, `tt_person_in_company`, `tt_tender_visible_to`, 0043) are bare id-to-id relationship booleans never used inside an anon-facing RLS policy (grepped every `create policy` in the schema - every one of the 157 is scoped `to authenticated`, zero target `anon`/`public`), so a direct anon call only confirms "does this id pair exist" with no sensitive payload - the same low-severity calibration Findings 109/110 already used for a sibling case. The other 44 each carry their own internal `auth.uid()`-derived gate (`is_company_member()`/`is_platform_admin()`/`is_employee_in_company()`, an explicit `if not is_platform_admin() then raise exception ... 42501` guard, or an equivalent WHERE-clause filter) that already independently blocks a real `anon` caller today, confirmed directly: `set role anon; select is_platform_admin()` returned `f` (not an error), `select * from platform_admin_companies()` returned 0 rows, `select bank_account_summaries(<any id>)` returned 0 rows - every one already silently inert for `anon`, by the function's own logic, with the grant table never actually being the thing stopping it. This is why the fix below is framed as hardening/defense-in-depth, not a vulnerability patch: it closes a door whose lock was already holding, so nothing a real caller does changes, but a future change that ever weakens one of those internal checks without anyone re-auditing the (misleadingly-already-"revoked") grant table would otherwise land live immediately instead of being caught.

Two functions - `is_company_member()` (0001) and `tt_is_company_admin()` (0050) - turned out to have an even more basic gap than the rest: neither had EVER carried any `revoke`/`grant` statement at all (both pre-date the `revoke all from public` convention), so each still also carried the plain generic `public`-pseudo-role default on top of the named `anon` grant (confirmed via `unnest(proacl)` showing a bare `=X/<owner>` ACL entry - the tell for an un-revoked `public` grant). Both are pure `auth.uid()`-gated booleans (always `false` for `anon`, which has no `auth.uid()` at all) - inert either way - but fixed with `revoke all ... from public, anon` instead of a plain `revoke execute ... from anon`, closing both gaps at once.

**Reproduced directly against the real scratch Postgres 16 instance, red-then-green** (dropped and rebuilt the `auth`/`storage`/`public` schemas from a clean slate first, to rule out stale state from an earlier attempt in the same run): **RED** - pre-`0120`, 52 functions anon-executable (counted via the same query above); `set role anon; select is_platform_admin()` and `select * from platform_admin_companies()` both executed with no `insufficient_privilege`/`permission denied` error (returning `f` / 0 rows respectively - confirming the grant was real, even though the business logic already masked its effect). Applied the real `0120` migration file itself (not a hand-copied fragment) - **GREEN** - anon-executable count dropped to exactly 5 (the 4 genuine callers + the deliberately-excluded `start_payfast_checkout`); the identical `set role anon` calls for `is_platform_admin()`, `platform_admin_companies()`, and `is_company_member(...)` now all raise `permission denied for function ...` (Postgres's own phrasing for `insufficient_privilege`/42501); `set role authenticated` (with a dummy `test.uid` session var the stub reads) still returns the correct business-logic result for all three - `is_platform_admin()` → `f` for a non-admin, `platform_admin_set_setting(...)` → its own `'Only a Tender Tool platform admin can do this'` 42501 raise (unchanged, business-logic-level, not a new grant-level denial), `bank_account_summaries(...)` → 0 rows for a non-member (unchanged) - confirming zero behaviour change for the one role that actually uses these. Scratch database dropped, Postgres service stopped after - also found and dropped 9 unrelated leftover scratch databases from earlier passes that were never cleaned up (`cmdcenter_test`, `narrative_check2`, `narrative_replay_check`, `phase2_replay_check`, `tenant_iso_test`, `tender_tool_replay`/`2`/`3`, `upsert_test`) - a housekeeping fix, not a code change, noted here so a future pass doesn't mistake them for live fixtures.

**Fixed** with new migration `app/supabase/migrations/0120_security_definer_functions_anon_grant_table_cleanup.sql`: 46 `revoke execute ... from anon` statements (one per function, exact signatures taken verbatim from the scratch database's own `pg_get_function_identity_arguments()` output, not hand-typed) plus 2 `revoke all ... from public, anon` statements for the two functions that never had any revoke at all, plus an updated `comment on function is_platform_admin()`. SQL-only, no JS/TS/Python file touched - deliberately excludes `start_payfast_checkout` (judgment-call item, untouched) and the 4 genuine anon callers (`apply_payfast_itn`, `invite_preview`, `signups_enabled`, `unsubscribe_lifecycle_email` - all untouched, same exclusions `0119`'s own entry already used).

**Verified with the full suite** (no app code changed, so no regression possible, but run in full per the standing instruction regardless, from `app/`): `npx tsc --noEmit` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors, 3 warnings** (the same pre-existing `Logo.tsx`/`analytics/page.tsx` warnings every recent entry already documents, confirmed unchanged). `npx vitest run` - **389/389 passed, 50/50 files**, identical to the `fdf51d7` baseline. The separate `node --experimental-strip-types --test` suite over every `*.test.ts` file (27 files) - **238/238 passed**, identical baseline. The migration itself was separately, actually executed against real Postgres as described above, not just parsed.

**Security/grant-table-shaped, but explicitly a hardening/defense-in-depth fix, not a vulnerability patch** - re-stated for anyone skimming: every one of the 46 (really 47, counting `start_payfast_checkout` left alone on purpose) functions already had its own independent, working protection against a real `anon` caller; this migration only removes a redundant, misleadingly-labelled grant that the schema's own comments (`revoke all ... from public` right above a function explicitly commented "Platform-admin only") already show the author intended to remove and believed they had. No role or tenant boundary was loosened - strictly narrower than before, same shape as `0119`.

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** - this pass's own finding is fixed outright (SQL-only, narrowly scoped, verified against real Postgres), not added as a new numbered item. The "pending migrations awaiting Sarel's application to production" item now covers **4** migrations: `0117`, `0118`, `0119`, `0120` - same item, updated count. None of the 4 standing judgment-call items were touched; `start_payfast_checkout()`'s own revenue-integrity gap specifically was read again in the course of this pass (to confirm it matched the grant-table bug pattern) but its underlying payment-timing logic was not touched, and it was deliberately left OUT of this pass's own fix for that reason - restated, not resolved.

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (SQL-only, strictly narrowing, well-verified - same standing convention as `0108`/`0119`):
- `app/supabase/migrations/0120_security_definer_functions_anon_grant_table_cleanup.sql` (new)
- `docs/specs/System-Status.md`

To verify independently: apply `engine/security/scratch_supabase_stub.sql` to a fresh Postgres 16 database, replay every file in `app/supabase/migrations/` in filename order through `0119` (current `main`, pre-`0120`), then run `select count(*) from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid=p.pronamespace where n.nspname='public' and p.prosecdef and p.prorettype != 'trigger'::regtype and has_function_privilege('anon', p.oid, 'EXECUTE');` - expect `52`. ## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): a fresh angle - security-adjacent but NOT PR `#176`'s class - the notification engine's own `claim_notification()`/`record_notification_sent()`/`record_deadline_reminder_sent()`/`record_operational_alert_sent()` were all callable by the truly-anonymous `anon` role (the app's public key, shipped in every client bundle), letting anyone pre-claim a one-time-ever notification token and permanently, silently suppress a real future send - most concretely, `scripts/send-founder-digest.ts`'s own date-only idempotency key makes the founder's own daily digest fully guessable and 100% pre-claimable with no login at all; fixed with a new migration revoking `anon` (keeping `authenticated`, the one genuine webapp caller), verified red-then-green against a real scratch Postgres 16 instance, pushed to `main` as a new migration awaiting Sarel's own application to production, same as `0117`/`0118`

The 3 standing judgment-call items (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-before-ITN gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap in `app/proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format) remain exactly as described in prior entries - not touched, not resolved. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, as expected - `#164`/`#165` (both draft, stale, untouched) and `#176` (open, NOT draft, NOT merged, left exactly as is - re-checked again after this pass's own push, still unchanged).

**Angle chosen**: the directive's own suggestion to look at "RLS policies on any table created/altered by a migration you haven't checked yet" - but reading every table's own RLS-enablement and policy count across all 108 migrations (scripted, not sampled) found RLS enabled everywhere with no gaps; the handful of tables with zero `create policy` statements (`notification_claims`, `lifecycle_unsubscribe_tokens`, `payfast_payment_attempts`, `platform_admins`, `platform_settings`, `sent_deadline_reminders`, `sent_operational_alerts`, `tender_watch_state`) are all deliberately, explicitly documented as "enabled with zero policies so PostgREST still closes it to anon/authenticated by default" - real, intentional "service-role/SECURITY-DEFINER-function-only" tables, not a gap. That led directly to the `grant execute on function ... to anon, authenticated` statements guarding those same SECURITY DEFINER functions, which this doc's own 2026-10-31 security-audit thread (Findings 109/110, migration `0108`) had already combed once - but under a specifically different question ("does this leak another tenant's data to a caller who doesn't own it"). That same entry explicitly names the 4 functions this pass fixes and explicitly declines to flag them: *"The idempotency/logging functions granted to `anon` (`claim_notification`, `record_notification_sent`, `record_deadline_reminder_sent`, `record_operational_alert_sent`) are insert-only with no sensitive read, so an ownership check doesn't apply the same way - noted, not flagged as a new item."* Read that reasoning again against a different question - not "what can `anon` **read**" but "what can `anon` **write**, and does that write alone cause real, irreversible harm" - since `notification_claims`' own primary key is a permanent, non-renewable, one-time-ever resource (0093's own header, and this doc's own repeatedly-fixed "claim a one-time-ever token too early" bug class both depend on exactly that).

**The finding**: all 4 functions are `security definer`, all 4 were granted `execute` to `anon` **and** `authenticated` (0079/0080/0092/0093) - `anon` being PostgREST's role for a request carrying nothing but the app's own public key, which is not a secret (shipped in every client bundle by design - the same framing migration `0108`'s own header comment already uses for the sibling `lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for()` bug it fixed). An anonymous caller doesn't need to read anything back to do real damage here: successfully **writing** a claim before the real sender ever tries to permanently and silently burns that exact future notification, by this engine's own by-design semantics ("already sent, do nothing" - this doc's whole "claim a one-time-ever token too early" bug class already establishes this is a real, serious consequence when the app's own code does it to itself; the same consequence is strictly worse when a stranger does it on purpose). Most concretely and completely reachable: `scripts/send-founder-digest.ts`'s idempotency key is `` `founder-digest-${sastDateKey}` `` - a plain ISO date string, zero UUID/secret material, 100% guessable for any future date with no reconnaissance at all. The other 3 functions' keys are UUID-keyed (company_id/tender_id) - a smaller, not-zero window (an id leaked or guessed some other way), the identical fix either way.

**Confirmed no genuine `anon`-context caller exists for any of the 4**, so revoking `anon` breaks nothing real: grepped every call site across `app/` and `engine/`. No other Server Action, API route, or SQL function calls any of these 4.

Both scratch databases dropped immediately after; Postgres service stopped again before finishing - no trace left running.

- `app/app/company/document-scan/actions.ts`'s `confirmIdDocument()` stamped `company_principals.certified_id_on` - a real `date` column (migration `0050`) - with `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` instead of `lib/publicHolidays.ts`'s own `sastToday()`. A document certified inside the bad window would be silently backdated by one day - a small, honest inaccuracy in a compliance-staleness count, not a false-positive/false-negative flip on its own, but the exact bug class and worth closing the same way every other instance of it in this codebase already was.
- `app/app/people/actions.ts`'s `applyCvExtraction()` built its project `source_note` audit-trail string (`"AI-extracted, confirmed <today>"`, written to `projects.source_note`, free text, never read programmatically) the same way. ## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): the "claim a one-time-ever notification token too early" bug class - already fixed once for `send-returnables-digest.ts` on 2026-10-30 - turned up in 4 more call sites across 2 scripts, missed because the prior sweep grepped only for `claim_notification` callers and these use sibling RPCs (`record_deadline_reminder_sent`, `record_operational_alert_sent`); fixed all 4, with new regression tests, red-then-green

**Context for whoever picks this up next, restated, unchanged**: migrations `0117`/`0118` (employee-RLS fixes) are both on `main` but **still NOT applied to the live production database**; PR `#176` (the 12-function `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC employee-RLS-bypass class) is **still open, independently verified, still awaiting Sarel's own explicit go-ahead to merge**. This pass's own task was explicitly told to stay off both of those (the orchestrator's own open review queue, not something for this pass to add to) - **`0117`/`0118` remain pending Sarel's application to production; PR `#176` remains open, unmerged, and untouched by this pass** - not reviewed, not commented on, not merged.

Oriented from `091e884` (own immediately-preceding pass). `git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only` confirmed clean - already at `091e884`, no new commits from any sibling session, no collision (re-checked again immediately before this entry's own commit - still clean). Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, as expected - `#164`/`#165` (both draft, stale, untouched) and `#176` (open, NOT draft, NOT merged - left exactly as is).

**Angle chosen**: the directive's own suggestion to look for this exact bug class (unguarded write + an irreversible consequence that proceeds regardless) OUTSIDE `app/app/**/actions.ts`, with a genuinely different trigger condition than the already-exhausted RLS membership race. Read every `app/lib/*.ts` helper actually called from a Server Action for a storage-delete-after-unchecked-update shape first (none - the one real `.update(` outside `actions.ts`, `lib/pipeline.ts`'s `advanceFoundToAssessing()`, is an explicitly-documented best-effort call with no downstream consequence either way). Then read every `app/scripts/send-*.ts` cron sender under the service-role key, since RLS doesn't apply there at all - a different mechanism would have to produce the same shape. Found one: every notification-claim RPC in this engine (`claim_notification`, `record_deadline_reminder_sent`, `record_operational_alert_sent`) is an explicit one-time-ever token (migration `0093`'s own header comment, `record_deadline_reminder_sent`'s unique constraint) - claiming it and then never actually sending (for ANY reason) permanently and silently loses that exact notification, even once the reason it couldn't send is later resolved.

**This is not a new bug class** - `send-returnables-digest.ts` was fixed for exactly this shape on 2026-10-30 (claiming before `operationalRecipients()`/render, both of which can fail), and that pass explicitly swept "every other caller of `claim_notification`" looking for the same thing, correctly leaving `send-compliance-digest.ts`/`send-discovered-tenders.ts`/`send-scout-alerts.ts` alone as a documented, batched-send tradeoff (see below for why I didn't re-open that specific call). **But that sweep's own search term - `claim_notification` - never would have found `scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts` or `scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`**: both claim through a different, sibling one-time-claim RPC (`record_deadline_reminder_sent`, `record_operational_alert_sent` - the same "insert with a unique constraint, catch the violation" shape, just not literally named `claim_notification`), so a literal grep for that one name skips them entirely. Read both files in full regardless of that prior "not touched" note, since the directive's own angle doesn't stop at a function name.

**The finding - 4 instances, all genuinely reachable, none batched (so none of the prior pass's "claim-many-before-a-batched-send" reasoning applies)**:
- `scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts`'s main loop: claimed `record_deadline_reminder_sent` BEFORE calling `criticalBidRecipients()` and checking `recipients.length === 0` (the existing `skippedNoMembers` counter proves this branch is genuinely hit in practice, not theoretical). A company with zero registered members at the exact moment this cron runs permanently loses that tender's one 3-day/24-hour closing-deadline reminder for good, even after a member is added before the tender actually closes.
- `scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`'s `runPrintCutoff()`, `runBriefingReminders()`, `runClarificationWindow()` - all three claim `record_operational_alert_sent` BEFORE `operationalRecipients()` (via the shared `claim()` helper, called first in every one of the three loops). Identical consequence for the 48-hour print/transit cutoff, the briefing countdown, and the clarification-window-expiry alert respectively - each a one-shot-per-threshold token, same as `record_deadline_reminder_sent`.
- (Checked in `runPrintCutoff()` while reading it: a second `if (!deadline) continue;` sits after the claim too, but `printSignDeadline()` is called with the exact same inputs `printCutoffCandidates()` already used to compute `hoursLeft` via the identical `hoursUntilPrintSignDeadline()` - which calls `printSignDeadline()` internally and returns null exactly when it's null - so a candidate that already passed `printCutoffCandidates()`'s own filter can never hit this branch. Confirmed by reading both functions side by side, not fixed - genuinely unreachable dead code, not a live bug.)

**Did NOT re-open `send-compliance-digest.ts`/`send-discovered-tenders.ts`/`send-scout-alerts.ts`** (the three the 2026-10-30 pass explicitly checked and left alone). `send-scout-alerts.ts` checks its one recipient (`ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL`) before any claim at all - genuinely fine, re-confirmed by reading it again. The other two DO have the identical "claim per item before the per-company recipients check" shape - re-confirmed by reading both again line by line - but I'm leaving the prior pass's documented "deliberate batched-send tradeoff" verdict as it stands rather than overriding it myself: unlike the two non-batched scripts above, fixing these two properly means restructuring the claim to happen AFTER grouping-by-company (claim each item in a company's own batch only once that company's recipient list is known to be non-empty), which is a materially bigger, batching-semantics-sensitive change than a two-line reorder, and a predecessor already looked at this exact question and reasoned about it explicitly. **Flagged honestly rather than silently dropped**: the stated rationale ("claiming early is deliberate... even if that batch's send later fails") describes a send that is attempted and fails, which is a different event from zero recipients meaning no send is ever attempted at all (no `notification_logs` row either way) - I think the zero-recipients sub-case specifically doesn't actually need the early claim the batching tradeoff justifies, but I'm not confident enough to override a predecessor's explicit, reasoned call on a non-security judgment question without discussing it, and it isn't the kind of unambiguous, mechanically-missed bug (wrong grep term) the other 4 instances are. Left for Sarel's own judgment call or a future pass with more room to restructure the batching carefully - not added to the numbered backlog (same "flagged inline" convention this doc already uses for similarly thin, contestable leads), not fixed.

**Reproduced directly against the real exported functions, red-then-green, not assumed**: both files' core per-candidate logic wasn't previously testable (no export, `main()` invoked unconditionally at module load) - the established project convention, confirmed by reading this doc's own 2026-10-30 entry, is that no `app/scripts/*.ts` file has ever had dedicated test coverage ("a standalone script needing a live Supabase client is heavier to unit-test"). Rather than accept that gap again for a bug this clear-cut and this mechanical to reproduce, split each file's per-candidate loop into an exported, directly-testable function (`processDeadlineReminderCandidates()` in `send-deadline-reminders.ts`; `runPrintCutoff()`/`runBriefingReminders()`/`runClarificationWindow()` in `send-operational-alerts.ts` were already separate functions, just not exported) and guarded each file's top-level `main()` call behind `import.meta.url === \`file://${process.argv[1]}\`` so importing the function for a test no longer also fires a real (doomed, since test env vars aren't real credentials) network call and `process.exit(1)` - verified this guard doesn't change the real CLI behaviour by running both scripts directly with no env vars set and confirming the identical "must both be set" exit-1 message as before. New `app/scripts/send-deadline-reminders.spec.ts` (3 tests) and `app/scripts/send-operational-alerts.spec.ts` (6 tests) use the same sequential/keyed-response Supabase mock technique the `actions.ts` passes already established, adapted for `.rpc()` calls by name and a minimal thenable/chainable `.from()` stub. Ran all 9 new tests against the pre-fix code first (reverted each fix in place, one file at a time, re-ran, restored): **all 9 failed exactly as predicted** - the zero-recipients tests showed the claim RPC called when it must not be, and the ordering tests showed recipients resolved AFTER the claim instead of before. Restored both fixes and reran: **9/9 passed**.

**Fixed** with the minimal correct change in both files, same shape as the already-established `send-returnables-digest.ts` fix: moved the recipients lookup (and, for the non-dry-run path, the `recipients.length === 0` skip) to before the one-time claim call in all 4 loops, leaving every other check, the dry-run row's own display logic, and the actual send/log steps untouched.

**Verified with the full suite**: `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole project) - 0 errors. `npx eslint` on all 4 touched/new files - clean. `npx vitest run` from `app/` - **387/387 passed, 49/49 files** (378 baseline + this pass's 9 new tests across 2 new files - no regression anywhere). The separate `node --experimental-strip-types --test` suite (27 `*.test.ts` files, unaffected since neither touched file is one) - **238/238 passed**. `node --experimental-strip-types --check` on both touched files - clean syntax. `git diff --numstat`: `app/scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts` (+95/-57, most of it the new exported function extracted out of `main()`), `app/scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts` (+34/-14), plus the two new spec files.

**Not security/RLS-shaped** - these scripts run under the Supabase SERVICE ROLE key, so RLS plays no role in this bug at all; the trigger is purely "zero opted-in/registered recipients at the moment the cron fires" (a company mid-onboarding, or one where every member has opted out), exactly the different, non-RLS trigger condition the directive's own angle asked for. No role or tenant boundary touched.

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** - no judgment-call item touched. The `send-compliance-digest.ts`/`send-discovered-tenders.ts` zero-recipients question above is flagged inline (see above), not added to the numbered backlog, same convention this doc already uses for similarly thin, contestable leads (e.g. the `scoreOutlookChips.ts`/`corrigendumAlerts.ts` notes in earlier entries).

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (small, well-verified, no live-DB access needed, no PR):
- `app/scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts`
- `app/scripts/send-deadline-reminders.spec.ts`
- `app/scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`
- `app/scripts/send-operational-alerts.spec.ts`
- `docs/specs/System-Status.md`

`git status --short` confirmed clean before and after (no stray build/cache artifacts at the repo root - everything `--ignored` lists is this repo's own established `.gitignore`d tooling output, `.next/`, `node_modules/`, engine's own per-directory `__pycache__`/`.ruff_cache`, `out/`, `state/`, same as every prior pass's own check - nothing new, nothing to clean up).

To verify independently: run `npx vitest run scripts/send-deadline-reminders.spec.ts scripts/send-operational-alerts.spec.ts` directly (3/3 and 6/6 should pass), then temporarily move the `recipients`/`companyRecipients()` lookup (and its `.length === 0` skip) in any one of the 4 fixed loops back to AFTER its claim call and rerun to see that file's "never claims for zero recipients" test fail exactly as this entry describes. Or read `scripts/send-returnables-digest.ts`'s own 2026-10-30 fix comment and compare directly against `scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts`/`scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`'s pre-this-pass `git show 091e884:app/scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts` to see the identical ordering mistake under a different RPC name.

## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): a genuinely systematic sweep (not another one-off find) of every `app/app/**/actions.ts` `.update(` call turned up three more instances of the same bug class - `company/principals/actions.ts`'s `uploadPrincipalDocument()`, `company/document-scan/actions.ts`'s `confirmVaultDocument()`/`confirmIdDocument()`, `experience/actions.ts`'s `saveExperienceTags()` - all fixed, each verified red-then-green with a new mocked Server Action test (8 new tests total); also settled the previously-undetermined `saveDocumentTemplate()` upsert question with a real scratch Postgres 16 instance (no bug - confirmed, not guessed); pushed to `main` as `0a3ac73`

**Context for whoever picks this up next, restated, unchanged**: migrations `0117`/`0118` (employee-RLS fixes) are both on `main` but **still NOT applied to the live production database**; PR `#176` (the 12-function `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC employee-RLS-bypass class) is **still open, independently verified, still awaiting Sarel's own explicit go-ahead to merge**. This pass's own task was explicitly told to stay off both of those (the orchestrator's own open review queue, not something for this pass to add to) - **`0117`/`0118` remain pending Sarel's application to production; PR `#176` remains open, unmerged, and untouched by this pass** - not reviewed, not commented on, not merged.

Oriented from `7345243` (own immediately-preceding pass: the `uploadVaultDocument()`/`savePropertyDocument()` fix, HEAD confirmed, no sibling-session collision - re-fetched once before committing and once again before pushing, still clean both times). Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, as expected - `#164`/`#165` (both draft, untouched) and `#176` (open, NOT draft, NOT merged - left exactly as is; re-checked again after this pass's own push, still unchanged).

**The sweep method, documented here so a future pass doesn't have to redo it from scratch** (same convention as the employee-RLS systematic check): `grep -n "\.update(" app/app/**/actions.ts` across all 22 `actions.ts` files under `app/app/`, with 3 lines of trailing context, read every hit by hand. For each, judged: (a) is the update checked only by `error`, with no `.select(...).maybeSingle()`/`.single()` already chained onto it, and (b) is there anything consequential AND irreversible downstream in the same function before it returns - specifically a storage delete (the pattern every real instance so far has used), but also watched for an email send, a job/queue insert assuming the write succeeded, or a second write that assumes the first did. Cross-referenced every file with storage-write activity first (`grep -l "storage\.\(from(.*)\.\)\?\(remove\|upload\)\(" app/app/**/actions.ts` - 8 files) since every real instance of this bug class so far has had its consequence be a storage delete; the other 14 `.update(`-containing files either have no downstream storage/irreversible step at all (confirmed by reading each: `app/people/actions.ts`'s `savePerson()`/`applyCvExtraction()`/`discardCvExtraction()`, `app/my-cv/actions.ts`'s three updates, `app/admin/taxonomy/actions.ts`'s two, `app/company/bank-accounts/actions.ts`'s ternary, `app/pipeline/actions.ts`'s one, `app/tenders/[id]/actions.ts`'s three task/milestone updates - none write a file or trigger anything irreversible afterward) or are deliberately out of scope (`app/admin/actions.ts`'s `writeReview()`/`writeAlertResolution()` - security-adjacent to the open `#176` class per the standing instruction not to pursue that file further this pass; confirmed by shape only, neither has a storage/email/job consequence either way, so nothing new to defer from this specific bug class there).

**Of the 8 storage-touching files, 3 were new candidates (not already fixed in `23b43b4`/`7345243`) and all 3 turned out to be genuine, real instances**:
- `app/company/principals/actions.ts`'s `uploadPrincipalDocument()` (certified ID copy / disability proof, 0050, the Document Vault upload pattern) - the exact file-upload sibling of `savePrincipal()` that an earlier pass's own read of this file (five-files pass, `0a2b2eb`'s predecessor) didn't cover, same shape as `savePropertyDocument()` turning out to be `saveProperty()`'s own missed sibling. Reads `existing` path, uploads new file, `supabase.from("company_principals").update(update).eq("id", id)` checked only by `error`, then unconditionally removes the `previous` path. "company_principals: tenant isolation" (0050) is `using (is_company_member(company_id)) with check (is_company_member(company_id))` - the same membership-revoked-mid-request race (another admin's `remove_member_checked()`, 0114) silently no-ops the update and the previous file (a still-valid certified ID or disability-proof document) gets destroyed anyway.
- `app/company/document-scan/actions.ts`'s `confirmVaultDocument()` and `confirmIdDocument()` (the bulk-onboarding-scan review screen's "file this document" actions, 0063) - a genuinely different and *worse* flavour of the same root cause. Both do: `loadPendingResult()` reads the pending result row early; `copyBetweenBuckets()` does a real network download-then-upload round trip (a wider, more realistic race window than any prior instance - this is the first instance with a genuine multi-second network operation between the early read and the final write); then `supabase.from("companies")`/`.from("company_principals")`.update(...).eq("id", ...)` checked only by `error`; then **unconditionally** removes the ORIGINAL onboarding-bucket source file - not a superseded previous copy, the document's only remaining copy at that point. If the race hits (same `remove_member_checked()` mechanism, on "companies: members can update" or "company_principals: tenant isolation"), the just-copied destination file is orphaned AND the source file is destroyed outright - and since `markApplied()`'s own trailing update hits the identical race, the `onboarding_document_results` row is left stuck on `review_status = "pending_review"`, which implies to the UI that the source file is still there to act on. This is actual data loss, not just an orphaned file - worse than every prior instance of this class.
- `app/experience/actions.ts`'s `saveExperienceTags()` (the company experience library's tagging step, 0012) - reads the item's current `storage_path` (`replacedPath`) before uploading a replacement, `supabase.from("experience_items").update(update).eq("id", id)` checked only by `error`, then unconditionally removes `replacedPath`. "experience_items: tenant isolation" (0012) is the same `is_company_member(company_id)` USING-only-on-the-old-row shape. Also noticed in passing and fixed alongside it, since it's the same minimal change: this function never cleaned up the newly-uploaded replacement file on a genuine (non-race) update error either - a separate, lower-severity, pre-existing gap (an orphan, not a destroyed-still-valid-file bug) that existed before this pass and isn't new, but was free to close with the same edit.

**Reproduced directly against the real exported functions**, not assumed, using the established sequential-response-mock technique (`23b43b4`'s own convention, extended this pass with a `storage.from().download()` mock for `copyBetweenBuckets()`'s own real network read): for all three files, with the relevant table's own update queued to return `{data: null, error: null}` (RLS's own real zero-row-match response) - confirmed in every case the action redirected with a false "saved"/"filed" URL pre-fix, and that the destructive storage removal happened regardless. New test files: `app/app/company/principals/actions.spec.ts` (2 tests), `app/app/company/document-scan/actions.spec.ts` (4 tests - `confirmVaultDocument()` and `confirmIdDocument()` each get a race test and a real-match test), `app/app/experience/actions.spec.ts` (2 tests) - none of these three directories had any test coverage before this pass. Ran all three spec files against the pre-fix code first (`git stash push -- <file>`, run, observe failure, `git stash pop`) - **all 4 race-condition tests failed exactly as predicted** (`uploadPrincipalDocument`: `saved=doc` where an error was expected; `confirmVaultDocument`/`confirmIdDocument`: `saved=filed` where an error was expected, in both cases with the onboarding source file still removed; `saveExperienceTags`: `saved=1` where `?error=` was expected). Restored each fix and reran: **8/8 passed**.

**Fixed** with the minimal correct change in all three files, the same established pattern as `23b43b4`/`7345243`: chained `.select("id").maybeSingle()` onto each update and check the returned `data` (not just `error`) before the destructive storage step - `uploadPrincipalDocument()` now checks `error || !updated`; `confirmVaultDocument()`/`confirmIdDocument()` likewise (`updatedCompany`/`updatedPrincipal`); `saveExperienceTags()` likewise (`updated`), with the added new-upload cleanup on any `error || !updated` path (the pre-existing gap noted above).

**Verified with the full suite**: full `npx vitest run` from `app/`: **378/378 passed, 47/47 files** (370/44 baseline + this pass's 3 new files, 8 new tests - no regression anywhere). All 27 `*.test.ts` files (the separate `node --experimental-strip-types`-run suite) re-run directly - 0 failures, unaffected (none touch any of the three changed files). `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole project) - 0 errors. `npx eslint` on all 6 touched/new files - clean. `git diff --stat` (code commit, `0a3ac73`): `app/app/company/principals/actions.ts` (+16/-3), `app/app/company/document-scan/actions.ts` (+30/-6), `app/app/experience/actions.ts` (+17/-3), plus the three new spec files.

**Also settled the `saveDocumentTemplate()` upsert question properly this time**, per the directive's own instruction, with a real scratch Postgres 16 instance rather than guessing from JS mocks (this machine already had `postgresql-16`/`postgresql-client-16` installed; started the cluster with `service postgresql start`, used it, then `service postgresql stop` to leave the machine as it was found). ON CONFLICT (company_id, document_type) DO UPDATE SET ...` statement PostgREST's `.upsert(row, {onConflict: "company_id,document_type"})` issues. **Result: a real, loud error** - `ERROR: 42501: new row violates row-level security policy for table "company_document_templates"`, raised at `ExecWithCheckOptions` (Postgres's own `WITH CHECK` enforcement, not a silent zero-row success). Because this table's policy uses the identical `is_company_member(company_id)` expression for both `USING` and `WITH CHECK`, and `company_id` itself is never part of the written row's changed columns, the two clauses can't diverge for this exact race - confirmed conclusively, not just for the common case. PostgREST surfaces this as a populated `error`, which `saveDocumentTemplate()`'s existing `if (error) { ...back(...) }` already catches correctly before the previous-file removal step is ever reached. **No bug - confirmed, not left undetermined.** The scratch database (`tt_scratch`) was dropped and the Postgres service stopped again before finishing this pass; no trace of it left running or in any migration/schema file.

**The finding - two genuinely fresh instances of the same bug class, both worse than `23b43b4`'s own**: both are in document-upload actions with a "swap the old file for the new one" step, and in both, the final storage cleanup of the *previous* file has no gate on the update having actually matched a row:
- `app/company/actions.ts`'s `uploadVaultDocument()` (vault compliance documents - COID, CIDB, SARS TCS PIN, PI insurance, ISO 9001, bank letter, B-BBEE proof): reads the company's current document path, uploads the new file to storage, then `supabase.from("companies").update({[column]: storagePath}).eq("id", companyId)` checking only `error`, then **unconditionally** `if (previousPath) remove([previousPath])`. "companies: members can update" (0001) is `for update ... using (is_company_member(id))` - re-evaluated against the OLD row, USING only. The realistic trigger: another admin calling `removeMember()` (`remove_member_checked()`, 0114, a real, already-shipped RPC that deletes another user's `company_members` row) on this same signed-in user while their vault-upload form is mid-submit. Confirmed, not assumed, by reading `remove_member_checked()` directly - it's a real deletion, not a soft toggle.
- `app/company/properties/actions.ts`'s `savePropertyDocument()` (per-building lease documents - title deed, owner mandate, zoning/fire/electrical CoC, SAPOA grading, etc., 0050): identical shape - `existing` document row read, new file uploaded, then `supabase.from("property_documents").update(row).eq("id", existing.id)` checking only `error`, then unconditional previous-file removal. "property_documents: tenant isolation" (0050) is the same `using (is_company_member(company_id))`, USING-only-on-the-old-row shape. This is a genuinely different function from `saveProperty()` (the building's own row, line 47 of the same file) - the one the prior pass already read and correctly judged to lack this consequence (it has no inline file upload); `savePropertyDocument()` (line 111) is the file-upload sibling the prior pass's own note didn't cover. Noted but deliberately NOT pursued further: `property_documents`/`company_properties` also carry a `0077` *restrictive* "employee has no access" policy (`is_employee_in_company`) - the same migration series as the open `0117`/`0118`/`#176` employee-RLS work. Confirmed this fix's own trigger (a company_members row disappearing via `removeMember()`) is unrelated to that restrictive policy or to any bypass of it - the bug is the same plain tenant-isolation USING-clause race as `23b43b4`'s and `uploadVaultDocument()`'s, not anything about employee access - but called out explicitly here in case a future pass sees it differently.

**Consequence - worse than `23b43b4`'s own finding**: that fix's bug only orphaned a newly-uploaded file. Here, because the *previous*-file removal is unconditional rather than gated on the update's own success, a zero-row-match update leaves the newly uploaded file orphaned **AND** actively deletes the previous file from storage - a file the row still references (the update never actually changed it) - destroying the company's/building's own still-valid, previously-saved document while the UI reports "Document saved".

**Reproduced directly against the real exported functions**, not assumed, using the sequential-response-mock technique `23b43b4` introduced (no reimplementation of either function's logic): for `uploadVaultDocument()`, pre-fix, with the `companies` update queued to return `{data: null, error: null}` (RLS's own real zero-row-match response) - confirmed the action redirected with `saved=doc` (false success), the new upload was never cleaned up, and the previous file WAS removed (`removeCalls` held exactly the old path, not the new one). For `savePropertyDocument()`, same mock shape against the real `property_documents` update - same three-part confirmation: false `saved=doc`, new upload left in `removeCalls`-untouched state, previous file removed anyway. Both reproductions exercise the real, unmodified exported action (`app/app/company/actions.ts`'s `uploadVaultDocument`, `app/app/company/properties/actions.ts`'s `savePropertyDocument`), not a reimplementation.

**Fixed** with the minimal correct change in both files, mirroring `23b43b4`'s own pattern: chained `.select("id").maybeSingle()` onto the update and check the returned data (not just `error`) before the previous-file removal can be reached - `uploadVaultDocument()` now checks `error || !updated`; `savePropertyDocument()`'s update/insert ternary was restructured into an `if (existing) {...} else {...}` (needed since only the update branch gets the new `.select()`/zero-row check; the insert branch's own RLS `with check` already raises a real error on a genuine violation, it doesn't silently no-op the way the update's `using`-only clause does) with the same `data`-null check added only to the update branch.

Reapplied each fix and reran: **both 2/2 passed**. Full `npx vitest run` from `app/`: **370/370 passed, 44/44 files** (366/42 baseline + this pass's 2 new files, 4 new tests - no regression anywhere). All 27 `*.test.ts` files (the separate `node --experimental-strip-types`-run suite) re-run directly - 0 failures, unaffected (none touch either changed file). `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole project) - 0 errors. `npx eslint` on all 4 touched/new files - clean. `git diff --stat`: `app/app/company/actions.ts` (+15/-2), `app/app/company/properties/actions.ts` (+18/-5), plus the two new spec files.

Not security/RLS-shaped - same reasoning `23b43b4` already established for this exact bug class: RLS is working exactly as designed in both cases (correctly refusing a write once the caller is no longer a member of the company the row belongs to); the bug is purely the app-level code not noticing that correctly-enforced refusal before doing something irreversible (deleting a file) on the strength of a false "it worked" read. No role or tenant boundary was changed by either fix. The one security/RLS-adjacent thing noticed in passing - `property_documents`/`company_properties`'s `0077` restrictive employee-no-access policy, in the same migration series as the open `#176` work - is called out above as checked-and-unrelated, not touched, not treated as a new finding to defer.

WHERE` - confirming whether it fails loudly (an actual RLS-violation error) or silently (zero-row no-op) on this exact race needs real Postgres semantics to settle, not something a JS-level mock can establish either way.
