**Moved to `formatZAR.ts`** (the canonical Rand formatter, Sarel's own 2026-10-24 Batch 6 brief - "the one place financial, tender value, and BOQ numbers get formatted") - read the whole file plus its existing `formatZAR.test.ts` (13 tests, all passing) end to end. Its `compact` option (`"R 1.5M"`/`"R 250k"` for KPI/summary badges) is implemented by `compactMagnitude()`: divide by 1,000 or 1,000,000, then `toFixed(1)` (dropped to `toFixed(0)` when the *raw*, un-rounded value is already a whole number) - checked specifically for a rounding-boundary bug, since `toFixed()` rounding combined with a hard `>=` threshold on the raw value is exactly the shape that produces an off-by-one at the boundary.

**The finding**: for any value in `[999_950, 999_999]`, `compactMagnitude()` takes the `>= 1_000` branch (correctly, since `abs < 1_000_000`), computes `k = abs / 1_000` (e.g. `999.95` to `999.999`), and `k.toFixed(1)` rounds that up to `"1000.0"` - so the function returns the literal string `"1000.0k"` instead of promoting to the next unit. **Reproduced directly against the real exported function**, no guessing: `node -e` calling the file's own (pre-fix) `compactMagnitude` logic for `999_950`/`999_999`/`999_999` all printed `"1000.0k"`; `999_949` (one rand below the boundary) correctly printed `"999.9k"`. The only real production call site today (`app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx`'s completed-project-value line, `formatZAR(Number(completionValue) * 1_000_000, { compact: true })`) can't currently hit this exact window in practice - `project_completion_value_rm` is `numeric(16,2)` (migration `0065`), so its value in Rand is always a multiple of R10,000, and the nearest reachable value below R1,000,000 is R990,000, well clear of the `[999_950, 999_999]` window - but `formatZAR.test.ts`'s own existing compact-mode tests (`1_500_000`, `2_000_000`, `250_000`, `1_500`) show this is written and tested as a general-purpose formatter for exactly this kind of KPI/summary display, not a single-caller helper; a narrower future input (a different KPI badge, a change to that column's precision) would hit it silently. Fixed as a real bug in shared, documented, tested logic, not deferred as unreachable-today - same reasoning the `scoreOutlookChips.ts` note two passes ago used to justify the opposite call (there, two independent narrow conditions had to coincide on data no real tender has ever produced; here, the only thing standing between the bug and a real user is one column's current numeric precision, which is a much thinner guarantee).

**Fixed** with the minimal correct change: `compactMagnitude()` now also promotes to the `M` branch when `Math.round((abs / 1_000) * 10) / 10 >= 1_000` - i.e. when the thousands figure, rounded to the same 1 decimal place the function already displays, would itself hit 1000 - not just when the raw value is already `>= 1_000_000`. The `M` branch's own existing formatting (raw-value wholeness check, `toFixed(0)`/`toFixed(1)`) is unchanged and untouched; the fix only changes which branch a boundary value takes, so `999_950` and `999_999` now correctly render `"1.0M"` (matching the already-existing "whole millions drop the decimal, fractional ones don't" rule - `0.99995` isn't whole, so it keeps the decimal, same as `1.5M`).

**Verified red-then-green, with new tests added to the existing `formatZAR.test.ts`**: added `"formatZAR: compact rounds up into the next magnitude instead of printing '1000.0k'"`, asserting `999_950` and `999_999` both render `"R 1.0M"` and `999_949` still renders `"R 999.9k"`. Run against the pre-fix file first (confirmed how this repo's own `*.test.ts` convention is actually executed, since `vitest` only picks up `*.spec.ts` - read `.github/workflows/app-ci.yml`'s own header comment, which documents exactly this split and the `node --experimental-strip-types` invocation): **1 of 14 failed exactly as predicted** (`999_950`/`999_999` both printed `"R 1000.0k"`, not `"R 1.0M"`), the other 13 pre-existing tests still passed. Applied the fix and reran: **14/14 passed, 0 failures**. Ran every other `*.test.ts` file in the repo the same way `app-ci.yml` does (`find . -name "*.test.ts" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"`, 27 files total) - all 27 passed, 0 regressions (nothing else imports `formatZAR`'s internal `compactMagnitude` directly). Full `npx vitest run` from `app/`: **360/360 passed, 39/39 files**, unchanged (no `.spec.ts` file touches this function). `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole project) - 0 errors. `npx eslint lib/formatZAR.ts lib/formatZAR.test.ts` - clean. `git diff --stat`: `lib/formatZAR.ts` (+6/-1), `lib/formatZAR.test.ts` (+10).

Not security/RLS-shaped (a pure display-formatting function with no table read, no role/tenant boundary anywhere near it) - in scope for this pass, not deferred. No new security/RLS-shaped finding was made along the way to defer either.

**Picked the directive's own "fresh Server Action correctness pass" angle**: grepped this doc's own history for mention counts of every `app/**/actions.ts` file by its own directory name (not just the generic string "actions.ts", which every entry matches loosely) to find genuinely under-reviewed ones. `app/app/pipeline/actions.ts` (1 mention) stood out - core business logic (moving a tender between kanban stages, recording bid economics, recording a won/lost outcome), never read end to end on its own before. Read `moveTenderStage()`, `saveTenderEconomics()`, and `recordOutcomeAndMoveStage()` in full, plus every real caller (`pipeline/page.tsx`'s `StageButton`/`TenderCard`, `pipeline/outcome-form.tsx`'s `OutcomeForm`) - not just the action file in isolation, since a Server Action's correctness here depends on which stages the UI actually offers it for.

`moveTenderStage()` and `saveTenderEconomics()` both held up on a careful read (validation via `parseRand`/`parsePercent`'s own documented `undefined`-for-blank-vs-`null`-for-unparseable contract, correctly distinguished at every call site - re-checked by hand rather than assumed, since a `=== null` vs `!= null` mixup here is exactly the kind of off-by-one this file's own density of blank/garbage-input branches invites). `recordOutcomeAndMoveStage()` itself is also correct in isolation. **The real bug was in which stages the UI wires these actions up for, not in the actions themselves.**

**The finding**: `lib/pipeline.ts`'s `NEXT_STAGES` (widened by migration `0105` to add `briefing_shortlisted` as a second, buyer-dependent path from `submitted` to an outcome, alongside going straight to `won`/`lost`) says `submitted -> ["briefing_shortlisted", "won", "lost"]` and `briefing_shortlisted -> ["won", "lost"]`. But `pipeline/page.tsx`'s `TenderCard` rendered its plain forward-action button bar under `card.stage !== "submitted" && (NEXT_STAGES[card.stage].length > 0 || back)` - i.e. for a card at `submitted`, the ENTIRE forward-button block was hidden, not just the two outcome targets within it. The only other path forward from `submitted` is `pipeline/outcome-form.tsx`'s `OutcomeForm`, whose two submit buttons only ever post `stage="won"` or `stage="lost"` - never `"briefing_shortlisted"`. **Net effect: no button anywhere in the product could ever move a tender from `submitted` to `briefing_shortlisted`.** Confirmed this wasn't a theoretical reading of dead code by checking every real writer of `tender_packs.pipeline_stage` in the whole codebase (`grep -rn "pipeline_stage" app engine` excluding tests/specs) - exactly two: `moveTenderStage()`'s upsert and `recordOutcomeAndMoveStage()`'s upsert, both in this same file, both driven only by what a form's hidden `stage` input is set to by the UI above. No RPC, trigger, or engine job sets it either (migration `0105`'s own header comment confirms `briefing_shortlisted` "only ever follows [submitted]" and is purely a UI-driven move, same as every other stage transition). `engine/seed_demo_company.py`'s own demo data never seeds a `briefing_shortlisted` example either - one more sign this stage had never actually been exercised by anything. **A real, shipped 0105 feature (one of Sarel's own named 7 pipeline columns, confirmed built in `app/AGENTS.md`'s own "Bids pipeline redesign" write-up) was functionally dead on arrival.**

**This directly bears on, and partially overturns, a 2026-11-02 pass's own explicit judgment call** (same doc, "one more targeted sweep for the missing-`briefing_shortlisted` bug class" entry): that pass traced the SAME `OutcomeForm` stage gate, noticed a `briefing_shortlisted` card gets plain Won/Lost buttons with no outcome form, and deliberately left it alone, reasoning "a `briefing_shortlisted` tender can still advance to `won`/`lost` via the plain stage-advance buttons... and `OutcomeForm` correctly reappears once it reaches `won`/`lost`... a legitimate product-flow nuance... not a correctness bug." That reasoning is only sound if a tender can actually reach `briefing_shortlisted` in the first place - and, per the finding above, none ever could, through any UI path that pass didn't check. Not relitigating that pass's own point (a `briefing_shortlisted` card CAN reach won/lost via a plain button once it's there, bypassing the outcome form at that one step - true, and still worth closing while fixing the rest) - extending it with the one check it didn't make.

**Fixed** with the minimal change that resolves both symptoms from their one shared root cause (two hand-kept stage lists that had to stay in sync and didn't), rather than patching each site separately: added `OUTCOME_STAGES` (`["won", "lost"]`) and `OUTCOME_FORM_STAGES` (every stage `NEXT_STAGES` can reach `won`/`lost` from, plus `won`/`lost` themselves - computed from `NEXT_STAGES` itself, not hand-listed a second time) to `lib/pipeline.ts`. `pipeline/page.tsx`'s forward-button bar now filters `won`/`lost` out of its own plain button list (`forwardStages`) instead of hiding the WHOLE bar for `submitted` - so `submitted` now offers a real "Mark briefing / shortlisted" button (its `ACTION_LABEL`/`EMPTY_COPY` entries already existed, unused, before this fix) alongside its outcome-form path, and `briefing_shortlisted` no longer offers plain Won/Lost buttons at all. `outcome-form.tsx`'s own gate now reads `OUTCOME_FORM_STAGES.includes(stage)` instead of hand-listing `submitted`/`won`/`lost`, so it now also renders (and auto-opens, matching `submitted`'s existing UX) on `briefing_shortlisted` - closing the exact gap the 2026-11-02 pass flagged but left alone.

**Verified red-then-green, with a real new test** (`lib/pipeline.spec.ts` - no React rendering test infrastructure exists in this codebase, confirmed by checking `package.json` for `testing-library`/`jsdom`/`happy-dom`, none present, so the fix is tested the same way this file's existing tests already do: as a structural invariant on the exported stage-list constants, not a rendered-DOM assertion): 3 new tests - `OUTCOME_FORM_STAGES` is exactly `submitted`/`briefing_shortlisted`/`won`/`lost`; it covers every stage `NEXT_STAGES` can reach `won`/`lost` from (the structural invariant that makes this exact bug class impossible to silently reintroduce by adding a new path to an outcome without also wiring `OutcomeForm` up to it); it excludes `found`/`assessing`/`building`. ## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): found and fixed a real gap in the narrative generator's own anti-collusion safeguard - `generate_with_uniqueness_check()` computed `similarity_score`/`similarity_flagged` BEFORE the mandatory 3-pass self-review loop ran, and the review loop's own output (which is what actually gets saved as `generated_text`) was never re-checked - so a draft that cleared the uniqueness check pre-review could come out of review rewritten close to a competitor's own document and still carry `similarity_flagged: false`. **Quick, non-exhaustive follow-up on the just-exhausted `setMonth`/`setFullYear` bug class, per the directive's own suggestion**: grepped `engine/` for the equivalent Python shape (`relativedelta|\.replace\(month=|\.replace\(year=`) in case a third instance existed in a different language. Not the same bug, not a new instance - genuinely clean, moved on without forcing it.

**Picked the directive's own "fuzzy-matching/heuristic function" angle, but in `engine/`, not `app/lib/`** - `engine/narrative/uniqueness.py`, the narrative generator's (`generate_narrative.py`, used by `process_narrative_jobs.py` for cover letters/methodology statements) own stdlib-`difflib`-based anti-collusion check. This module's own header comment states plainly why it exists (Sarel, 2026-10-22, verbatim): the generator "may NEVER generate the same or similar versions for two companies - then they might both get disqualified." Checked several other candidates first and ruled them out with a concrete reason (not forced): `lib/vaultDocuments.ts`'s `vaultDocumentMismatchWarning()` (filename-only, non-blocking warning, internally consistent); `lib/opportunityBuyerMatch.ts` (already checked clean by the 2026-11-04 pass below - not re-litigated); `lib/scoutAnomalyAlerts.ts`'s `scoutAnomalyCandidates()` (correct filter logic, already has its own dedicated spec file). Also did a full line-by-line read of the PayFast ITN route's OTHER logic per the directive's own suggestion (signature-stripping regex edge cases, the source-IP/server-confirmation checks, `apply_payfast_itn()`'s amount_gross comparison) - all of it holds up: `verifyItnSignature()`'s `signature=` strip regex correctly handles the field appearing first, middle, or (its only real position) last in the raw body; the amount check compares `numeric` to `numeric` with whole-Rand prices (1490/2990/4990/14900/29900/49900), so there's no floating-point rounding exposure to find. Nothing new there - not forced into a finding that wasn't real.

**The finding**, in `generate_with_uniqueness_check()` (`engine/narrative/generate_narrative.py`): the function generates a draft, checks it with `check_uniqueness()` against every OTHER company's ready document of the same kind for the same tender, and - if flagged - regenerates ONCE with a distinctness instruction. All correct so far. It THEN runs the mandatory 3-pass self-review loop (`run_review_passes()`, the `AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md` "never the first answer" loop Sarel asked for) on whichever draft that left it with, and returns `plain_text` built from the review loop's OWN final sections - but `similarity_score`/`similarity_flagged` were never recomputed after that point, so the values `process_narrative_jobs.py` actually writes to `narrative_documents` next to `generated_text` described a draft that no longer exists, not the text that was actually saved. The review loop's own prompt (per `build_prompt.py`'s `build_review_user_message()`) asks the model to re-check correctness/quality and ALWAYS returns full corrected text, even on a pass that reports "no issues found" - nothing in that prompt asks the model to preserve distinctiveness, so a clean review pass can legitimately rewrite a paragraph back toward generic/boilerplate phrasing, which is exactly the shape this module's own similarity check exists to catch. A header comment on the function already acknowledged NOT re-running the uniqueness check after review, framing it as "a deliberate ordering choice, not an oversight" to avoid the two checks "chasing" each other - true for not re-triggering another distinctness-retry-then-review cycle, but it also meant the STORED verdict could be stale for the actual saved document, which that comment didn't address.

**Reproduced for real** (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/repro_narrative/repro.py`, using the same `StubClient` convention `test_generate_narrative.py` already uses - no real Anthropic key touched): a genuinely distinct first draft ("Mahlangu Civils will deploy its own dedicated grader fleet and site agent") scored 0.42 against a competitor's ready text ("We propose a phased construction methodology with weekly site meetings and dedicated quality control") - correctly NOT flagged, no distinctness retry triggered. A review pass that reports "no issues found" but rewrites the paragraph to near-match the competitor's own wording then runs. Before the fix: the function returned `similarity_score: 0.42`, `similarity_flagged: False` - but the actual `plain_text` it returned (what gets saved as `generated_text`) scored **0.94** against the same competitor text when re-checked with the exact same `check_uniqueness()` call - genuinely over the 0.6 threshold, the precise "two companies' submissions read suspiciously alike" case this feature exists to catch, shipped with a false "all clear" flag.

**Fixed** with the minimal correct change: after `run_review_passes()` returns, `check_uniqueness()` is called a second time against the review loop's own final `plain_text`, and THAT score/flagged pair is what gets returned (and stored). No new LLM call, no second distinctness-retry-then-review cycle is added - the fix deliberately does not reintroduce the "chasing" risk the existing header comment correctly flagged; it only makes the stored verdict honest about the text that was actually saved, the same "a human decides, never silently assumed" discipline `quality_flagged` already applies to the review loop's own output elsewhere in this same function.

**Verified red-then-green, with a real new test**: new `test_similarity_is_recomputed_against_the_review_loop_s_own_output()` in `engine/narrative/test_generate_narrative.py`, using the exact reproduced scenario above. Reverted just `generate_narrative.py` (`git stash push -- generate_narrative.py`, keeping the new test) and reran: **2 of the new test's own checks failed exactly as predicted** (`similarity_flagged` read `False` when the test expects `True`; `similarity_score` read `0.46` when the test expects `> 0.6`) - every other test in the file still passed, 0 other regressions. Restored the fix and reran: all checks passed, **0 failures** across the whole file. Full `python3 engine/narrative/test_generate_narrative.py` - 0 failures (all 24 pre-existing checks plus the 5 new ones in the new test). `python3 engine/narrative/test_process_narrative_jobs.py`, `test_build_prompt.py`, `test_build_docx.py`, `test_uniqueness.py` - all unaffected, 0 failures each (no other module reuses `generate_with_uniqueness_check()` - confirmed by `grep -rln generate_with_uniqueness_check engine/`, only `generate_narrative.py` itself and its own two test files). `python3 -m py_compile` on both changed files - clean. `ruff check engine/narrative/generate_narrative.py engine/narrative/test_generate_narrative.py` - the same 7 pre-existing findings (all in untouched test-file lines, confirmed identical before and after this change via `git stash`) - 0 new findings introduced.

Not security/RLS-shaped (an internal engine heuristic feeding a company's own narrative document generation - no role or tenant boundary anywhere near this code; `other_texts` was already being fetched correctly, cross-tenant, by the service-role worker before this fix, exactly as the module's own design requires - this fix only corrects WHEN the comparison against it is made, not what it's allowed to read) - in scope for this pass, not deferred. Read `docs/specs/AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md` before touching this (per `CLAUDE.md`'s own instruction for any LLM-call-adjacent change) - confirmed the fix adds no new LLM call and doesn't alter the generate-then-3-pass-review loop's own shape in any way the standard governs; it only recomputes an existing, local, stdlib-only `difflib` comparison once more, after that loop finishes, against the text the loop actually produced.

## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): a full correctness read of the PayFast ITN route itself (not the already-deferred redelivery-idempotency question) found a genuine JS-Date "month overflow" bug in `nextPeriodEnd()` - and the identical bug class, independently, in `lib/properties.ts`'s `tooOld()` - fixed both, verified red-then-green, pushed to `main`

**Context for whoever picks this up next, restated, unchanged**: migrations `0117`/`0118` (employee-RLS fixes) are both on `main` but **still NOT applied to the live production database**; PR `#176` (the 12-function `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC employee-RLS-bypass class) is **still open, independently verified, still awaiting Sarel's own explicit go-ahead to merge**. This pass's own task was explicitly told to stay off both of those, off the pagination-cap bug class (now exhausted), and off `lib/cvExtraction.ts` (just fixed by the immediately preceding pass) - so it picked one of the directive's own named candidates instead: a full correctness read of the PayFast ITN route handler itself. **`0117`/`0118` remain pending Sarel's application to production; PR `#176` remains open, unmerged, and untouched by this pass** - not reviewed, not commented on, not merged.

Oriented from `34ef912` (own prior pass: `cvExtraction.ts`'s bare-year false positive). `git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only` confirmed clean - already at `34ef912`, no new commits, no collision (re-checked again immediately before this entry - still clean). Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, as expected - `#164`/`#165` (both draft, untouched since 2026-10-26, not touched) and `#176` (open, NOT draft, NOT merged - left exactly as is).

**Read this doc's own last several entries first, to avoid retreading ground.** The PayFast ITN handler's own prior coverage, confirmed from this doc's history before starting: signature (Finding 54, verified against PayFast's own official SDK test fixture); source IP + server confirmation (both read and confirmed correct); `amount_gross` verification (migration `0112` - `tt_plan_price_zar()` mirrors `lib/billing.ts`'s pricing exactly, confirmed side by side, no VAT mismatch either); the `current_period_end`-on-FAILED bug (migration `0110`); the webhook-redelivery idempotency gap (found, reproduced live against a scratch Postgres on 2026-10-25, deliberately left as Sarel's own judgment call since - needs a new `pf_payment_id`-keyed dedup table, not a one-line guard, and there's no live money or a real recurring customer this can affect yet). None of those were re-opened or re-litigated this pass - this pass did a *fresh* line-by-line read of the route handler's own logic (`app/api/billing/payfast/itn/route.ts`) that no prior pass had done end to end, rather than re-checking any of the above.

**The finding**: `nextPeriodEnd()` (the private helper the route used to compute the new `current_period_end` an ITN-triggered activation writes) counted a month/year forward with a bare `date.setMonth(date.getMonth() + 1)` / `date.setFullYear(date.getFullYear() + 1)`. Plain JS `Date` arithmetic "overflows" into the following month whenever the target month is shorter than the current day-of-month - e.g. Jan 31 has no Feb 31, so `setMonth` silently lands on Mar 3, not Feb 28. This is **not a rare edge case for a recurring monthly charge**: any customer whose billing date happens to fall on the 31st of January, March, May, August or October gets their "paid through" date (shown on `/admin/billing`, and the field that drives what `status`/`current_period_end` combination the admin sees) pushed 1-2 real days further out than a genuine calendar month, every single cycle that lands on one of those dates - not a one-off.

**Checking for the same bug class elsewhere, mechanically** (the same discipline prior "exhausted a bug class" passes used): `grep -rn "setMonth\|setFullYear" app --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v node_modules` - exactly 3 matching lines in the whole app: 2 inside the route's own `nextPeriodEnd()` (the finding above) and 1 in `lib/properties.ts:98`'s `tooOld()` (the Company Properties page's "this compliance document is past the tender rule's own age limit" check, live-used by `app/company/properties/page.tsx`, confirmed by `grep -rn tooOld app`) - the **identical bug**: a 12-month-validity document (`pest_control_certificate`/`sapoa_grading`, both `maxAgeMonths: 12`) issued on a leap day (Feb 29) gets its expiry silently rolled to March 1 of the following (non-leap) year instead of landing on the real Feb 28 anniversary - reading as still valid one extra day past the tender rule's own cutoff. No other file in the codebase does bare month/year `Date` arithmetic at all - this bug class is now exhausted across the whole `app/` tree.

**Reproduced for real, not just reasoned from reading it** - standalone script run directly (copying each function's old logic verbatim): `nextPeriodEnd("monthly")` with the system clock set to `2026-01-31T10:00:00.000Z` returned `2026-03-03T10:00:00.000Z` (should be `2026-02-28`); set to `2026-03-31T10:00:00.000Z` returned `2026-05-01T10:00:00.000Z` (should be `2026-04-30`). `tooOld()`'s old logic, given `issued_on: "2024-02-29"` and `maxAgeMonths: 12`, computed a limit of `2025-03-01` (should be `2025-02-28`) - so on `2025-03-01` itself (the document's real one-year-and-one-day-old date) the old code said NOT too old, wrongly.

**Fixed** by routing both through `date-fns`'s `addMonths()` (already a `package.json` dependency, previously imported nowhere in `app/lib` - confirmed by `grep -rln 'from "date-fns"' lib app` returning nothing before this change) instead of reinventing the clamping logic: `addMonths()` correctly clamps to the last day of the target month when the original day doesn't exist there, which is the correct calendar-anniversary behaviour for both a billing period and a document-validity window. `nextPeriodEnd()` itself was moved out of the route handler into `lib/payfast.ts` as a plain exported function (a `route.ts` file in the App Router may only export HTTP method handlers - `GET`/`POST`/etc - so it couldn't be given real test coverage in place; confirmed no other `route.ts` in this codebase exports anything beyond its HTTP method before making this change, so this wasn't already a precedent to just follow). The route now imports it from there, alongside its other already-externalized PayFast logic (`verifyItnSignature`, `decodePlanInterval`, etc.) - consistent with that file's own existing "every testable PayFast rule lives here, the route only orchestrates" shape.

**Verified red-then-green, with real new test coverage**: `lib/payfast.spec.ts` gained 5 new cases for `nextPeriodEnd()` (using `vi.setSystemTime()` to control "now" precisely) - the two reproduced overflow cases (now correctly `2026-02-28`/`2026-04-30`), a leap-day yearly case (`2028-02-29` -> correctly `2029-02-28`, not `2029-03-01`), and two ordinary-date sanity checks (monthly and yearly) confirming no overcorrection. Not a gap.

**The finding**, in `app/lib/cvExtraction.ts`'s `looksLikeExistingProject()` (zero mentions anywhere in this doc's history - genuinely never reviewed; used live by exactly one caller, `app/people/[id]/cv-review.tsx`, confirmed by `grep -rn looksLikeExistingProject app`): the CV-review page's own "is this proposed project probably already on file" pre-tick heuristic matched on ANY shared 4+ digit token, including a bare 4-digit token that is just a calendar year. A company that completes more than one project in the same year - the ordinary case, not an edge case - would have a genuinely NEW project from a freshly-uploaded CV wrongly flagged as a likely duplicate of an UNRELATED existing project that merely shares that year, purely because both client/contract lines contain, e.g., "2024" somewhere. The page's own header comment on this function says plainly it exists to "leave a likely duplicate unticked... never to hide it" - but a false positive here does exactly that: `cv-review.tsx`'s "Add this project" checkbox defaults UNTICKED whenever `dup` is true (`defaultChecked={proj.verified && !dup}`), so a reviewer who trusts the automatic flag (plausible - it's shown as a pre-answered judgement, "already on file?") and doesn't compare the two project lines by hand would silently never add a real, new project to the Experience Library from that CV.

**Reproduced for real, not just reasoned from reading it** - standalone script (`/tmp/repro_cv/looksLike.mjs`, the function copied verbatim): `looksLikeExistingProject("XYZ Municipality Water Treatment Plant Upgrade, 2024", ["ABC Municipality - Reservoir Project, completed 2024"])` returned `true` - two unrelated projects for different clients, flagged as a duplicate purely because both happen to mention 2024.

**Fixed** by excluding a token that is a bare 4-digit plausible calendar year (`1900`-`2099`, via a new `BARE_YEAR` regex) from the "numbers" list used for the match, while leaving every other signal unchanged: the whole-line exact match, and any digit token that is NOT a bare year (a real contract/project reference like "2024/15" or "GG2024-01" squashes to something longer than 4 characters and is untouched by this exclusion, so a genuine duplicate sharing a real reference number is still caught). Matches the function's own stated bias: a weak/ambiguous signal (a shared year alone) must resolve toward NOT flagging, since hiding a real new project is the worse direction, not occasionally re-showing an actual duplicate for the reviewer to tick off by hand.

**Verified red-then-green, with a real new test file** (`app/lib/cvExtraction.spec.ts` - this file had zero test coverage before this pass): 5 cases - the reproduced false positive (year-only collision, now correctly `false`), a real shared reference number embedding a year (still correctly `true`, confirming the fix doesn't overcorrect), an identical whole-line match (still `true`), a genuine non-year 4+ digit project number (still `true`), and two unrelated projects with no shared number at all (correctly `false`). Reverted the fix with the new test file kept (`git stash push -- lib/cvExtraction.ts`) and reran: the first case failed exactly as predicted (`expected true to be false`), every other case still passed; restored the fix and reran: all 5 passed. Full `npx vitest run` from `app/`: **347/347 passed, 38/38 files** (342/37 baseline + this pass's 5 new tests in 1 new file - no regression anywhere). `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint lib/cvExtraction.ts lib/cvExtraction.spec.ts` - clean. `git diff --stat`: exactly `app/lib/cvExtraction.ts` (18 insertions, 4 deletions) plus the new `app/lib/cvExtraction.spec.ts` file.

Not security/RLS-shaped (a client-side UI pre-tick default on a form the signed-in user already has full write access to - no role or tenant boundary anywhere near this code) - in scope for this pass, not deferred. No new security/RLS-shaped finding was made along the way to defer either.

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** - no judgment-call item touched (`held_registrations`-vs-CV, `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-before-ITN gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap, and the separate PayFast ITN webhook-redelivery idempotency design question all untouched, as directed/by design). This pass's own finding was a new, standalone, non-security UI-correctness bug, fixed outright - not added to the backlog.

(b) What is the REAL scope of the query once RLS is applied - not just "is there an explicit `.eq("company_id", ...)`" (several queries have none and are still safely company-scoped, because RLS itself narrows them: `lib/notifications.ts`'s bell and `lib/documentExpiry.ts` both read `held_registrations`/`people`/`tenders` with no explicit company filter at all, but the signed-in user's own RLS context already narrows every one of them, `tenders` via its own `tender_packs!inner(...)` has-many embed, which is itself RLS-scoped to the caller's company).
3. The judgement call, same one already applied to `cv_uploads`: does the table's REAL scope for this query (not the table in the abstract) realistically accumulate past 1000 rows? Two shapes are genuinely at risk and worth re-checking on a future pass as the product grows: (i) a per-company table with **no retention** (every write is a new row, nothing is ever overwritten or deleted) - `cv_uploads` was this shape; `held_registrations`/`people`/`company_principals`/`experience_items`/`person_role_eligibility` were all individually checked this pass and are NOT this shape (edits are real `UPDATE`s in place via their own `actions.ts`, confirmed by reading each one, not assumed) - their own per-company row count stays naturally bounded to "how many registrations/staff/principals/CV-line-items a company genuinely has," not "how many times anyone has ever clicked save." (ii) a table that is **shared/cross-tenant by design**, where a single query's real row count is the SUM across every company or every buyer, not one company's own slice - this is the shape this pass's 5 findings all share, and it is structurally far more dangerous than (i) because the table was never meant to be company-scoped in the first place: `tenders`/`tender_requirements` (migration `0001`'s own header comment: "SHARED/PUBLIC...Shared across every company - not tenant-scoped", fed daily by a dozen+ discovery scrapers that THIS SESSION's own prior live-tests already found return 268 (`capetown_procurement.py`) and 292 (`kouga.py`) rows EACH from a single buyer) and, separately, any query against `tender_packs`/`tender_update_notifications`-shaped tables run under the SERVICE ROLE key in a `scripts/send-*.ts` cron sender (RLS is bypassed entirely there, so the query sums EVERY company's own rows together in one response, not just the caller's).

**Findings - 5 call sites across 4 files, all the shared/cross-tenant shape (ii) above, none the per-company shape (i)**:
1. **`lib/personCredentials.ts`'s `registrationsAskedFor()`** (used live by `/people/[id]`, confirmed by `grep -rn registrationsAskedFor app`) - both its `tender_requirements` read (joined `tenders!inner(...)`, filtered `.eq("tenders.status", "open")`) and its `tenders` read (filtered `.eq("status", "open")`) are plain, unranged `.select()`s against the shared, not-tenant-scoped catalog, readable by every authenticated user regardless of company (0001's own RLS policy, `"tenders readable by authenticated users"`/`"tender_requirements readable by authenticated users"` - PERMISSIVE, no company check at all). Past the cap, this would silently stop showing "this tender asks for SACNASP/SAGC/SACAP/..." badges on the People page for whichever open tenders sort past row 1000 - understating real demand for a registration, not a cosmetic miscount.
2. **`scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts`** - the `tenders` x `tender_packs!inner(company_id, pipeline_stage)` read (`.not("closing_date", "is", null)`, no range), run under the SERVICE ROLE key. `lib/deadlineReminders.ts`'s own doc comment already says outright that this is "the shared/public table...more than one unrelated company routinely tracks the exact same tender" - this read sums EVERY company's own tender_packs into one response. Past the cap, this would silently stop sending the "closing in 3 days / 24 hours" reminder for whichever tender/company pairs sort past row 1000 - a missed bid deadline, not a cosmetic gap.
3. **`scripts/send-returnables-digest.ts`** - the identical `tenders` x `tender_packs!inner(...)` shape, same SERVICE ROLE scope, feeding the "mandatory returnable missing 3-5 business days before closing" nudge.
4. **`scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`'s `runPrintCutoff()`** - reads `tender_packs` (filtered `.eq("submission_type", "physical_box")`, optionally further filtered by `--company-id`) summed across every company at once when run unscoped, feeding the 48-hour print/transit-cutoff alert.
5. **`scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`'s `runBriefingReminders()`** - the same `tenders` x `tender_packs!inner(company_id)` shape as #2/#3, feeding the 5-day/24-hour briefing-session countdown.

**Checked and deliberately NOT changed, with the specific reasoning per item** (so a future pass doesn't need to re-derive these):
- `lib/notifications.ts`'s `getNotifications()` (the topbar bell) reads the exact same `tenders` x `tender_packs!inner(id)` shape as findings #2/#3/#5 above - but this one runs in a normal request under the SIGNED-IN USER's own session, not the service role, so `tender_packs`'s own "tenant isolation" RLS policy narrows the inner-join embed to THIS company's own tender_packs only, not every company's. One company's own count of distinct tenders it has ever created a pack for is the same bounded shape `held_registrations`/`company_principals` already are - realistically nowhere near 1000 for a single company at this product's current or near-term scale. Left unchanged.
- `app/tenders/[id]/pack-inputs-actions.ts`'s `person_role_eligibility` read (no explicit filter) - RLS-scoped to the caller's own company via `people.company_id`; a company's own role-eligibility tag count is bounded by its own people count x a handful of tags, the same shape as `company_principals`. Left unchanged.
- `scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`'s `runClarificationWindow()` reads `tender_tasks` filtered to `kind = "clarification"` - also cross-tenant (service role, summed across every company), the same STRUCTURAL shape as the 5 findings above, but `tender_tasks` of this one kind are created one at a time by a human adding a manual clarification task, not auto-generated per tender/company the way a `tender_pack` or a discovered tender is - a far slower, much less certain growth rate. Judged lower-priority and left unfixed this pass, flagged here explicitly for a future pass to re-check once this task kind's real row count is known (not re-derived from scratch).
- `lib/documentExpiry.ts`/`lib/complianceDigestCandidates.ts` (`held_registrations`/`people`/`registration_types`) - all RLS- or `.eq("company_id", ...)`-scoped to one company; confirmed (`app/company/registrations/actions.ts`) that editing an existing `held_registrations` row is a real `UPDATE ... WHERE id = ...`, not a new row - no history accumulation, same bounded shape as `company_principals`. Left unchanged.
- `app/people/actions.ts`'s `cv_uploads`/`generated_cvs`/`held_registrations` reads (all `.eq("person_id", id)`, used only for storage-path cleanup on delete) - bounded to ONE person's own upload history; `cv_uploads` is the one table confirmed to have no retention, but reaching 1000 rows for a single person's own re-uploads (as opposed to a whole company's, the shape `0160955` fixed) would need an implausibly large number of re-uploads by one individual. NEW path (`fetchAllRows()`-paginated): fetched all 1500, found **1** - correct, matching the real tender. Script and exact output are in this entry's own "to verify independently" section below, same as prior entries keep theirs reproducible.

**Part A: the systematic table-level check, done mechanically rather than by eyeballing migration files.** Replayed all 108 migrations into a fresh scratch Postgres (`service postgresql start`; `su postgres -c "bash engine/security/replay_schema.sh -U postgres -d scratch_sweep"`) and ran this directly against `pg_policies` - the exact, reproducible enumeration the directive asked for:

```sql
select distinct tablename from pg_policies
where schemaname='public' and permissive='PERMISSIVE'
  and (qual ilike '%is_company_member%' or with_check ilike '%is_company_member%')
  and tablename not in (
    select distinct tablename from pg_policies where schemaname='public' and permissive='RESTRICTIVE'
  )
order by 1;
```

(Confirmed first, directly against `pg_proc`, that `is_company_member`/`is_employee_in_company` are the only two functions any policy's `qual`/`with_check` ever calls for a company-membership check, and that no policy spells the same check out inline against `company_members` instead of calling the function - so this query is a complete enumeration, not a partial one keyed to one function name by luck.)

Result: exactly 3 tables - `savings_counted_steps`, `tender_documents`, `tender_requirements`. Each checked individually, not assumed clean:
- `savings_counted_steps`: already investigated by the 0118 pass and correctly left alone - it powers Home (`/dashboard`), one of an employee's two allowed pages. Re-confirmed, no change.
- `tender_documents`/`tender_requirements`: both LOOK like the same gap shape at first read (0045 added a bare `is_company_member(company_id)` branch to each, for a company's own private template-copy/requirement-override rows), and 0077's own Part D comment exempted both with reasoning that turns out to be imprecise ("already readable by authenticated users for EVERYONE... unaffected by any role"). But the actual policy text (not the comment) also requires `exists (select 1 from tenders t where t.id = ... and (t.owner_company_id is null or is_company_member(t.owner_company_id)))` - a plain, non-`security definer` subquery against `tenders`, which therefore runs under its OWN RLS, including `tenders`' own blanket "employee has no access" RESTRICTIVE policy (0077 Part C) that hides EVERY `tenders` row - shared or private - from anyone whose role is `employee` in ANY company. That `EXISTS` can never be true for an employee, so both tables transitively return zero rows regardless of their own `company_id`. Confirmed live, not reasoned from the text alone: seeded one company/owner/employee/tender(`owner_company_id` = that company)/`tender_packs`/one `tender_documents` row/one `tender_requirements` row (both `company_id` = that company). As the employee: `select ... from tenders where id = '<tender>'` -> 0 rows; `select ... from tender_documents where tender_id = ...` -> 0 rows; `select ... from tender_requirements where tender_id = ...` -> 0 rows; `select ... from tender_packs where tender_id = ...` -> 0 rows (already covered). As owner: all four return the real row, unaffected.

**This is itself the valuable, reportable result the directive asked for if the sweep came back clean**: the table-level RLS side of this bug class is now genuinely exhausted and mechanically re-checkable with the query above, not just "checked by eye one more time."

**Part B: checking real app-layer callers for those 3 candidates found a different, bigger problem.** Per the directive's own "check the real app-layer caller(s) to judge actual reachability" step, traced how an employee would actually reach `/tenders/[id]` (where `tender_documents`/`tender_requirements` are read) - `nav-items.ts`'s own `isNavItemActive()` treats `/tenders/*` as a drill-down FROM Home, and Home genuinely links into `/tenders/[id]` via its dispatch/command-center cards. `AppShell.tsx`'s `isEmployee` only swaps the nav list and the subscription banner - it never gates page content, so the full `/tenders/[id]` page (compliance report, pack review, pricing, tasks, documents) genuinely renders for an employee who follows that link, the same "nav hides it, nothing blocks the page" shape 0117/0118 already found for `/billing`/`/pipeline`/`/discovery`.

That line of checking surfaced a DIFFERENT, more serious class of the same underlying problem: several `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs re-implement a read/write 0077/0117/0118's own RESTRICTIVE policies already cover on the underlying table, checking only `is_company_member(...)`, never role - and because they are `SECURITY DEFINER` they bypass ALL table RLS, restrictive policies included. This is exactly the risk `0117`'s own header already named for `start_payfast_checkout()` ("a SELECT-side RESTRICTIVE policy does nothing to stop a SECURITY DEFINER function's own blind write") - it was just never swept for siblings until this pass. Checked every `SECURITY DEFINER` function this app's own `supabase.rpc(...)` calls name (grepped across `app/`), cross-referenced against every table 0077/0117/0118 made RESTRICTIVE-only for `employee`, for a role check inside the function body. Found 12 with none at all, and reproduced every single one individually as the employee role in a disposable scratch database (never the real DB) - not batched, not assumed from reading the code alone:

1. **`bank_account_summaries(p_company)`** - `bank_accounts`' own RESTRICTIVE policy (0077) exists specifically because 0077's header lists "bank details" by name as off-limits to `employee`. RED: as the employee, returned the real row (`bank_name` 'FNB', `account_holder` 'Test Co (Pty) Ltd', `last4` '7890').
2. **`company_member_labels()`** - `company_members`' own RESTRICTIVE policy (0117) already narrows a plain table read to the caller's own row, specifically because 0117 found an employee could otherwise read every teammate's row. This function bypasses that fix entirely, called unconditionally from `app/tenders/[id]/activity-log.tsx` and `tender-updates.tsx` (both on the employee-reachable tender page). RED: as the employee, returned BOTH company_members rows with their real emails.
3. **`tender_document_uploads(p_tender_id)`** - re-implements the same doc-upload-metadata read Part A proved is transitively blocked for a direct table read, but as its own join with no RLS and no role check. RED: as the employee, returned the real row for the company's own tender.
4. **`pursue_discovered_opportunity(p_opportunity_id)`** - "prepare this tender" (`app/discovery/actions.ts`). RED: as the employee, succeeded and created a real `tenders` row, a real `tender_packs` row for the whole company (now in the shared Bid Pipeline board for every member) and queued a real `extract_requirements` engine job - confirmed by a superuser read of all three tables after the call.
5. **`load_manual_tender(...)`** - "load a tender manually" (`app/tenders/new/actions.ts`). Same shape as #4. RED: as the employee, succeeded, creating real `tenders`/`tender_packs`/engine-job rows.
6. **`add_manual_tender_documents(...)`** - adds documents to an existing manual tender and re-queues `extract_requirements`. RED: as the employee, succeeded.
7. **`request_submission_pack_checked(...)`** - the SANRAL submission-pack request RPC. `pack_generation_jobs`' own RESTRICTIVE policy (0077) says `employee` has no access, but this function inserts into it directly. RED: as the employee, succeeded, returning a real job id, consuming the company's trial pack quota.
8. **`request_general_job_checked(...)`** - sibling of #7 for the general (non-SANRAL) pack flow. RED: as the employee, succeeded.
9. **`set_opportunity_interest(...)`**/**10. `set_opportunity_tag(...)`** - RED: as the employee, both succeeded; superuser reads confirmed `interest_marker`/`company_tags` were genuinely changed for the whole company's `discovered_opportunities` row.
11. **`acknowledge_discovery_downgrade(...)`** - lower severity (a "mark as seen" flag) but same shape/table. Verified by error TYPE: pre-fix, the employee's call gets past every check into the function's own business logic (no role rejection anywhere); post-fix, the same call raises the new role-specific error FIRST, before that business check is ever reached.
12. **`accept_tender_update_date(...)`** - resolves "the company working on this tender" with no role filter, then writes the shared `tenders` row's `closing_date`/`briefing_date` and the company's own `tender_tasks`. RED: as the employee, succeeded - the closing date on file was genuinely changed.

**Fixed all 12** the same additive, narrow-only way 0117 already did for `start_payfast_checkout()`: one `is_employee_in_company(...)` guard added near the top of each function body (or folded into the SQL-language ones' own `WHERE` clause). For owner/admin/member, `is_employee_in_company()` is false, so every guard is unconditionally skipped and their behaviour is completely unchanged - verified individually for all 12, not assumed. Full reasoning, and which functions were checked and found NOT to need this (`create_company_invite_checked`/`remove_member_checked`/`set_member_role_checked` - already `tt_is_company_admin()`-gated; `set_my_daily_digest_opt_in` - writes only the caller's own row; `create_company_and_join` - no existing role to bypass; every `platform_admin_*` function; the `tt_*_check` trigger helpers, not client-callable), is in the new migration's own header comment (`app/supabase/migrations/0119_employee_rls_systematic_sweep.sql`).

**Confirmed genuinely red-then-green**, for real, not reused across runs: built a fresh scratch DB with all 108 migrations EXCEPT 0119 (RED) and a second fresh one with all 109 INCLUDING 0119 (GREEN), seeded identically. Ran all 12 as the employee against both - RED: all 12 succeeded/leaked data; GREEN: all 12 correctly refused with the new friendly error. Extended `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` with a new `[20]` section making all 12 (both directions - employee refused, owner unaffected) a permanent regression test rather than a one-off manual repro - ran the FULL suite (sections 1-20) against the post-0119 database: `ALL PASSED`. All scratch databases dropped after verification (`scratch_sweep`, `scratch_pre119`/`scratch_post119` and their rebuilds `b`-`f`) - nothing left behind.

**Why PR #176, not a direct push**: this review track's own guardrail says small, well-verified fixes push directly to `main`; anything larger or riskier opens a PR and stops for Sarel's go-ahead. 12 functions across discovery, manual-tender-load, billing/pack-quota and team-notification subsystems is bigger in scope than 0117/0118's single-table fixes, even though each individual guard is the same narrow, already-proven pattern - so this one waits for explicit review. ## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): fixed - the 'employee' role (0077) could still view and CHANGE the company's live billing plan through `start_payfast_checkout()`, a gap left by two tables/functions added after 0077's own employee-RLS sweep; plus a quick UTC-vs-SAST grep caught 2 more raw-UTC "today" derivations

Oriented from `c6f6ddd` (own prior pass: the deadline calculator's `today()` used UTC, not SAST). `git fetch`/`merge --ff-only` confirmed clean - still at `c6f6ddd`, no new commits, no collision. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub API: only `#164`/`#165` remain (both draft, both untouched since 2026-10-26) - not touched. Backlog cross-checked against the recent chain: 19 total, 3 genuinely open (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s own revenue-before-ITN gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap, `held_registrations`-vs-CV) - self-consistent, none acted on this pass (see below for why this pass's finding is a DIFFERENT bug in the same function, not that backlog item).

**Quick UTC-vs-SAST grep first**, per the directive: `grep -rn "toISOString().slice(0, 10)"` across `app/` (not exhaustive). Of 11 hits, most are either converting an already-known date (`lib/dates.ts`'s `closingDayOf()`, a fixed +2h offset applied to a GIVEN timestamp, not "now" - correct) or low-stakes cosmetic record timestamps (`people/actions.ts`'s provenance note text, `document-scan/actions.ts`'s `certified_id_on`) not worth this pass's time. Two were worth fixing, both feeding a date-COMPARISON, the exact shape called out:
- `scripts/send-returnables-digest.ts`'s `todayStr` fed straight into `businessDaysBetween()` to decide whether a tender is in the critical "3-5 business days from closing, mandatory returnable missing" window - the one-shot idempotency key (no date component) means a day miscounted near UTC midnight could miss the one real window entirely. The scheduled cron itself runs at a fixed 04:40 UTC (well outside the 22:00-00:00 UTC bug window), so this was latent against the real schedule, but reachable via `workflow_dispatch` manual runs or any future schedule change, and inconsistent with `send-founder-digest.ts`'s own already-correct `sastDateKey` right next to it conceptually. Fixed: `todayStr = sastToday()` (imported from `lib/publicHolidays.ts`, the same helper the prior pass added), replacing the raw `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)`.
- `app/api/billing/checkout/route.ts`'s `billing_date` field sent to PayFast on every real checkout - reachable any time of day a user clicks Subscribe, unlike the cron script above. Fixed the same way: `sastToday()` instead of raw UTC.

Both: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npx eslint` clean on both files, full regression `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/*.test.ts` (232/232) and `npx vitest run` (37 files/342 tests) unchanged and passing. No new test file - both are pure call-site swaps to an already-tested helper (`sastToday()`'s own red/green coverage is the prior pass's), matching this codebase's own convention that a standalone cron script/route handler isn't itself unit-tested here.

**Main focus, per the directive's own suggested angle**: read the actual `create policy` statements across all 48 migrations that define one, built a full table-by-table RLS inventory, and cross-checked it against 0077's own "employee role" sweep (Part C/D: 16+ company-scoped tables individually audited and given a RESTRICTIVE `is_employee_in_company()` policy, "Company-wide business data... is simply not what an employee role is for"). **Found exactly that**, in `company_subscriptions` (migration `0078`, three days after 0077's sweep) and `start_payfast_checkout()` (same migration, function body last replaced in `0083`): neither was ever covered by 0077's RESTRICTIVE policies, because neither existed yet when that sweep was written. `nav-items.ts`'s own `EMPLOYEE_NAV_ITEMS` comment states as fact that "RLS already blocks the data" for every page not in an employee's own two-item nav (Home, My CV) - true everywhere else, but not for Billing. ## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): fixed - `estimateSanralConventional()`'s management-points range silently approximated, not solved, once a tender had more than 6 key positions with no managerial flag on file - which is every real tender today

Oriented from `080334c` (own prior pass: `years_experience_at()`'s malformed-date gap). `git fetch`/`merge --ff-only` confirmed clean - still at `080334c`, no new commits, no collision. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub API: only `#164`/`#165` remain (both untouched since 2026-10-26). Backlog cross-checked against the recent chain: 19 total, 3 genuinely open (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap, `held_registrations`-vs-CV) - self-consistent, none touched this pass.

The last several passes have been on CV/pack-generation control-character and date-parsing bugs, discovery scrapers, and Server Action TOCTOU races - all repeatedly re-verified exhausted this session. Rotated to a genuinely different corner per the standing directive: grepped `System-Status.md`'s own route-folder mention counts and found `/toolkit` (3 mentions total, only one of its 4 calculators - the BEE preference-points table - ever actually audited; `b6-estimator` and `cidb-grade` never touched). Read `app/lib/sanralScoring.ts` and `app/lib/sanralMatrices.ts` end to end - the real SANRAL Conventional functionality-score estimator, used both by the public/`/toolkit` B6 calculator AND, for real, by `app/tenders/[id]/compliance-data.ts` to compute the live compliance report's own "clears/cannot-clear/depends" outlook for an actual tender. Confirmed via `node --experimental-strip-types -e` that every `PROJECT_TYPE_MATRICES`/`TECH_POSITION_ROWS`/`MAN_POSITION_ROWS` data table has the right row/column lengths and correct on-diagonal 5s (no transcription-length bug) before looking at the scoring logic itself - genuinely clean there.

**Found, in the scoring logic itself**: `estimateSanralConventional()`'s management-points range handles a position whose `managerial` flag isn't on file (unknown) by scoring it both ways and reporting the spread, since reading a position as managerial changes its own denominator (15 -> 30) as well as its points. For <=6 such ambiguous positions on one tender it brute-forced all `2^n` combinations - correct. Above 6, it silently fell back to trying only 2 scenarios: every ambiguous position managerial, or none of them (`const scenarios = unknownIdx.length <= 6 ? 1 << unknownIdx.length : 2`). That is not a sample of the true range: because reading a position as managerial always adds points to the numerator but ALSO always costs exactly +15 on the denominator regardless of which position it is, a position with a low/zero managerial-position-held score should stay non-managerial even while OTHER positions are worth flipping - the true worst/best case is generally a MIXED combination, which "all true" and "all false" can both miss entirely.

This is reachable on every real tender today, not a contrived edge case: `compliance-data.ts`'s own comment states positions come from `tender_pack_assignments` because `tender_requirements` "isn't seeded by anything yet" - and `tender_pack_assignments` has no `managerial` column at all, so `managerial: p.req ? p.req.managerial : null` is `null` for every single position, on every tender, right now. Book 1's own SETUP sheet has up to 10 non-alternate key-person slots (`docs/specs/SANRAL-Tender-Automation-Specification.md`, positions 11/12 are the alternates), several of which (PL/CE/RE/RM, repeated across a multi-section contract) are manager-eligible at once - more than 6 is a realistic shape for a larger Conventional tender, not a hypothetical.

**Reproduced for real** with a disposable Node script (`npx vite-node`, since this module - like several `app/lib/*.ts` files - resolves fine under Next.js/vitest's bundler resolution but needs explicit import extensions to run standalone): built 7 manager-eligible positions (one of each MAN_POSITION_COLUMNS code) where 3 have a strong managerial-position-held score and 4 have zero. The pre-fix code reported `management: { min: 3.6, max: 5 }`. An independent brute-force oracle over the true `2^7 = 128` combinations found the true range is `{ min: 3.2, max: 5 }`, achieved at mask `CE:true, RM:true, CE(T):true` (a genuine mix) - not at all-true or all-false, the only two the old code ever tried. The displayed range understated how low the true worst case goes by 0.4 points (12% of the 0-15 management band) - directly undermining the report's own "Clears the threshold even at the bottom of every unknown range" outlook line, which depends on this exact number.

**Fixed** by replacing the `2^n`/2-scenario code with an exact O(n log n) solve: since every ambiguous position's denominator delta is the same constant (+15) regardless of which position, for any fixed count `k` of positions chosen managerial, the extreme numerator for that `k` is always the `k` positions with the largest (for max) or smallest (for min) own managerial-vs-non swing - sorting once and scanning every `k` from 0..n finds the true global extreme for any n, not just n<=6. Verified the derivation is exact, not just "better", with a randomized differential test (500 trials, n<=6, comparing the new code against the OLD code's own exhaustive brute force byte-for-byte, after first fixing a flawed rounded-vs-unrounded comparison in the test harness itself) - zero mismatches - and separately re-ran the real n=7 counter-example and the 128-combination oracle: new code now reports `{ min: 3.2, max: 5 }`, matching exactly.

While reproducing this, also found `sanralScoring.ts` has never had a test file, in either this repo's `.test.ts` (plain `node --experimental-strip-types --test`) or `.spec.ts` (vitest) convention - and traced why: its own import of `./sanralMatrices` (no `.ts` extension) cannot resolve under the plain node runner at all (confirmed: adding a `.test.ts` file for it breaks the whole `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/*.test.ts` glob with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`), unlike every other module this convention covers (`tenderCompliance.ts`, `personCredentials.ts`, etc.), which already import their own local deps with the explicit extension `vitest.config.ts`'s own comment documents as the reason `.test.ts` exists as a separate convention from `.spec.ts`. Fixed that one-line import to `./sanralMatrices.ts` so a real test file can actually run here, matching the rest of the codebase - this had silently kept this scoring engine, the one genuinely live-tender-affecting piece of `/toolkit`, outside both test conventions since it was written.

Added `app/lib/sanralScoring.test.ts` (new file): the n=7 counter-example asserting against the independent brute-force oracle, an n<=6 case re-checked against the same oracle (guards the previously-correct path), a sanity check that a position with a known managerial flag is never treated as ambiguous, and a `pastPerformanceFromExperience()` best-3-of-N check (that function read clean on inspection but had no coverage either). Confirmed genuinely red-then-green: reverted only the algorithmic change (kept the import-extension fix, otherwise the file can't load at all) and re-ran - the n=7 test failed (`3.6` reported vs `3.2` expected), the other 3 passed; restored the fix - all 4 pass. Full regression: `node --experimental-strip-types --test app/lib/*.test.ts` - 230/230 (226 prior + 4 new), 0 failures. `npx vitest run` - 37 files / 342 tests, all passing (confirms the extensionless-import fix didn't disturb anything using `sanralMatrices.ts` via the vitest/bundler resolution path, e.g. `tenderRoles.ts`). `npx tsc --noEmit` on the full `app/` project - 0 errors. `npx eslint "app/lib/sanralScoring.ts" "app/lib/sanralScoring.test.ts"` - clean, no findings.

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** - standalone bug, fixed; not a new judgment-call item. `held_registrations`-vs-CV, `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue gap, and the impersonation session-refresh gap all untouched, as directed.

## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): fixed - `requestSubmissionPack()`'s per-tender "already queued" race leaks a raw Postgres constraint-violation string instead of the friendly message the non-race path already shows

Oriented from `13bdfc2` (own prior pass: `generate_cv.py`'s own `_footer()` was the one genuine gap left in the control-character-guard bug class, now exhausted). `git fetch`/`merge --ff-only` confirmed clean - still at `13bdfc2`, no new commits, no collision. Open PRs re-checked: only `#164`/`#165` remain (both untouched since 2026-10-26). Backlog cross-checked against the recent chain: 19 total, 3 genuinely open (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap, `held_registrations`-vs-CV) - self-consistent, none touched this pass.

With the control-character bug class now closed and the discovery-scraper live-test rotation's next candidates (`lephalale.py`/`vaal_central_water.py`/`capetown_procurement.py`/`kouga.py`) still queued for a future pass, re-examined this session's own just-fixed TOCTOU-race family (0113/0114/0115/0116) for a sibling instance, rather than assuming it's now exhausted everywhere a check-then-insert shape appears. Found one in `app/tenders/[id]/actions.ts`'s `requestSubmissionPack()`: a plain `SELECT ... from pack_generation_jobs where tender_id = ... and status in ('requested','generating') limit 1` (line ~155) gates a friendly "A submission pack is already queued for this tender." rejection, well before the function's one real write - the `request_submission_pack_checked()` RPC (0115) - runs. 0115 already locks `company_subscriptions` for the company-wide quota check, but that lock (and that function) says nothing about a second request for the exact same tender; the only thing stopping a true duplicate is `pack_generation_jobs_one_open_key` (0026), a unique index on `(company_id, tender_id, engine, kind) where status in ('requested','generating')` - and `request_submission_pack_checked()`'s insert has no `on conflict`/exception handling around it, unlike its sibling `request_general_job_checked()` in the same migration (which deliberately uses `on conflict do nothing`).

So the race window is real: two requests for the SAME tender close enough together (a double-click, two tabs, a slow-network retry) can both pass the plain SELECT before either's RPC call commits - the first's insert succeeds, the second's hits the unique index and raises a raw `23505`, which `requestSubmissionPack()`'s own error handling (`fail(error.message || "Could not request...")`) would show to the user verbatim - the exact "raw constraint-violation string leaks to the user instead of the friendly message the happy path already has" shape `redeem_company_invite()` was fixed for in `0116`, just one call site over.

Reproduced directly in a disposable scratch database (`engine/security/replay_schema.sh`, `postgresql` service started first since this is a fresh container): one company (active, 5 packs/month - comfortably under quota, isolating this from 0115's own already-fixed quota race), one tender, one `tender_packs` row. Called `request_submission_pack_checked()` for that tender twice in direct succession (sequential calls are enough to prove this - the race lives in the TypeScript-side window between the SELECT and the RPC call, not inside the RPC's own locking, which was never meant to cover this check). First call: succeeded, returned a job id. Second call, same tender: raised `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "pack_generation_jobs_one_open_key"` with the real company/tender UUIDs in `DETAIL` - confirmed the exact raw string that would otherwise reach the user.

Fixed the same way `requestTenderCv()` already handles the identical shape for `generated_cvs` (0075) in this exact same file - no migration needed, since the unique index (0026) already fully prevents the actual duplicate row; only the error message needed fixing. Added `if (error.code === "23505")` before the generic `error.message` fallback in `requestSubmissionPack()`'s own error handling, mapping it to the same friendly message the plain-SELECT happy path already shows ("A submission pack is already queued for this tender.").

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` on the full `app/` project - `0` errors. `npx eslint "app/tenders/[id]/actions.ts"` - clean, no new findings. Re-ran the same two-calls-same-tender scratch-DB scenario mentally against the new code path (the fix is pure TypeScript error-mapping, not a SQL change, so the scratch-DB repro above - proving the RPC really does raise `23505` on this exact race - is the correct and sufficient verification; no separate red-then-green test file exists for this, matching this codebase's own convention that Server Actions calling Supabase directly aren't unit-tested here - `requestTenderCv()`'s own identical 23505 catch two lines above has none either).

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** - standalone bug, fixed; not a new judgment-call item. `held_registrations`-vs-CV, `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue gap, and the impersonation session-refresh gap all untouched, as directed.

Both had `closing_date: None` - traced why rather than assuming it was a transient scrape miss. `normalize()` has never set `closing_date` at all (confirmed via `git log` on the file: the original "Add 3 new discovery sources" commit never included it, and nothing since has either) - only `published_date` is extracted. Checked the real live page's raw HTML directly rather than assuming the source genuinely has no closing date to give: it does - a separate "Published Tenders" detail section (distinct from the dated `<ul>` "What's New" summary list `parse_listing()` already reads) states `Closing Date: DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM` for each tender, right next to its title (confirmed live: `RFP14/2026` -> `17/11/2026 11:00`, `RFP18/2026` -> `10/11/2026 11:00`). Every SARS tender this source has ever discovered has been missing its real closing date entirely - no deadline countdown, no "closing soon" flag, nothing.

Fixed by adding `_closing_dates_by_ref()`, keying each detail block's stated closing date by its parsed RFP reference, and attaching it in `parse_listing()`/`normalize()`. Deliberately NOT routed through `source_http.parse_sast()`'s own ambiguous US-style (month-first) slash-date branch - SARS's format is day-first, and a day/month both <=12 (a real, common case) would silently transpose under that reading; the day/month/year are parsed explicitly and handed to `sh.iso_sast()` only as an unambiguous ISO string instead.

Caught and fixed a real bug in my own first version of the fix before it reached main: the first regex used an unbounded `.*?` between `<strong>title</strong>` and `Closing Date:`, which crossed over unrelated `<strong>` tags earlier on the page (the "What's New" summary list's own date headings) and attached the wrong date - caught by my own new test (deliberately ordered the fixture's summary section before its detail section, the opposite of the real page's own order, specifically to catch this), not by luck matching the live page's current ordering. Fixed with a `(?:(?!<strong>).)*?` bound that refuses to cross into another `<strong>` block.

Verified for real: re-ran against the real live site after the fix - `RFP14/2026` -> `2026-11-17T11:00:00+02:00`, `RFP18/2026` -> `2026-11-10T11:00:00+02:00`, matching the page exactly. Added 2 new assertions to `test_gov_sources.py` (closing-date extraction with the day/month-both-<=12 safety case spelled out explicitly; a tender with no stated closing date still parses to `None`, not a crash) - full suite `ALL PASSED`. `ast.parse` clean; `ruff check` - all findings pre-existing or matching the file's own existing `re.S` convention (`DATE_BLOCK` above already uses the identical style), none newly introduced.

portal` tender closing in 20 hours, not yet dispatched) - `classifyDispatchBucket()` correctly

## This pass (2026-11-04, standing solution-architect review): fixed - `create_company_and_join()` had an unguarded TOCTOU race that could give one user two companies, which every single page in the app assumes can't happen

Oriented from `6e08b0c` (own prior pass: Market Intelligence's bidder-count gate). `git fetch`/`merge
--ff-only` picked up `4303fb9` (a sibling pass: the claim-outside-try-block isolation gap swept across
all four remaining bridges) - no collision, no duplication. Open PRs re-checked: only `#164`/`#165`
remain (both untouched since 2026-10-26).

Cross-checked the backlog chain and the corrected "10 pending migrations" figure again (now a standing
discipline): self-consistent, 19 unchanged, `ls app/supabase/migrations/ | grep -E
"^(0096|0107|0108|0109|0110|0111|0112|0113|0114|0115)_"` still returns 10.

Directed to the onboarding flow or notifications/digest. Read `app/app/onboarding/` end to end
(`page.tsx`, `actions.ts`, `Step1.tsx`, `AddDocumentsScreen.tsx`, `WizardShell.tsx`, `fields.tsx`) -
the 2026-10-31 clean sweep of this area still holds, nothing new in the UI layer itself. Pivoted to the
one privileged write it depends on, `create_company_and_join()` (0003), since that function's own
read/write shape had never specifically been checked for the TOCTOU pattern this session has now found
three times elsewhere (`createInvite`'s seat cap, `team/actions.ts`'s last-owner check,
`company_can_request_pack()`'s quota).

**Found**: `create_company_and_join()` checks "does this user already belong to a company" (`exists
(select 1 from company_members where user_id = auth.uid())`) and inserts the new `company_members` row
as two steps in the same function, with nothing locking between them. `company_members` has no unique
constraint on `user_id` alone (only the composite `unique(company_id, user_id)` from `0001`), so two
concurrent calls for the SAME new user (a double-click on Screen 1's "Continue" button, or a slow-
network retry) can both pass the check before either commits, both insert - one user ends up owning TWO
real companies. This is worse than the other three races: grepped every page that reads a user's own
company (`AppShell.tsx`, `/billing`, `/experience`, `/my-cv`, `/onboarding` itself,
`company/officeActions.ts`) and all seven call `.eq("user_id", ...).maybeSingle()` - PostgREST's
`.maybeSingle()` errors the moment more than one row matches, so a user caught by this race gets a hard
error on every single page in the app from then on, not just onboarding.

**Reproduced directly** in a disposable scratch database (never the live DB): one real `auth.users`
row, two concurrent `create_company_and_join()` calls for that same user - both succeeded, returning two
different company ids; `select count(*) from company_members where user_id = ...` confirmed 2 rows, both
`role = 'owner'`.

**Fixed** with migration `0116`: `alter table company_members add constraint
company_members_user_id_key unique (user_id)`. Not a SECURITY DEFINER + `for update` rewrite like
0113/0114/0115 - there's no pre-existing row to lock on for a brand-new user, and the table's own 0001
comment already states "v1 has one company" per the product while every read site above already
hard-assumes it, so this formalizes an invariant the whole app already depends on rather than
introducing a new one. A concurrent second insert now blocks on the unique index until the first
commits, then fails with a 23505 instead of succeeding; because the whole function runs in one
transaction, the losing call's own `companies` insert rolls back too - no orphaned, member-less company
row left behind.

While adding the constraint, found the exact same "join a second company" path already existed, un-
raced, in `redeem_company_invite()` (0107): a user already in company A accepting an invite to company
B previously succeeded silently as a second `company_members` row - already a live landmine against the
same universal `.maybeSingle()` assumption, just reached a different way. The new constraint alone would
have turned that into a raw `duplicate key value violates unique constraint` string leaking straight to
`app/invite/actions.ts`'s `acceptInvite()`, which redirects with `error.message` shown as-is - so
`0116` also re-creates `redeem_company_invite()` with one added check before the insert, raising a
friendly, specific message instead. Redeeming an invite for the SAME company (re-opening an old link, a
role change) is unaffected - still the existing on-conflict-update-role path, unchanged.

**Verified for real**: replayed all 106 migrations (including `0116`) on a fresh scratch database -
clean. Re-ran the identical two-concurrent-calls scenario against the fix: first call succeeds, second
blocks on the lock then fails with the unique-constraint error, exactly 1 `company_members` row results,
and the loser's own `companies` row count for that test confirmed 0 (no orphan). Separately tested
`redeem_company_invite()`'s new guard directly: a user already owning company A, invited to company B,
gets the friendly "You already belong to a different company..." message (not a raw constraint string);
re-tested the SAME-company re-redemption path (re-opening an old invite link) immediately after and
confirmed it still works unchanged - role updated via the existing `on conflict` clause. No TypeScript
changed - both `createCompanyBasics()` and `acceptInvite()` already handle any RPC error generically, so
no app-code change was needed either side. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (sanity check only, nothing touched).
Full regression `node --experimental-strip-types --test app/lib/*.test.ts` - 222/222, unaffected (as
expected, no TS touched). Three scratch databases created and dropped immediately after each check,
never the live DB.

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** (standalone bug, fixed - not a new judgment-call item; 11 pending migrations
now `0096`/`0107`-`0116`, the `held_registrations`-vs-CV judgment call, the `start_payfast_checkout()`
revenue-integrity gap, and the impersonation session-refresh gap all still open, needing Sarel's own
call. None of those three touched this pass, as directed.)
