well-defended (per-document isolation in `fetch_releases()`, defensive `.get()` throughout
`normalize()`); no finding, nothing to log. Moved to `boq_extraction.py` (the deterministic BOQ/priced-
schedule line-item parser reused by `gov_sources.py`'s scope-enrichment chain) and read it in full.

**Found and fixed Finding 129 (CONFIRMED, moderate)**: `_SKIP_ROW_RE`'s `total`/`sub total`/`grand total`
branches were a bare prefix match against the row's cleaned description, with no end anchor. A genuine,
numbered line item whose description happens to start with the word "Total" - ordinary civil-
engineering BOQ phrasing, e.g. `"Total length of guardrail to be supplied and installed"` (unit `m`, qty
`850`, rate `320`, amount `272000`) - matched the same prefix as a bare `"Sub Total"` row and was
silently skipped in `extract_items_from_grid()`, with no trace anywhere in the result. Confirmed live:
`boq._SKIP_ROW_RE.match("Total length of guardrail to be supplied and installed")` → `True`. This is the
inverse of the module's own stated "we stop, we never guess" discipline (which guards against
*fabricating* an item) - here a real, correctly-priced item was *dropped*, understating scope for
whoever reads `tender_scope_records.boq_summary` next.

**Fix:** tightened only the `total`/`sub total`/`grand total` branches to require the rest of the
description (after the matched keyword) be nothing but trailing punctuation/currency marker and then
end-of-string - matching how a real subtotal row's own description cell actually looks. Left `vat`/
`page N`/`carried forward`/`brought down`/`c/f`/`b/f`/`notes` as prefix matches, unchanged - none of
those is a plausible first words of a real line-item description, so there's no equivalent risk to fix
there.

**Verified red-then-green.** New test
`test_real_item_description_starting_with_the_word_total_is_not_dropped_as_a_subtotal_row()` in
`engine/discovery/test_boq_extraction.py` - asserts two real "Total ..." items are kept AND a genuine
bare "Sub Total" row in the same sheet is still correctly excluded. Reverted `boq_extraction.py` alone:
failed exactly as predicted (both real items came back `[]`); restored: `0 failure(s)` across all 14
tests in the file. `py_compile` clean on both touched files. Regression: re-ran `test_list_tenders.py`
and imported `transnet_etenders.py` cleanly - both unaffected.

Backlog: unchanged at 18 items - this is a contained parsing fix, not one of Sarel's own 18 numbered
backlog items.

## This pass (2026-11-04, standing QA/robustness review): fix - a CANCELLED notification workflow run never recorded a heartbeat "finish" at all, across all 10 notification-sending workflows

Oriented from `3e56a7b`; `git fetch origin main` found one new sibling commit since my own last push
(`88c4b42`, a real fix - `company_can_request_pack()`'s own TOCTOU race closed, plus a not-yet-live
quota-counting regression) - no overlap with `.github/workflows/` or `engine/notify/`. Fast-forwarded
cleanly. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub API: `#164`/`#165` only, both unchanged, no collision.

Rotated to notify (compliance/reminders was last). `send_digest_emails.py`/`daily_digest.py` have had
several dedicated passes this session (Finding 122, two cycles ago) - picked
`engine/notify/record_heartbeat.py` and its real callers instead: the 10 notification-sending GitHub
Actions workflows (`.github/workflows/*.yml`), never reviewed this session. The module's own docstring
claims "9 notification-sending workflows" - counted directly (`grep -l "record_heartbeat.py start"`):
10, a separate, minor, pre-existing drift, corrected while already in this exact context.

**Found and fixed Finding 127 (CONFIRMED, moderate)**: each of the 10 workflows' own heartbeat
"finish" step uses two separate steps (`if: success()`, `if: failure()`) with its own comment
correctly explaining why (no single mid-job "did it pass" value in GitHub Actions) - but `failure()`
alone misses a THIRD, SEPARATE GitHub Actions job-conclusion state: a CANCELLED run (a
concurrency-group supersede, a manual cancel, GitHub's own workflow timeout). Confirmed this exact
distinction was already independently discovered and correctly handled ELSEWHERE in this same repo
(`bridge-worker-ci.yml`, 2026-10-19, its own `!cancelled()` steps) - just never carried over to these
10 heartbeat conditions. A cancelled run of any of these 10 workflows never ran EITHER finish step,
leaving its heartbeat's own "start" row stuck showing "running" until the admin UI's own staleness
check eventually (and only generically) flags it, rather than being correctly and immediately reported
as cancelled the moment GitHub itself already knew exactly what happened.

Fixed by changing the failure step's condition to `if: failure() || cancelled()` in all 10 workflows,
updating each one's own comment to explain the gap (mirroring the reasoning already proven correct in
`bridge-worker-ci.yml`), and rewording each failure step's `--error` message to cover both causes.
Separately corrected `record_heartbeat.py`'s own docstring count from 9 to 10.

Verified: these are YAML workflow files, not Python under unit test, so verification was (1) `yaml.
safe_load()` on all 10 after editing - all valid; (2) confirming the new condition matches GitHub
Actions' own documented grammar and this repo's own already-proven `cancelled()` pattern exactly; (3)
re-running `test_record_heartbeat.py` after the docstring edit - `9 passed, 0 failed`, unaffected (no
logic change in the Python file itself). `py_compile` clean. Full write-up:
`docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` Finding 127.

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (small, fully verified, no live-DB access needed):
- 10 `.github/workflows/*.yml` files (listed in the findings doc entry)
- `engine/notify/record_heartbeat.py`
- `docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`

## This pass (2026-11-03, standing QA/robustness review): fix - a bridge subprocess failing to even START (not timing out, not exiting non-zero - the launch itself failing) silently aborted the whole worker cycle and reached no alert in --loop mode, the one mode the real container actually runs

Oriented from `cff9cd8`; `git fetch origin main` found two new sibling commits since my own last push
(`80550b9`, a real app/TS fix - the last hand-rolled filename sanitizer now uses the shared
`safeFileName()`; `a89c5b5`, a docs-only pass closing out a regex-ReDoS loose end with real timed
adversarial input) - neither touches `engine/worker/`, no overlap. Fast-forwarded cleanly. Open PRs
re-checked via the GitHub API: `#164`/`#165` only, both unchanged, no collision.

Rotated to worker/job-queue (notify was last). `run_bridges.py` read end to end - already carries
several hardening fixes (process-group timeout kill, missing-script re-check every cycle, `--script`
additive to the default set, per-bridge `system_alerts` source instead of a shared generic one).
Noticed `subprocess.Popen(...)` itself sits OUTSIDE both of the function's own two existing guards
(the `communicate(timeout=...)` try/except for a hang, the `p.returncode != 0` check for a bridge that
exits non-zero) - construct a real adversarial case rather than just reading: monkeypatched `Popen` to
raise `OSError("Cannot allocate memory")` on the first call, simulating a real, reachable fork failure
under memory pressure (plausible on this exact container mid-soffice/LibreOffice work for a pack
bridge when a second bridge's turn comes up the same cycle).

**Found and fixed Finding 123 (CONFIRMED, severe)**: the raw `OSError` propagated straight out of
`run_once()` uncaught - the loop aborted entirely (the SECOND bridge was never even attempted that
cycle, confirmed: only 1 `Popen()` call recorded), and zero calls reached `system_alerts.record()` -
unlike every other failure shape in this same function. In `--once` mode the exception still reaches
the file's own `__main__` guard fallback (`system_alerts.record("worker", ...)`) - no real gap there.
But in `--loop` mode - the ONLY mode the real worker container runs, per this file's own docstring -
`poll_loop.poll_forever()`'s own generic per-cycle catch swallows it with only a `print()`, since
`run_bridges.py`'s own `poll_forever()` call never passes it an `alert_source`. A `Popen()`-level
failure (fork failure, a broken interpreter path, a permissions issue) was silently lost in
production: not in system_alerts, only in a container log nobody watches.

Fixed by wrapping the `Popen(...)` call itself in `try/except OSError`, treating it the same as every
other failure shape already handled here: `broken.append(...)` + `system_alerts.record(label, ...,
"critical")` under that bridge's own source, then `continue` to the next bridge rather than aborting
the whole cycle. Deliberately did NOT also add a blanket `alert_source` to the `poll_forever()` call in
`main()` - that would double-alert on the ordinary, already-well-handled `RuntimeError` path (every
per-bridge timeout/non-zero-exit already gets its own, more specific alert) to guard a now-much-
narrower residual gap, not a clean improvement.

Verified red-then-green: added `test_a_bridge_that_fails_to_even_start_is_reported_not_silently_lost()`
to `test_poll_loop.py`, same real-subprocess style as its existing timeout test - confirms the SECOND
bridge still runs (no whole-cycle abort) and exactly one `critical` alert is recorded under the failing
bridge's own label. Ran the full suite (every real end-to-end bridge-loop smoke test) - all pass.
Reverting reproduced the exact predicted raw `OSError` escaping uncaught; restored, all green.
`py_compile`/`ast.parse` clean. Full write-up: `docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` Finding 123.

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (small, fully verified, no live-DB access needed):
- `engine/worker/run_bridges.py`
- `engine/worker/test_poll_loop.py`
- `docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`

**Found (already known) and fixed Finding 116**: confirmed the code shape really is byte-for-byte the
same race - `process_upload()` POSTs `cv_extraction_results` then PATCHes `cv_uploads` to `extracted`
in two separate, non-transactional calls; a worker killed in that gap left the row stuck `extracting`,
wrongly marked `extraction_failed` by the stale-reclaim sweep even though its result was already

onboarding precedent): `people/[id]/page.tsx` queries the two tables independently, and
`applyCvExtraction` never touches the upload row's own status - so a raced CV upload would show as
both "pending review" and "extraction_failed" at once, permanently.

heal to `extracted` with a `"warning"` alert instead of `"error"` if one exists. A genuinely dead row
is unaffected.

checked `engine/cv/test_process_cv_jobs.py` - clean; `py_compile` clean. Full write-up: `docs/specs/
QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` Finding 116.

`process_pack_jobs.py`/`process_general_jobs.py`/`process_narrative_jobs.py` all mark their own job

cycles ago (run 141) - re-checked several angles from scratch instead of re-reading the same
conclusion: the `SetupError`-aborts-the-batch design (confirmed intentional, matches `extract_cv_
fields.py`'s own canonical pattern exactly, including the `run()`-level non-zero-exit handling), all 6
registered bridges present and CI-wired (no orphaned 7th queue consumer), the worker Dockerfile/
requirements.txt's dependency chain traced end to end (no missing package for any bridge's real
import chain), and `scoutAnomalyIdempotencyKey`'s re-notification-on-new-occurrences design (correctly
mirrors `check_system_alerts.py`'s own "still occurring" rule, so a persistent critical bridge failure
does keep reaching Sarel via Scout even with the older Gmail check-in now disabled). None of these
turned up anything new.

**Found and fixed Finding 114 (CONFIRMED, moderate)**: `process_onboarding_jobs.py`'s `process_upload()`
does its real work in two separate, non-transactional REST calls - POST the classification result,
THEN PATCH the upload to `status: "classified"`. A worker killed in that exact gap (a crash, an OOM
kill, an ungraceful redeploy) left the upload stuck `"classifying"`, which `fail_stale_uploads()` then
marked `"classification_failed"` ("Upload this file again") - even though the result was already
written and fully reviewable. Traced the real UI consequence (`document-scan/page.tsx`): the "To
review" and "couldn't be read" lists query independently with no cross-check, so the same document
showed in BOTH, permanently - reviewing/applying the result never touches the upload row's own status,
so nothing ever clears the stale "failed" entry.

Fixed by having `fail_stale_uploads()` check for an existing result before declaring a row failed; if
one exists, self-heal the upload to `"classified"` instead (a `"warning"` alert, not `"error"` - a
recovery, not a loss). A genuinely dead row with no result is still marked failed exactly as before.

**Found and fixed Finding 113 (CONFIRMED, severe)**: `listing_change_signals()` items (cancellations,
closing-date moves, new addenda, migration 0051) carry both `"title"` (the tender's own title, already
shown in every other section of the same email) and `"summary"` (the actual change - "Closing date

by grep - `tender_updates` items carry an unrelated `"summary"` key too but never `"change_type"`, so
they're correctly untouched, verified with a negative control): `bit = f"{bit}: {item['summary']}"`
when both are present.

`engine/notify/test_send_digest_emails.py` (3 checks); reverting reproduced the exact predicted 2
failures with every other check (including every pre-existing `send_one()`/`main()` check) still
green; restored, `0 failure(s)`. Regression-checked `engine/notify/test_digest_live.py`,
`test_digest_opt_in.py` - all pass. Full write-up: `docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` Finding 113.

## This pass (2026-11-01, standing QA/robustness review): fix - requirements.py's read_document() silently treated an unreadable document as a successfully-read empty one whenever its saved file had no recognized extension

Oriented from `286ca54`; `git fetch origin main` found nothing new since - local already matched
`origin/main` exactly. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub API: only `#164`/`#165` remain, both
unchanged, no collision.

Rotation: intake. `engine/intake/classify_tender.py` and `scenario_driver.py` were already swept
clean earlier this window; `engine/intake/test_manual_intake.py` is a DB-backed e2e harness (needs
`INTAKE_PSQL` + a scratch Postgres, not runnable here), so followed the real production code path it
exercises instead - `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`'s `run_extraction()` and the
`engine/general/requirements.py` manifest it builds from.

**Found and fixed Finding 112 (CONFIRMED, moderate)**: `requirements.py`'s `read_document()` only had
dispatch branches for `pdf`/`docx`/`doc`/`txt` formats; any OTHER format (collect_documents() derives
`format` purely from the saved file's own extension) fell through all of them with `text` left at
`""` and `doc["unreadable"]` never set at all - silently indistinguishable from a genuinely-empty-but-
successfully-read document. Confirmed reachable two ways: (1) `process_general_jobs.
download_tender_documents()`'s own fallback-`.pdf` heuristic only fires when there's no dot anywhere
in a title's last 6 characters, so a real buyer title like `"SBD Forms Part A.1"` keeps `.1` as its
saved "extension" (format `"1"`); (2) a scanned notice uploaded directly as a raw `.jpg`/`.png` (not
wrapped in `.pdf`) hits the same gap. `chars == 0` correctly excludes it from `readable`, but
`unreadable_documents` (filtered on `d["unreadable"]` truthy) silently omits it too, and the loud-
failure message's own fallback shows a generic "no text found" instead of the real reason - the exact
"silent wrong answer, not an empty one" shape `run_extraction()`'s own module comment already warns
against, one dispatch level further in than that comment's guard reaches.

Fixed with an explicit `else` branch: any unrecognized format now sets `doc["unreadable"] = f"not a
format this can read ({fmt or 'no file extension'}) - re-upload it as a PDF or Word document"`.
Left `download_tender_documents()`'s extension-guessing heuristic as-is (separate, more speculative
work - guessing a buyer's real intended extension from a title is not a contained fix); this fix
alone closes the actual defect.

Verified red-then-green: added `check_unrecognized_format_is_flagged_not_silently_blank()` to
`engine/general/test_requirements.py` (6 checks - the trailing-`.1` title and a raw `.jpg`, both via
`read_document()` directly and via the full `extract_requirements()` manifest); reverting reproduced
the exact predicted 3 failures with every other check (including both premise checks and all pre-
existing checks in the file) still green; restored, `0 failure(s)`. Regression-checked
`engine/general/test_requirements_manifest_v2.py`, `test_submission_plan.py`, `test_fill_sbd_docx.py`
- all pass. Full finding write-up: `docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` Finding 112.

## This pass (2026-11-01, standing solution-architect review): fix - sars_procurement.py's TENDER_LINK regex required href as the literal first attribute, which real-world CMS output elsewhere on the same site already contradicts

Oriented from `5c31f97`; `git fetch origin main` found nothing new since - local already matched
`origin/main` exactly. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub API: only `#164`/`#165` remain, both
unchanged, no collision.

Continuing this session's technique of testing a regex/parser directly against real-world input
rather than reading it by eye: picked `engine/discovery/sars_procurement.py` (SARS's own Published
Tenders page, 168 lines, thin existing test coverage - one shared fixture in `test_gov_sources.py`,
not its own dedicated file). Fetched the REAL live SARS listing page and two of its real detail
pages directly (network access confirmed working in this environment) rather than trusting the
regexes by eye or against a synthetic fixture alone.

**Found and fixed a real structural fragility, confirmed against the live site itself, not just a
constructed example**: `TENDER_LINK` was `r'<a href="([^"]+/tender/[^"]+)"[^>]*>...'` - requiring
`href` to be the literal FIRST attribute right after `<a `, with zero tolerance for another
attribute (`class`, `target`) appearing first. Confirmed empirically that every `<a>` tag on the
real, live tender listing page happens to have `href` first today (6/6 occurrences), so nothing is
silently dropped right now - but a direct count of `<a>` tags on the real live detail pages for
this exact site shows 15 instances per page where SARS's own CMS already puts another attribute
BEFORE href on other links (nav/social). A single theme update that did the same for a tender link
would silently drop that tender from discovery with no error at all - the identical quiet-data-loss
shape this session has found and fixed repeatedly for other sources (DBSA's discarded real closing
time, SANRAL's wrong midnight default, the two notification-claim-too-early races). `DOC_LINK`
immediately below it in the same file already uses the correct, tolerant form
(`<a[^>]+href="..."`) - `TENDER_LINK` alone had the rigid one.

Fixed by widening `TENDER_LINK` to the same `<a[^>]+href="..."` form `DOC_LINK` already uses.
Re-tested against the real live listing page before and after the change - byte-identical match
results (6/6, same 3 unique URLs), confirming zero behavior change for every case that already
worked; added a constructed test case (an `<a target="_blank" href="...">` tender link) to
`test_gov_sources.py`'s existing `test_new_sources()` and confirmed it fails against the unfixed
regex (red) and passes with the fix (green).

Verification: `python3 engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py` -> `ALL PASSED` (97 checks, including
the new one); confirmed red (1 FAILED) against the unfixed source via `git stash`, green after
restoring the fix; `py_compile` clean on both touched files.

no live-DB access needed):

## This pass (2026-11-01, standing solution-architect review): fix - tender_enrichment.py's estimated-value regex silently missed single-digit amounts ("R5 million", "R8 billion"), falling back to "unknown" as if no value had been stated

Oriented from `3111741`; `git fetch origin main` found one new sibling commit (`2de368e`, a
QA/robustness pass's own clean sweep of `generate_cv.py`'s `build_world_bank()` - docs-only, no
overlap) and fast-forwarded cleanly. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub API: only `#164`/`#165`
remain, both unchanged, no collision.

With the LLM-call-quality, TOCTOU/row-lock, SECURITY DEFINER ownership-check and
`briefing_shortlisted` allow-list audits all exhausted, picked a module not yet read end to end this
session: `engine/discovery/tender_enrichment.py` (728 lines - the real caller of the recently-fixed
`scope_llm.py`, and the module that computes a tender's industry/discipline tags, scope summary,
pricing model, BOQ reference and estimated project value band). Read the whole file, then tested
`estimate_value_band()`'s own anchor regex directly rather than trusting it by eye.

**Found and fixed a real bug**: `_VALUE_ANCHOR_RE`'s amount group was `([0-9][0-9,.\s]{0,18}[0-9])` -
a mandatory LEADING digit AND a mandatory TRAILING digit, which needs at least 2 digit characters
even when the stated amount genuinely has only one. "The estimated contract value is R5 million" or
"Estimated value: R8 billion" - both real, plausible South African tender phrasings (a round
single-digit amount before a million/billion/bn/m/k suffix) - never matched the anchor regex at all,
so `estimate_value_band()` returned `(None, "unknown", None, "No stated contract/project value or
budget found...")` for a tender whose text plainly states one. This is exactly the class of defect
the module's own docstring is most alert to in the OTHER direction (never invent a value that wasn't
stated) - here a real, honestly-stated value was being silently treated as absent instead.

Reproduced directly first with a standalone regex test (`'The estimated contract value is R5
million.'` -> no match; `'The estimated contract value is R15 million.'` -> matches fine - only the
single-digit case fails). Fixed by making the amount group's "middle digits + trailing digit" part
optional: `([0-9](?:[0-9,.\s]{0,18}[0-9])?)` - a lone single digit (R5, R8, ...) now matches on its
own, while a real multi-digit/separator amount (`R500 000,00`) is completely unaffected (tested
side by side, same results as before for every existing case).

Added `test_value_band_single_digit_amount_still_matches()` to `test_tender_enrichment.py`, wired
into `main()`'s own explicit test list (this harness has no auto-discovery - a test function that
isn't called from `main()` silently never runs; caught this myself when the new test reported "0
failure(s)" on the deliberately-unfixed source during the revert-and-confirm-red check, traced it to
the missing `main()` call, fixed that too). One test case (`"R5 million"` itself) initially expected
the wrong band - R5 million lands exactly on `_band_for()`'s own `R0-5m`/`R5-20m` boundary (`< 5_000_000`
is false at exactly 5 000 000, same boundary convention `test_value_band_stated_amount_is_banded_correctly()`
already exercises for R15m) - corrected the test case to R4 million to test the single-digit fix in
isolation, not the unrelated boundary rule.

Verification: confirmed red against the unfixed source (6 failures, `git stash` revert), confirmed
green after restoring the fix (`0 failure(s)`); full `engine/discovery/test_tender_enrichment.py` ->
0 failures; sibling sanity sweep on `engine/discovery/test_award_outcomes.py` (the real source of
`parse_rand()`, reused by this module's own `_parse_amount()`) -> ALL PASSED, unaffected; `py_compile`
clean on both touched files.

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (no PR - small, fully verified, no live-DB access needed):
- `engine/discovery/tender_enrichment.py`
- `engine/discovery/test_tender_enrichment.py`

## This pass (2026-11-01, standing solution-architect review): Finding 112 - scope_llm.py's evidence_quotes were never actually checked against the document text, despite the prompt telling the model they would be

Oriented from `bb65de2`; `git fetch origin main` found nothing new, local already matched exactly. Open
PRs re-checked via the GitHub API: only `#164`/`#165` remain, both unchanged, no collision.

Picked a fresh, previously-unread module this session: `engine/discovery/scope_llm.py` (316 lines, the
LLM-assisted scope-of-work fallback used when the fast/free regex heuristic finds nothing) - read end to
end against `docs/specs/AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md` per CLAUDE.md's own pointer, rather than assuming
compliance because the module's own docstring describes following the standard.

**Found and fixed a real gap**: `SYSTEM_PROMPT` (line 88) explicitly tells the model "[evidence quotes]
are checked against the text afterward, and a summary whose quotes cannot be found is treated as
unverified" - but grepping this file and its only real caller (`tender_enrichment.py`) end to end, no
code anywhere ever actually performed that check. The mandatory review pass (`AI-Call-Quality-
Standard.md` part 2) asks the model to re-check its own quotes against the text as one of five explicit
checklist items, but a model reviewing its own prior output is not the same as a deterministic,
code-side check - and nothing backstopped it if the review pass's own self-check missed a bad quote
(said "No issues found" on a draft whose `evidence_quotes` didn't actually appear in the document).
This is exactly the gap `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py`'s own `evidence_in_text()` exists to close for
CV extraction, in a sibling file that even cites `extract_cv_fields.py` as "this codebase's own proven,
tested call site" for its calling conventions - but the one piece of defense-in-depth that function
provides was never carried over.

Fixed by adding `quote_in_text()`/`verify_evidence_quotes()` (a local reimplementation of
`evidence_in_text()`'s own fuzzy-match rules - normalized substring, then a squeezed-alphanumeric
fallback for a quote a narrow PDF column wrapped across a line break - kept local rather than
cross-importing `engine/cv/` into a production `engine/discovery/` module for one small helper) and
wiring it into `extract_scope_with_review()`: after the review loop finishes, if `scope_found` is true
and the review loop itself didn't already flag an issue, every `evidence_quotes` entry is mechanically
re-checked against the real document text. Any quote that can't be found there - including the
zero-quotes case, which the prompt's own rule says must never accompany `scope_found: true` - now sets
`needs_human_review = True` and appends an explicit note, the same "never silently ship a flawed result"
rule this file's own docstring already states for the pass-cap case. Also corrected
`extract_scope_summary_llm()`'s own `NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW` note wording, which previously always said "the
review pass still found an issue after 3 passes" regardless of why the flag was actually set - now
inaccurate for a flag raised by the new programmatic check on an earlier, "clean" pass.

Verified: wrote 5 new regression tests (direct unit tests of `quote_in_text()`/`verify_evidence_quotes()`,
plus integration tests through the real `extract_scope_with_review()` call: a hallucinated quote flags
`needs_human_review` even when the review pass itself reports "No issues found"; a genuinely-quoted
result is not falsely flagged; `scope_found: false` is never checked against evidence at all). Red-then-
green: stashed the source fix alone, re-ran the suite - it crashed immediately with `AttributeError:
module 'scope_llm' has no attribute '_norm'` (the new tests exercise genuinely new code, not something
already present), confirming a real gap before the fix; restored and re-ran clean. Full suite:
`python3 engine/discovery/test_scope_llm.py` → 44 checks, 0 failures (up from 20). Regression-checked the
only real caller's own suite, `test_tender_enrichment.py` → 0 failures. `py_compile` clean on both
touched files.

Rather than starting a fresh engine-area rotation this cycle, picked up the one specific, well-
described, honestly-unconfirmed lead the immediately-preceding architect pass left open:
`extract_key_person_minimums()`'s `alternatives` list (several qualification/years pairs for one key
position, e.g. R.396's real Senior Materials Technician row - None specified/20, National Diploma/10,
Pr Techni Eng/5) is only built when the qualification column's own phrase-splitting manages to
separate it into as many phrases as there are years values; when it can't, `years_min`/`years_under`
fall through to `(None, None)` unconditionally, even when the individual years figures are still
perfectly legible in the raw text.

Constructed two real-world-plausible trigger layouts (not available before this pass, which is why
the prior one could trace the mechanism but not confirm it with a concrete failing case): a
qualification phrase ending in a dangling connector word ("None specified **or**") right before a
line-wrapped continuation - a genuine `pdftotext -layout` artifact this same file's own `DANGLE` list
already exists to handle elsewhere, just not for this exact row shape - and an all-lowercase
qualification column (the phrase-splitter requires an uppercase first letter). Both reproduced the
exact mechanism the prior pass traced: `alternatives` correctly stays `[]` (the split genuinely
fails), but the row's real stated minimum (5 years, confirmed against the same real R.396 figures the
docstring itself quotes) silently became `None` instead of being recovered.

Fixed: when `alternatives` can't be built but more than one numeric years fragment exists, take the
lowest of the individually-parsed fragments as the row's own `years_min` - the same "the lower bound
is the binding minimum" rule the `alternatives` branch immediately above it already applies.
`alternatives` itself stays honestly empty (which qualification pairs with which figure is genuinely
lost), but the one number the actual compliance check reads is recovered rather than silently dropped.

across both constructed layouts); reverting reproduced the exact predicted 2 failures with every other

`0 failure(s)`. Regression-checked `engine/general/test_requirements.py` (a real consumer) - passes.

## This pass (2026-10-31, standing solution-architect review): fix - CV email verification falsely flagged a correctly-extracted, line-wrapped email address as unverified

Oriented from `b0117c0`; `git fetch origin main` found one new commit since - a sibling QA/robustness
pass's clean sweep (`e3afe62`, `engine/discovery/` only, no overlap) - and fast-forwarded cleanly.
Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub API: only `#164`/`#165` remain, both unchanged, no collision.

Per this session's own judgment call on where to look next (the narrative module turned out already-
hardened last pass), read `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py` (979 lines) end to end for the first time
this session, directly against `docs/specs/AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md` - an AI-call module CLAUDE.md
itself names as one of the three real call sites that standard governs. The prompt-specificity and
honesty-rule requirements are already well met (`SYSTEM_PROMPT`'s explicit "leave it null rather than
inferring", per-field verbatim `evidence` quotes checked afterward); the mandatory 3-pass self-review
loop is genuinely absent, but that standard's own text says so explicitly ("today's three call sites
are single-pass... retrofitting them is separate follow-up work") - a known, already-accepted gap,
not a new finding.

**Found and fixed a real bug** in `validate_proposal()`'s per-field verification: every other check in
this function normalises whitespace before comparing (`evidence_in_text()`'s own "squeezed" branch for
a quote, `_digits()` for `ecsa_number`/`sacpcmp_number`/`phone`) specifically because `pdftotext
-layout` wraps a narrow contact-info column's value across a line break - the exact, already-documented
artifact `test_sa_id_redaction_line_break()` proves happens for real SA ID numbers in real CVs. The
`email` field's own check was the one exception: a literal `value.lower() not in text.lower()`
substring match with no whitespace handling at all. Reproduced directly: for a CV where the email
reads `"Email:    john.doe@\n          example.com"` and the model correctly proposes
`john.doe@example.com` with a correct evidence quote, `evidence_in_text()` itself already returns
`True` for that exact quote/text pair - but the email check disagreed and flagged the value "doesn't
appear in the CV text", a false warning on an already-correct value that would make a reviewer doubt a
field that needed no doubting.

Fixed by stripping all whitespace from both sides before the substring check (`re.sub(r"\s+", "", ...)`
on both `value.lower()` and `text.lower()`), the same "survive a mid-token line wrap" fix already
applied to `SA_ID_RE` for ID numbers. Verified a hallucinated email with no basis in the CV at all is
still correctly flagged - the fix narrows a false positive, it doesn't weaken real detection.

New test `test_email_verification_survives_line_wrap()` added to `test_extract_cv_fields.py` (test 8),
covering both the line-wrapped-but-real case and the genuinely-wrong case. Revert-and-confirm-red
performed: stashing the source fix alone made the new "real, line-wrapped email is verified" check
fail exactly as expected, with the sanity-check assertion (`evidence_in_text()` already agrees) still
passing - proving the two checks genuinely disagreed, not a flaky repro. Restored, full suite green.

Verification: `python3 engine/cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py` - ALL PASSED (9 checks in the new test
function, full suite unaffected); `python3 -m py_compile` clean on both touched files.

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (no PR - small, fully verified, no live-DB access needed):
- `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py`

worker/job-queue rotation (compliance/reminders was last cycle - clean sweep, logged above). Read
`engine/worker/poll_loop.py` (the one polling loop every async bridge shares) and `engine/worker/
run_bridges.py` (the multi-bridge orchestrator the production worker container actually runs) end to
end - both already tightly designed with this exact bug class in mind (per-poll isolation, per-bridge
isolation, signal handling only from the main thread, a bridge's whole process GROUP killed on

infrastructure (confirmed by its own docstring), lower priority under this session's "real production
robustness" scope.

One lead reproduced, then ruled out as unreachable: `run_bridges.py`'s `BridgeRunner.run_once()` calls
`p.communicate(timeout=self.timeout)` on each bridge subprocess with `text=True` (strict UTF-8
decoding) inside a `try/except subprocess.TimeoutExpired` that does NOT also catch
`UnicodeDecodeError` - confirmed directly with a throwaway script that writes non-UTF-8 bytes to its
own stdout: `communicate()` really does raise `UnicodeDecodeError` uncaught, which would abort the
WHOLE `run_once()` pass (skipping every bridge after the broken one, that cycle) rather than being
isolated to just the one broken bridge the way a `TimeoutExpired`/non-zero-exit already is. Traced
whether any of the six registered bridges could plausibly write raw non-UTF-8 bytes to their own
stdout/stderr: every one of them only ever uses plain Python `print()`/exception formatting, which
Python re-encodes through valid Unicode before it ever reaches the OS pipe - the only way invalid
bytes would reach THIS layer is a C extension or the interpreter's own stdout encoding being
misconfigured, not a company's own malformed data flowing through. Not a confirmed, reachable bug via
any of the six real bridges; not fixed, per the standing instruction's own "genuinely clean, not a
weak finding" allowance.

**No code bug found - a genuine clean sweep**, reached by actually reproducing a lead end to end and

QA/robustness review session's own clean sweep of `watch_deadlines.py`/`registration_reminders.py`,

GitHub API: new `#175` ("Add signatory-capacity nudge to new-company setup checklist") is open/draft on
the same reused branch as the earlier merged `#172`/`#173`/`#174`, already shows `mergeable_state:
"dirty"` (its own cross-session conflict to resolve, not this pass's), and its stated file list
(dashboard/notification/people/tender-workspace files) doesn't touch anything this pass changed - no
collision. `#164`/`#165` unchanged.

Reviewed the admin area (`app/app/admin/`) and the onboarding flow first - both came up clean
(`discovered-opportunities/actions.ts`, `requirement-extractions/actions.ts`,
`customers/impersonation-actions.ts`, `taxonomy/actions.ts` are all correctly admin-gated;
`onboarding/actions.ts`'s own ignored `buildCompanyUpdate().error` return is real but not reachable
today - Screen 1's form only ever submits two TEXT fields, which that function can never return an
error for, so not flagged). Pivoted to `engine/general/submission_plan.py` (the "assessment engine"'s
Python reference implementation) and its TypeScript port, `app/app/tenders/[id]/submission-plan-logic.ts`
- a genuine side-by-side comparison of two independent implementations of the same logic, the exact
shape this session has repeatedly found real bugs in.

**Found and fixed a real gap**: `requirements.py` sets `cidb.ambiguous = true` on the stored manifest
when more than one different CIDB grading is found across the documents read (e.g. an addendum
correcting the original notice) - a real Finding from 2026-10-24, with its own warning text in the
Python reference's `compile_plan()`. `process_general_jobs.py` writes this flag verbatim into
`tenders.document_requirements`/`tender_packs.document_requirements`. But the TypeScript
`RequirementManifest["cidb"]` type (`app/lib/generalTender.ts`) never declared an `ambiguous` field at
all, and `cidbGradingStep()` (the TS port's own CIDB-grading classifier, the only call site, from
`submission-plan-data.ts`) never read or surfaced it - so the live Submission Plan screen silently
dropped a real, already-identified compliance warning the Python reference still carries for the exact
same stored data. A company relying on the live screen for a tender with a genuinely conflicting CIDB
grading across its documents would never see that warning at all.

Fixed by adding `ambiguous?: boolean` to the `cidb` type and appending the same warning text
`submission_plan.py`'s own `compile_plan()` uses when `cidbGradingStep()` sees `cidb.ambiguous`.
Reproduced first with a `git stash` of just the two source files (keeping the new test): the new
assertions failed exactly as expected against the unfixed code (`have.note` contained the plain
grading note with no ambiguity warning at all); restored the fix, same test passed. Added 2 new
regression tests to the existing `submission-plan-logic.spec.ts` (ambiguous case surfaces the warning
for both the "have a grading" and "no grading" branches; the ordinary non-ambiguous case never mentions
it, guarding against the warning leaking into every CIDB step by mistake).

Verification: `npx vitest run app/tenders/[id]/submission-plan-logic.spec.ts` -> 37/37 (up from 35);
full `npx vitest run` -> 335/335 (up from 333, unaffected elsewhere); `node --experimental-strip-types
--test lib/*.test.ts` -> 215/215 unaffected (this file isn't under `lib/`); `npx tsc --noEmit` and
`npx eslint` on all 3 touched files -> clean.

for QA-pass-comment density to find the least-reviewed ones: `engine/fill_a_forms.py` (527 lines, the
full A2-A23 returnable-declarations bundle) and `engine/fill_docx_forms.py` had zero QA-pass markers
at all, unlike `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py`/`engine/general/fill_sbd_docx.py` (both already fixed
this session - Findings 100/101).

Found a real, well-known Python gotcha nobody had hit before: `fill_declaration_blanks()`'s "I, the
undersigned, ...." substitution passed an f-string straight to `re.subn()` as the REPLACEMENT
argument. `re.sub`/`subn` treat a STRING replacement's own backslashes specially (`\1` is a
backreference to a captured group; `\9`/`\g<bad>` raise `re.error` for an invalid one) - a
signatory's name containing a literal backslash (a pasted Windows path fragment, an OCR artefact from
the CV-extraction pipeline, a plain typo) either silently spliced this regex's OWN matched "I, the
undersigned," text into the middle of the name with zero error (`"John\1 Doe"` -> `"I, the
undersigned, JOHNI, the undersigned, DOE hereby declare"` - fabricated text in a document meant to be
wet-signed and submitted to SANRAL), or raised a raw, uncaught `re.error` that aborted the whole
company's SANRAL pack build (`"John\9 Doe"`, no group 9 in this pattern). Grepped every `fill_*.py`
file for the same `.sub(f"..."`/`.subn(f"..."` shape and found exactly one more real instance:
`engine/general/fill_sbd_docx.py`'s `fill_dotted_paragraph_count()` (the non-SANRAL/general pack's
own Treasury SBD form filler, used for every free-text field across every SBD1/4/6.1/7/8/9 form) -
same crash, confirmed with `"Smith\1 Construction"` as a bidder name.

Scored severe (not moderate) specifically for the silent-corruption half of this: every other bug this
session found either corrupts internal data with some trace of what happened, or crashes loudly; this
one can put fabricated text directly into a document meant to be submitted to a government buyer with
nothing anywhere - no log line, no warning, no crash - to show it happened.

Fixed both call sites by changing the replacement from a literal f-string to a callable
(`lambda m: f"..."`) - a callable's return value is used by `re.sub`/`subn` completely verbatim, no
backslash processing at all. This is exactly the convention `fill_a_forms.py`'s own `fill_footer()`
(two functions below the fixed one, for the identical name/position/company values) already uses -
it was never vulnerable, which is how the fixed function's own gap stood out by contrast.

Verified red-then-green: new file `engine/test_fill_a_forms.py` (no dedicated test for this module

## This pass (2026-10-31, standing solution-architect review): RLS-policy audit + email-escaping audit - both clean, one non-issue ruled out

Directive: the last two passes thoroughly audited `SECURITY DEFINER` function ownership checks (two
real findings, then a confirmed-clean follow-up). This pass pivoted to two different security-adjacent
angles per the brief: (a) RLS policies themselves (`using`/`with check` clauses), not functions, for a
"forgot to scope by tenant" gap; (b) text-field escaping in generated emails/documents for an
XSS/injection-shaped gap, not the function-ownership shape already covered.

Oriented from `bb6f39c`; `git fetch origin main` found one new sibling commit (`8670a4e`, a different
session's real backslash-in-`re.sub()` fix in `fill_a_forms.py`/`fill_sbd_docx.py`, confirmed via its
own diff, no overlap with anything checked here). Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub API: `#174`
("Split-recipient architecture") confirmed still **open and draft, not merged** - the "submitted-tender
nagging gap" backlog item stays open. `#164`/`#165` unchanged. No collision.

**(a) RLS policy audit.** Cross-referenced every `create table` against every `alter table ... enable
row level security` across all 109 migrations (a small script, not manual reading) - zero tables were
ever created without RLS being enabled on them. Cross-referenced RLS-enabled tables against every
`create policy` (both quoted and bare policy-name syntax, having first caught and fixed a quoting bug
in my own first pass of this check) to find tables locked out entirely (RLS on, no policy at all) -
9 tables matched (`lifecycle_unsubscribe_tokens`, `notification_claims`, `payfast_payment_attempts`,
`platform_admins`, `platform_settings`, `sent_deadline_reminders`, `sent_operational_alerts`,
`tender_listing_snapshots`, `tender_watch_state`); spot-checked 2 of the most sensitive
(`platform_admins`, `payfast_payment_attempts`) and confirmed no client-side code anywhere reads them
directly - these are genuinely internal, service-role-only tables, secure by RLS's own default-deny,
not an oversight. Also grepped for any permissive (non-`restrictive`) write policy (`insert`/`update`/
`delete`) using a blanket `using (true)` - found none; the one `using (true)` write policy that exists
(`tender_packs`'s update policy, 0032) is explicitly `as restrictive`, ANDs with the real tenant-scoped
policy rather than replacing it, and was already reviewed by an earlier pass. Every bare `for select
... using (true)` policy found (11 across 7 migrations) was individually checked against its own table
and confirmed to be deliberately shared/public government-tender reference data (tenders,
tender_requirements, tender_roles, discipline_categories, etc.) - documented as such in each
migration's own comment, not private tenant data. **No RLS gap found - a genuine clean sweep.**

**(b) Email/document text-escaping audit.** Read every `infoCard()`/`tenderHeader()`/`pill()`/
`button()`/`checklist()`/`recipientContextLine()` call site across all 4 email-template tiers
(`emailTemplatesTier0-3.ts`) plus the shared `emailTemplates.ts` and `emailBrand.ts` helpers
themselves - roughly 15 render functions, 20+ individual interpolations of company names, person
names, tender titles, buyer names, and free-text quotes. Every single one that carries real
user-controlled text is wrapped in `escapeHtml()`, either at the call site or inside the shared helper
itself (`infoCard()`'s own `label` column, `tenderHeader()`, `pill()`, `button()`,
`recipientContextLine()` all escape internally - only `infoCard()`'s `value` column relies on the
caller to escape first, and every current caller does). **No unescaped-interpolation gap found.**

Also checked a different, real-world injection class while in this area: Excel formula injection (a
malicious company name/field value starting with `=`/`+`/`-`/`@`, executed as a formula when a SANRAL
evaluator opens a generated submission workbook). Confirmed this is a non-issue for this codebase's
actual `.xlsx` writer (`engine/sanral_fill.py`'s `set_value()`): every string value is written with
`t="inlineStr"` cell typing in the raw OOXML, which every real spreadsheet application (Excel,
LibreOffice, Google Sheets) treats as a literal string regardless of its leading character - only a
cell with an actual `<f>` formula element is ever evaluated, and this writer never emits one for a
data field. The classic CSV-injection variant of this (where Excel's own CSV importer guesses a
leading `=` is a formula) doesn't apply either - grepped for any CSV export anywhere in `app/`/`engine/`
and found none exists in this codebase at all.

No code changed this pass. QA tooling not re-run (nothing to verify - a documented audit, not a fix).
Committed and pushed docs-only.

Backlog unchanged at **19 items** - nothing resolved (PR #174 still unmerged), nothing new added. This

## This pass (2026-10-31, standing solution-architect review): Finding 110 - following up on Finding 109's own pattern, company_can_request_pack()/company_packs_this_period() had the identical gap, leaking a company's real billing/quota state to any other signed-in user who knew its id

Directive: given how significant Finding 109 was (an anon-reachable function leaking any user's secret unsubscribe token), this pass was explicitly a security audit - grep every `SECURITY DEFINER` function granted to `anon`/`authenticated` and check each one actually verifies the caller against the id it's given, not assume Finding 109 was the only instance.

Oriented from `d018ba0`; `git fetch origin main` found one new sibling commit (`a02a699`, the QA/robustness track's own `daily_digest.py` fix two entries below - `engine/notify/`, no overlap) and fast-forwarded local `main` before starting. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub API: `#174` still open/draft (confirmed directly, not trusted from its own description), `#164`/`#165` unchanged - none collide with anything touched here.

Audited roughly 25 `grant execute on function ... to anon, authenticated` statements across every migration (full list pulled by grep, not sampled blind). Confirmed correctly gated, by actually reading each body, not just the grant line: `bank_account_summaries()` (`is_company_member()` in its own WHERE), `acknowledge_discovery_downgrade()`/`set_opportunity_interest()`/`set_opportunity_tag()`/`pursue_discovered_opportunity()` (all four `select ... where id = p_id` then `if not found or not is_company_member(opp.company_id)`), `record_tender_document()` (checks both the tender's owner and the pack's company), `is_employee_in_company()`/`own_linked_person_id()` (both key off `auth.uid()` internally regardless of the company id passed in, so there's nothing to leak), `tender_folder_readable()`/`tt_has_own_requirements()`/`tt_template_object_readable()` (storage-policy helpers, all three gate on `is_company_member`), and a representative sample of `platform_admin_*` functions across migrations 0064/0098/0101/0102 (every one either raises or filters on `is_platform_admin()`). The idempotency/logging functions granted to `anon` (`claim_notification`, `record_notification_sent`, `record_deadline_reminder_sent`, `record_operational_alert_sent`) are insert-only with no sensitive read, so an ownership check doesn't apply the same way - noted, not flagged as a new item.

**Found the one genuine second instance**: `company_packs_this_period(p_company_id uuid)` and `company_can_request_pack(p_company_id uuid)` (0083) never called `is_company_member(p_company_id)` at all. Both are `security definer`, both granted to `authenticated` (PostgREST exposes every RPC to any signed-in session via the public anon key alone). Confirmed all 3 real call sites (`tenders/[id]/actions.ts`, `general-actions.ts`, `app/app/billing/page.tsx`) only ever pass the caller's own `companyId` - so this was pure unused attack surface, not something the UI itself ever misuses.

Reproduced in a disposable scratch Postgres database (not this app's live DB; dropped after): seeded two companies, one ("victim") with `status = 'active'`, `max_packs_per_month = 3`, and 2 `ready` jobs. Company B's own signed-in member called `company_can_request_pack('<victim's uuid>')` and `company_packs_this_period('<victim's uuid>')` directly and got back the victim's real answers (`true`, `2`) - a genuine cross-tenant leak of another company's billing/quota state, reachable with nothing but the app's public anon key and a guessed/known company id.

Fixed by adding the same `is_company_member()` guard every correctly-gated sibling already uses, returning `null` (not `false`/`0`, which would be indistinguishable from a real answer) for a non-member caller. Re-ran the same two-session scratch test after the fix: the attacker now gets `null` from both; the real company's own member still gets the unchanged, correct answer. Checked 4 adjacent real-member cases to confirm no regression: trialing-with-0-packs (`true`), trialing-with-1-pack (`false`), active-under-quota (`true`), active-over-quota tested indirectly via the same logic path. Scratch database dropped after verification.

New migration `0109_company_can_request_pack_membership_check.sql` - `create or replace function`, same pattern `0105`/`0107`/`0108` used to replace a `0083` function body whole, no other behavior change. **Not yet applied to the live database** - needs Sarel's run via Supabase's SQL Editor, same as `0096`/`0107`/`0108` before it.

No JS/TS or Python files touched - SQL-only, no existing test suite covers these RPCs (confirmed via grep, none reference them), verification was the scratch-database replay above.

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (no PR - SQL-only, fully verified against a scratch DB, consistent with every other SQL fix this session):
- `app/supabase/migrations/0109_company_can_request_pack_membership_check.sql` (new)
- `docs/specs/System-Status.md`

**Backlog: 18 → 19** (new item: migration `0109` needs applying to live DB, closing the second cross-tenant billing-data leak this session found). Everything else on the list is unchanged - not re-investigated, not re-flagged, per the standing instruction. The audit itself, beyond this one fix, came back clean across ~25 functions checked - a genuinely thorough security pass, not a token "looked and found nothing" sweep.

## This pass (2026-10-31, standing QA/robustness review - one-hundred-and-thirty-sixth run): Finding 109 in QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md - daily_digest.py's --mode local was unconditionally wired to the wrong object, so document-expiry and person-credential-expiry sections were silently empty for every company, every run

(Numbered independently of the solution-architect review's own "Finding 109" immediately below - two
separate tracks, same number by coincidence, no relation; see this file's own standing note on that.)

Oriented from `2115727` (fast-forwarded cleanly before the architect review's own `d018ba0` landed;
re-fetched again before pushing - no collision, confirmed below). Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub
API: `#174` (still open/draft, `app/lib`/`scripts` only), `#164`/`#165` (unchanged) - none touch
`engine/notify/` or `engine/compliance/`.

notify rotation (discovery was last cycle - see the entry below). `record_heartbeat.py` and
`send_digest_emails.py` came up clean on direct reading and reasoning (both already correctly never
raise, already have the per-item "one bad entry doesn't abort the batch" guard from an earlier
"Enterprise-readiness audit round 2, 2026-10-20" pass). `daily_digest.py` itself is large (898 lines)
and extremely well-guarded everywhere else (every independent sub-system - tender updates,
re-assessed tenders, listing changes, the per-roster-entry digest-build loop - already has its own
isolated try/except from prior passes), so read it function-by-function looking for the one area not
already covered that way.

Found it in `main()`'s own `--mode local` wiring: `local_document_expiry()`/
`local_person_credential_expiry()` read a profile's `"company"`/`"key_people"` keys (the RAW
profile.json shape `suggest_pack.py`/`generate_cv.py` also read directly) - but `main()` was feeding
them `assess_tender.load_company_profile()`'s own return value, which is a DIFFERENT, already-
transformed dict (`disciplines`/`bee_level`/`black_ownership_pct`/`has_cidb_grading`/`offices` only -
confirmed by reading that function's own `return` statement, no `"company"`/`"key_people"` key at
all). Reproduced directly: feeding the transformed dict into `local_document_expiry()` always returns
`[]`, regardless of what the real profile.json contains - not a rare edge case, the ONLY possible
outcome through this wiring. The existing dedicated test for `local_person_credential_expiry()` masked
this completely, because it hand-builds a `{"key_people": [...]}` fixture directly rather than going
through `main()`'s own wiring. Confirmed `--mode live` (the only mode the real scheduled workflow,
`.github/workflows/daily-digest.yml`, ever runs) reads these two sections from Supabase through a
completely separate path and was never exposed to this - `--mode local` is the dev/offline-only
convenience path (also what `main()` falls back to automatically whenever the Supabase env vars
aren't set), not what runs in production, but exactly the path a developer verifying a change to
either section offline would reach for, and it silently couldn't do that at all.

While fixing the wiring, also fixed the same "null present, not missing" gap this session has hit
repeatedly elsewhere (`suggest_pack.py`, Finding 107 above): `profile.get("company", {})`/`profile.get
("key_people", [])` only substitute the default when the key is ABSENT, not when it's `null` - a real
profile.json shape for the identical file's own `"key_people"`/`"projects"` keys. Fixing the wiring
alone would have made this newly reachable (these two functions had never actually received a real
profile before), so fixed both in the same pass.

Fixed: `main()` now re-reads the raw profile JSON directly (same graceful OSError/JSONDecodeError
degrade as `assess_tender.load_company_profile()`'s own read) and passes that to both functions;
`profile.get(key, default)` changed to `profile.get(key) or default` in both. Verified red-then-
green: extended `engine/compliance/test_watch_person_credentials.py` with 5 new checks (a control
case proving the bug's premise, the real fix finding both sections, explicit-null degrading safely);
reverting reproduced the exact predicted `AttributeError` at the exact line, every other check (old
and new) stayed green; restored, `0 failure(s)`. Regression-checked `engine/notify/test_digest_live.py`,
`engine/notify/test_digest_opt_in.py`, `engine/compliance/test_watch_deadlines_urgency.py` - all pass.

## This pass (2026-10-31, standing solution-architect review): Finding 109 - lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for() granted the public anon role the power to fetch ANY user's secret unsubscribe token by uuid

Oriented from `2115727`; `git fetch origin main` found one new commit (`e1de394`, a sibling QA-
robustness pass's real `assess_tender.py`/`taxonomy` fix - Finding 108 above - confined to
`engine/discovery/`, no overlap) and fast-forwarded cleanly. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub API:
`#174` ("Split-recipient architecture", still **open and draft**, not merged) and `#165`/`#164`
(unchanged) - none touch anything below. **PR #174's own diff was read in full as independent,
read-only verification** (fetched its branch locally, diffed against `main`, deleted the temp branch
after) rather than trusted from its description: it genuinely adds `pipeline_stage` filtering to both
`deadlineReminders.ts`/`returnablesDigestCandidates.ts` (new `DEADLINE_REMINDER_EXCLUDED_STAGES`/
`RETURNABLES_EXCLUDED_STAGES`, both correctly wired into the sender scripts' own `select()` calls to
actually fetch `pipeline_stage`), which would resolve the "submitted-tender nagging gap" backlog item
- but it is **still unmerged**, so that item stays open, not resolved, until it actually lands.

Checked `/auth/callback/route.ts` and `lib/safeRedirect.ts` (an API-route/auth-boundary sweep,
following up on the session's "check every route handler" thread) - already correctly hardened from
an earlier QA pass (both the `//`-protocol-relative and the WHATWG backslash-as-path-separator open-
redirect bypasses are covered). Checked `/api/unsubscribe/route.ts` next, which led to a real finding:
read `lifecycle_unsubscribe_tokens`/`lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for()`/`unsubscribe_lifecycle_email()`
(0093) end to end.

**Found and fixed a real, independently-reproduced security bug**:
`lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for(p_user_id uuid)` - the function that looks up (or lazily creates) a
user's real, secret, unguessable unsubscribe token - takes an arbitrary caller-supplied `p_user_id`
with **no check that the caller is that user**, and was granted to `anon` AND `authenticated`. Those
are exactly the two roles PostgREST exposes every Supabase RPC call to using nothing but the app's own
public anon key (shipped in the client bundle by design, not a secret) - so anyone holding it could
call this RPC directly against the REST endpoint for ANY uuid and get back that real user's token, then
redeem it via the (correctly public, by RFC 8058 design) `/api/unsubscribe` endpoint to silently flip a
stranger's `lifecycle_email_opt_out` to true. The sibling function with the identical shape and
sensitivity - `company_notification_recipients()` (0094/0095), also a privileged by-id lookup with a
caller-supplied argument - is correctly granted to `service_role` ONLY; this one alone broke that
already-established pattern. Confirmed the one real caller
(`app/scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.ts`) authenticates with `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, a role that
bypasses every grant/revoke here entirely - so the `anon`/`authenticated` grant was never actually
needed for the function to work, only to be exploited. Grepped the whole repo for every other call
site to confirm this is the only one.

Not exploitable purely from today's UI by itself (no page currently hands another user's own
`auth.users.id` to the browser), but the grant is wrong independent of that, and it's the one thing
standing between "needs an id leak somewhere else first" and "needs nothing at all" - the id itself is
an unguessable random v4 UUID, not brute-forceable.

Reproduced and fixed safely in a disposable scratch Postgres database (`scratch_grant_test`, dropped
immediately after - the live DB was never touched, per the standing production-DB-mutation rule):
built a byte-for-byte copy of the real table/function/grant from 0093, confirmed `set role anon;
select lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for(<any uuid>)` genuinely returned a real token before the fix,
then applied the exact revoke/grant from the new migration and confirmed the identical call now fails
with `permission denied for function`, while `set role service_role` (the real caller's actual role)
still succeeds unaffected.

Fixed with new migration `0108_lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for_grant.sql` (`revoke all ... from anon,
authenticated; grant execute ... to service_role`) - a pure privilege change, no schema/data change,
no app-code change needed (the real caller already uses the service-role key). Migration `0108` is
written and pushed but **NOT applied to the live database** - needs Sarel's run via Supabase's SQL
Editor, same as every other pending migration on this list. `unsubscribe_lifecycle_email(text)` itself
(the actual RFC 8058 bearer-token redemption) is correctly left untouched - only its sibling token
GETTER was over-granted.

No JS/TS/Python touched, so no code-level QA tooling applies; the fix's own correctness was verified
end-to-end against the scratch-database reproduction above, which is the real test here.

**Backlog: 17 + 2 new = 19** (Finding 109 above: migration `0108` needs applying to close the
over-grant; PR #174 remains open/draft, NOT YET a resolution of the submitted-tender nagging item -
watch for it to merge before closing that one). All 17 prior items carried forward unchanged.

regex, confirmed by direct fuzzing) and `taxonomy.fit_overlap()` didn't crash on unknown slugs or
empty inputs either.

Found a real, silent (non-crashing) data bug instead: `assess_tender.load_company_profile()` reads
`company.get("disciplines", [])` straight from a hand-maintained `profile.json` with no type check.
Every other field on a real profile's `company` object genuinely is a bare string (`bee_level`,
`black_ownership_pct`), so typing `"disciplines": "roads_civil"` instead of `["roads_civil"]` is a
realistic hand-editing mistake. `taxonomy.fit_overlap()`'s own `set(company_disciplines or [])`
doesn't reject that - Python iterates a string into its individual characters - so the company's own,
exactly-matching discipline tag then never equals any real category slug. Reproduced directly: a
profile with `disciplines` as a bare string scored that company's own `road_maintenance` tender as
"outside the company's disciplines" / `not_a_fit`, with no error or warning at all - the same "silent
wrong data is the main risk" failure mode this same file's own `find_delivery_address()`/
`find_closing_time()` already guard against everywhere else, just unguarded here. Confirmed the live,
automated Discovery fan-out (`company_profiles.py`, always builds `disciplines` as a real
`sorted()`-of-a-set list) can never hit this - only the CLI/manual-profile path
(`classify_tender.py`'s own `--profile` flag, or any manual fit check) can.

Fixed: a bare string normalises to a one-item list (the obviously intended reading); a genuinely
wrong type (an int, a dict) falls back to `[]` with a loud `WARNING` printed, never silently
iterated into garbage; a real list is unchanged. Verified red-then-green with a brand-new
`engine/discovery/test_assess_tender.py` (no dedicated test for this function existed at all before
this pass) - 4 test functions, 5 checks; reverting reproduced all 3 predicted failures exactly, the
control case stayed green throughout. Regression-checked `engine/discovery/test_taxonomy.py`,
`engine/discovery/test_discovery_fanout.py`, `engine/intake/test_classify_tender.py` - all pass.

two separate RPCs from two different TypeScript call sites, so the real fix is a new, single atomic
SQL function (quota check + job insert in one transaction, locking the subscription row for its
duration) that both `actions.ts` and `general-actions.ts` would need to switch to calling instead of
their current two-step pattern. That's a larger, multi-call-site change touching the revenue-metering
path directly - genuinely riskier than this pass's "small, safe, well-verified, direct-to-main" bar,

## Prior pass (2026-10-30, standing solution-architect review): Finding 105 (not fixed, flagged for Sarel) - no storage-level size/type limit on ANY of this app's 9 upload buckets; the only guard is client-side JS, trivially bypassed by a user who already holds a valid session

Oriented from `b9c5ed2`; `git fetch origin main` found one new commit since (`fd7b327`, a different
session's `opportunity_requirements.py` per-release exception-isolation fix - read the real diff,
`engine/discovery/` only, no overlap) and fast-forwarded local `main`. Open PRs `#172`/`#165`/`#164`
re-confirmed unchanged via the GitHub API, no collision.

**Re-checked the "submitted-tender nagging gap" backlog item first** (per this pass's own directive,
having just touched `send-returnables-digest.ts` for an unrelated fix last pass): re-read both
`send-returnables-digest.ts` and `send-deadline-reminders.ts` directly. The diagnosis is still
exactly accurate - neither file selects or filters on `pipeline_stage` anywhere (confirmed by grep),
and the prior pass's own fix to `send-returnables-digest.ts` only moved where `claim_notification` is
called, a completely different part of the file; it didn't touch, and couldn't have accidentally
fixed, this gap. `send-operational-alerts.ts`'s `CLOSED_STAGES` guard (`lib/printCutoffReminders.ts`)
is still the one deliberate exception. No change needed to that backlog entry's wording - it already
describes the real, current state correctly.

**The new finding**: every one of this app's 9 `storage.buckets` inserts (`0008` CV uploads, `0012`
experience documents, `0014` vault compliance documents, `0017` pack-generation output, `0018`
submission packs, `0022` admin harness, `0063` onboarding documents, `0071` discovered-opportunity
documents, `0087` narrative documents) only ever sets `(id, name, public)` - none sets Postgres
Storage's own `file_size_limit` or `allowed_mime_types` columns (confirmed by grep across every
migration). The RLS policy on each (e.g. `0063`'s own `"onboarding-documents: tenant isolation by path
prefix"`) checks only `is_company_member((storage.foldername(name))[1]::uuid)` - tenant isolation,
nothing about size or type.

The ONLY size/type enforcement anywhere in this app is client-side: `FileDropzone`'s
`validateFiles({ acceptedExtensions, maxBytes })`, called before every `uploadBatch()` call site
(`upload-form.tsx`, `VaultDocumentUploader.tsx`, `quick-blocker-drawer.tsx` - all three checked, all
three do call it). But `uploadBatch.ts`'s own header comment says plainly why uploads go straight from
the browser to Supabase Storage rather than through a Server Action: "a Server Action body is capped
at 4.5 MB; a batch of certificates together would blow past that" - which means the browser already
holds a real, valid Supabase session token with write access to that bucket path. Client-side JS is
not a security boundary for a user who already has a legitimate session: calling the Storage REST API
directly with that same token (trivial - it's exactly what the browser's own `fetch` does, just not
gated by `validateFiles()` first) uploads any size or type of file with nothing in Postgres or Storage
ever refusing it.

Traced one concrete consequence rather than stopping at "this looks bad": `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py`'s
shared `storage_download()` (used by `process_onboarding_jobs.py`, `process_cv_jobs.py`, and others)
streams the download straight to a local worker disk file via `shutil.copyfileobj` with no size check
of its own - so this isn't a memory-exhaustion crash, but it IS an unbounded disk-fill / storage-cost
vector: nothing stops a company from uploading a multi-GB file (or many of them) to a bucket meant for
a few-page PDF certificate, consuming real Supabase Storage billing and, on a shared worker with
limited disk, potentially starving a job for every other company's queue too.

**Why this is flagged, not fixed**: Postgres Storage's `file_size_limit`/`allowed_mime_types` columns
could be set via a straightforward migration, but the right VALUES are a real product decision I'm
not positioned to guess at - a cap sized wrong (too small) would start silently rejecting legitimate
scanned multi-page PDF certificates or CV documents that currently work fine, which is worse than the
status quo; too large defeats the point. This also spans all 9 buckets at once, not one isolated file,
same shape as the already-flagged submitted-tender nagging gap. Not reproduced against a live Supabase
project (no live credentials in this sandbox) - reasoned directly from the migration SQL and RLS
policy text, which is sufficient to establish every bucket genuinely has no server-side limit set,
without needing a live run. One caveat stated honestly: if Sarel's Supabase project has a
project-level global upload-size cap configured in the dashboard (outside this repo's migrations),
that would already provide a partial backstop this review has no visibility into - worth confirming
rather than assuming the worst case is the live case.

QA tooling: nothing in this file/area touched; no code change this pass.

No code fixed this pass - this is a genuine finding surfaced for Sarel's own call, following the same
discipline as the submitted-tender nagging gap. Backlog: 13 -&gt; **14** (new item: no storage-level
size/type limit on any upload bucket).

## This pass (2026-10-30, standing solution-architect review): fixed `send_pack_ready_email.py` claiming its one-time notification token before every failure-prone step, not just the missing-API-key one

Oriented from `b2550a6`; `git fetch origin main` found one new commit since (`8cf31b5`, a sibling
standing-review session's clean sweep of `engine/compliance/` + a confirmation that
`tenderCompliance.ts`'s COID "renew soon" fix was the only hand-rolled sibling - no overlap) and
fast-forwarded local `main`. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub API: `#172`/`#165`/`#164`, all
unchanged, no collision.

Per the directive, read the actual email-sending retry/error-handling mechanics (not the content
bugs already fixed this session) across `engine/notify/`. `send_digest_emails.py`'s bounded
429-retry and per-recipient failure isolation are already careful and correct - no bug there.

**Found and fixed a real bug** in `send_pack_ready_email.py`'s `send_pack_ready_email()`: it called
`claim_notification()` - the one-time, atomic, *never-unclaimed* idempotency token (migration 0093)
- BEFORE the recipients lookup, the tender/company `select()`s, and `_render()` (a 30s subprocess
call to a Node render script). Every one of those can genuinely fail (a transient Supabase/network
error, an empty lookup, a bad render-script exit), and since no cron or retry ever re-invokes this
function for the same job id once a pack is "ready" (its own docstring says so explicitly), any
failure after the old claim point permanently burned the claim with the email never actually sent -
the pack-ready notification for that job would be lost forever, with only a `system_alerts` entry to
show it happened. This is the *exact* bug class a 2026-10-28 QA pass already fixed one instance of
here (claiming with no `RESEND_API_KEY` configured) and that `lib/notificationEngine.ts`'s own
`sendNotification()` is deliberately written to avoid (claim immediately before the real send, never
before it) - the earlier fix closed the API-key case specifically but left every other failure mode
between claim and send still open.

Reproduced directly first with a standalone repro mirroring the file's own test harness: forced
`_render()` to fail and confirmed `claim_notification` was still called and "consumed" even though
nothing was ever sent. Fixed by moving the claim to immediately before the first real send, after
recipients/tender/company/render have all already succeeded - the same position the canonical
TypeScript sender claims in.

Updated `test_send_pack_ready_email.py`: `test_skips_cleanly_when_already_claimed` now mocks render
(it genuinely runs before the claim check in the new order) and asserts on the final outcome instead
of call ordering that no longer holds; `test_render_failure_is_caught_and_never_raises` gained an
assertion that `claim_notification` is now never even called when render fails (the actual
regression check); added `test_render_failure_never_wastes_the_one_time_claim`, which asserts the
recipients lookup happens before the claim on the happy path. Revert-and-confirm-red: stashing only
`send_pack_ready_email.py` made exactly those two new assertions fail with the old call order, every
other test still passed; restoring made all 17 checks pass again.

Verification: `python3 engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py` -> 17/17 (0 failures); `py_compile`
clean on both touched files; `test_send_digest_emails.py` and `test_record_heartbeat.py` re-run as an
adjacent sanity sweep, both unaffected and both reporting `0 failure(s)` (the digest suite's own
printed "1 failed" line is its own test deliberately exercising a malformed-entry case, not a real
test failure - neither file was touched by this change).

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (no PR - small, fully verified, no live-DB access):
- `engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py`
- `engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py`

judgment-call item for Sarel. Old count 13 + 0 new = **13**.

## This pass (2026-10-30, standing solution-architect review): Finding 104 - a person's project value had NO validation at all (not even negative/garbage), written verbatim onto a real SANRAL Form B1/B2 experience row; the sibling "company experience" form had the same gap minus the negative check

Oriented from `8ceaf9a`; `git fetch origin main` found nothing new since, local already matched. Open
PRs re-checked via the GitHub API: `#172`, `#165`, `#164`, all open and unchanged, no collision.

Per this pass's own directive - follow up on the immediately-prior pass's finding (`companyProfileUpdate.ts`'s
missing upper bound on percentage/`bee_level` fields that get written onto real government documents) by
looking for the same bug SHAPE elsewhere - searched every `build*Update()`-style function (only one exists)
and then every form-action file under `app/app/**/actions.ts` that parses a numeric field from `FormData`.
`company/principals/actions.ts`'s `ownership_pct` already correctly bounds 0-100 - not a bug, a sibling that
got it right.

**Found and fixed a real, reachable bug**: `app/app/people/actions.ts`'s `saveProject()` - the "add a
project to this person's experience" form, used from the person's CV/project-history page - had NO
validation on `value_rm` (the project value in R millions) AT ALL: not NaN, not negative, nothing. Traced
where this value actually goes: `engine/fill_tender.py`/`engine/fill_conventional.py` both read it straight
from the `projects` table and write it with `wb.set_value(T, f"I{r}", pr["value_rm"])` onto a real SANRAL
Form B1/B2 experience-schedule cell on an actual government bid submission - there is no check constraint
on `projects.value_rm` either (`0001_init_schema.sql`, plain `numeric`). A negative value (e.g. "-50", maybe
a typo for a minus sign meant as a dash) would print unchanged on a real tender document. Reproduced
directly (`node -e`): `"-50"` -> `-50` (accepted), `"999999999"` -> `999999999` (accepted, though no
documented sane ceiling exists for this one the way `bee_level`'s 1-9 did, so this fix does NOT add an
upper bound - only an unambiguous, defensible lower one); garbage text like `"abc"` silently became `null`
on insert (Supabase-js JSON-serializes `NaN` to `null`) rather than being rejected with an error, so the
user's typed value just vanished with no feedback.

Fixed by rejecting `NaN` and negative values with a clear error redirect, matching this file's own existing
`?error=` query-param convention. While tracing this, found the identical gap (missing negative check, NaN
already handled) in the sibling `app/app/experience/actions.ts`'s `saveExperienceTags()` - the
company-level "experience" item, same `value_rm` unit per `0012_experience_items.sql`'s own comment ("R
millions, same unit as projects.value_rm and Form B1"). That value feeds
`engine/narrative/build_prompt.py`'s `"R{value_rm}m"` text in a real, customer-facing AI-generated
narrative, and `0012`'s own `match_experience()` RPC's `>=` filter - a negative value would read as visibly
broken in the narrative and silently corrupt that filter's comparison. Fixed the same way, matching that
file's own `err(back, "...")` convention.

Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on both touched files; `npx eslint` clean on both; a standalone
Node reproduction confirmed the exact before/after behavior (`-50`/`"abc"` now rejected, `150`/empty still
accepted unchanged). No dedicated test file exists for either action file (both are `"use server"` Next.js
actions calling `redirect()`/Supabase `createClient()`/`requireCompanyId()` - heavier to unit-test directly
than a pure `lib/` function like the prior pass's fix - noted as a gap, not filled this pass, to keep this
change small and focused). Ran the full existing suites as a sanity sweep instead: `node
--experimental-strip-types --test lib/*.test.ts` -> 207/207 (one transient single-test flake on the first
run, cleared on 3 immediate reruns at 207/207 each - pre-existing and unrelated, since neither touched file
is under `lib/`); `npx vitest run` -> 295/295, unaffected.

**Honest limitation of this fix**: unlike `bee_level`'s 1-9 (a real, documented SANRAL range) or a
percentage's 0-100 (mathematically fixed), there is no equally defensible upper bound for a monetary value
in R millions - South Africa's largest real infrastructure contracts run into the tens of thousands of
R-millions, so inventing a round "big enough" ceiling without a source would risk rejecting a real large
contract. This fix closes the unambiguous half of the gap (negative/garbage) and deliberately leaves the
upper-bound question open rather than guessing at a number with no documented basis - flagging it here
rather than quietly deciding it myself.

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (small, well-verified, no PR, no live-DB access):
- `app/app/people/actions.ts`
- `app/app/experience/actions.ts`
- `docs/specs/System-Status.md`

Backlog: unchanged at 13 items - this finding was standalone (negative/garbage rejection, not a new
judgment-call item), nothing resolved or added. Old count 13 + 0 new = **13**.
