## This pass (2026-10-29, standing solution-architect review): Finding 99 - DBSA's real stated closing TIME (`@ 23H55`) was being discarded, not just defaulted - the actual bug was worse than the "date-only default" shape found earlier this session

Oriented from `12a4908` (a different session's `fix(notify)` for `daily_digest.py`'s silently-dropped
ownerless seen-row, found after my own last-known commit `05acc4f`) - `git fetch origin main` showed
this one new commit; verified its real diff (not just its commit message) before fast-forwarding
local `main`, no overlap with anything touched this pass. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub API:
`#172`, `#165`, `#164`, all unchanged, none touching `engine/discovery/` - no collision.

Per this pass's own directive, looked at the discovery scrapers for a non-SANRAL source for a sibling
of the "closing-time convention" bug class this session has repeatedly found (day-count drift, the
SANRAL date-only default). Found something **more serious than that shape, not just another
instance of it**, in `engine/discovery/dbsa_procurement.py` (the Development Bank of Southern
Africa's open-RFP/RFR table, wired live into `gov_sources.py`, 14 open tenders as of the last real
check 2026-10-18): DBSA's own closing-date cells always carry a real, explicit time in the form
`02 November 2026 @ 23H55` - but the old `_strip_time_suffix()` discarded that `@ 23H55` suffix
entirely before handing the bare date to `sh.iso_sast()`, which then defaulted it to SAST midnight
(the generic "no time given" marker). That's not the earlier "picked the wrong default for an
unknown time" bug - DBSA's time here is **known and real**, and the old code threw it away, turning
a 23:55 deadline into one `tenders.closing_date` recorded as `00:00:00` on the same calendar day (and
rendered by `dates.ts` as `"(Time TBC in RFP)"`, actively telling the customer the time was unstated
when DBSA had in fact stated it) - up to a full day earlier than the real deadline, in the wrong
direction a customer could act on.

Confirmed the existing test fixture (`test_gov_sources.py`'s `DBSA_TABLE_HTML`, a real row captured
2026-10-18) already encoded this as the *expected* result (`closing_date ==
"2026-11-02T00:00:00+02:00"`) - the bug was baked into the test, not merely untested.

Fixed by replacing `_strip_time_suffix()` with `_parse_dbsa_closing()`: it now converts DBSA's
`@ HH'H'MM` suffix into the `HH:MM` form `parse_sast()` already understands for a `DD Month YYYY`
date (same format Rand Water uses) and keeps calling `sh.iso_sast()` on the result - preserving the
real time instead of discarding it. Only a genuinely time-less DBSA closing (none seen in practice,
not ruled out) now falls back to `sh.iso_sast_closing()`'s existing 11:00 SAST convention, the same
default every other confirmed date-only source already uses - previously even that bare-date case
would have defaulted to midnight via `iso_sast()`, so this closes that latent gap too.

Verified: updated the existing fixture assertion to the correct value
(`"2026-11-02T23:55:00+02:00"`), added two new checks (a single-digit-hour case, `9H00` -> `09:00`;
and a genuinely date-only case confirming the 11:00 fallback), and did a revert-and-confirm-red pass -
stashed the fix and re-ran: the main assertion failed exactly as expected (red), the typo-month case
stayed green (unaffected), restored, clean. `python3 engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py` -> ALL
PASSED; `test_source_http.py` and `test_tender_updates.py` run as an adjacent sanity sweep, both
clean; `py_compile` clean on both touched files.

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (small, fully verified, no PR):

- `engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py`
- `docs/specs/System-Status.md`

**2026-10-29 ~08:50 UTC — Discovery page: fixed the slow Opportunity-preferences save and the flaky
"Interested" button (same root cause), added a preferred-clients preference, and three new filters
(Sarel's own live feedback, 2026-10-29).**

**Root cause, confirmed by reading the code, not guessed:** `preferencesActions.ts`'s
`setOpportunityPreferences()` and `actions.ts`'s `setOpportunityTag()`/`setOpportunityInterest()` all
called `revalidatePath("/discovery")` on every single checkbox/chip/button click - forcing
`page.tsx`'s own deliberately heavy `renderDiscovery()` (8 parallel queries, N+1 listing-change/scope
lookups, up to `MAX_PRICING_LOOKUPS=40` market-pricing lookups) to re-run synchronously before the
click could visually resolve. `OpportunityQuickActions.tsx`'s "Interested"/tag controls had NO local
optimistic state at all (by design, per its own prior header comment) - they relied entirely on that
slow revalidate to show the new value, so a user who clicked again before it resolved was reading the
STALE `interest` prop and could flip it straight back off - not "nothing happened", an actual
flip-flop. Two fixes, not one band-aid:
- `preferencesActions.ts`: dropped `revalidatePath("/discovery")` entirely (confirmed by reading the
  file's own header comment that `interested_disciplines` is "a UI-level filter/sort only" - a pure
  in-memory re-sort of rows the page already fetched, never a WHERE clause - so nothing there
  genuinely needs a synchronous refetch); kept `revalidatePath("/pipeline")` (`hide_sanral_board`
  really does gate that page's own "found" column, a real branch, not just a sort).
- `OpportunityQuickActions.tsx`: added the exact optimistic-update-then-revert-on-failure pattern
  `OpportunityPreferencesPanel.tsx` already used successfully - `setOpportunityTag`/
  `setOpportunityInterest` (`actions.ts`) now return `{ok}` so the component knows whether to revert.
  Their own `revalidatePath("/discovery")` stays (interest_marker genuinely gates the Declined/
  Interested tabs' real full-history filter), it just no longer blocks what the user sees on click.

**Preferred clients (Sarel: "add a list of clients as preferences"):** new `preferred_buyers text[]`
column on `company_tender_preferences` (migration `0104`, GIN index, same shape as `interested_disciplines`
0088) - a tag-style add/remove list in the Opportunity preferences panel, saved through the same
action. Same additive, non-authoritative sort-boost role as disciplines - never a filter, never
changes `verdict`. New `lib/opportunityBuyerMatch.ts` (`sanitizePreferredBuyers()`/
`matchesPreferredBuyers()`, 13 tests): matching is a case-insensitive substring check either direction
(e.g. "SANRAL" matches "South African National Roads Agency SOC Ltd (SANRAL)"), not an exact
comparison - confirmed by grep that `discovered_opportunities.buyer` has no canonical taxonomy
anywhere in this schema, unlike disciplines (migration 0040).

**"Likely to qualify" filter (Sarel: "a filter for high likelihood of compliance ... tenders I
potentially qualify for"):** new `VerdictFilter` value `likely_fit` = `verdict IN ('strong_fit',
'possible')` (`lib/discoveryPagination.ts`) - deliberately a DIFFERENT grouping than the existing
"Needs review" tab (`possible` + `needs_review`): `possible` means "you likely qualify, with some
uncertainty", a bare `needs_review` means "we don't know yet" - reusing needs_review's grouping here
would have answered a different question than the one asked.

**Client/buyer filter (Sarel: "add a filter for clients"):** a plain GET-form text input (no client
JS needed), `ilike` substring match on `buyer`, applied to the main query AND every per-tab count
query so counts stay accurate for whatever's typed - same reasoning `withVerdictSpec()` already
documents for verdict. Suggestions (`<datalist>`) come from the currently-loaded window plus the
company's own preferred_buyers, same documented "scoped to current window" limitation `allCompanyTags`
already has (no canonical buyer list to draw a full-history list from).

**"Interested" filter + hide Declined everywhere else (Sarel: "add a filter for Interested... once i
click on not interested then it should be removed from the list ... unless i specifically want to
filter and look at all not interested"):** new `VerdictFilter` value `interested` (symmetric with the
existing `declined`), and a new `shouldExcludeDeclined()` pure function - true for every tab except
"declined" itself - composed into `withVerdictSpec()` via a NULL-safe `.or("interest_marker.is.null,interest_marker.neq.declined")`.
Deliberately NOT a plain `.neq()`: Postgres's three-valued WHERE logic means `interest_marker <>
'declined'` evaluates to NULL (excluded) when the column IS NULL, which is almost every row today - a
naive `.neq()` here would have hidden everything, not just declined rows. Caught this before shipping,
not after.

**Real finding while wiring these in:** `page.tsx` had its OWN locally-redeclared `VerdictFilter` type
- identical values, but a second, silently-driftable copy of `lib/discoveryPagination.ts`'s own
export, the exact "two places computing/declaring the same real-world fact" bug shape this session's
other standing-review passes have repeatedly found and fixed elsewhere (see the entries below). Fixed
in passing: now imported, not redeclared.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx eslint` on all 7 touched files clean; `node
--experimental-strip-types --test lib/*.test.ts` 194/194 (13 new in `opportunityBuyerMatch.test.ts`, 5
new in `discoveryPagination.test.ts`); `npx vitest run` 295/295; `npm run build` clean, `/discovery`'s
own route classification unchanged.

**2026-10-28 ~18:30 UTC — Standing review: Tender Command Center's own "days to close" math had
drifted into a second, disagreeing copy of `lib/dates.ts`'s canonical `daysUntil()`; fixed.**

Found while cross-checking the Command Center feature (dashboard/page.tsx's dispatch lanes,
`command-center.tsx`) against the same "never a second number that could disagree" rule this app
already documents and enforces elsewhere (`dispatchTriage.ts`'s own module header literally states
this rule for blocking-item lists - just not for day counts). `lib/dispatchTriage.ts` had two inline
`Math.ceil((closingDate - now) / day)` computations (in `deriveDecisionNeeded` and
`classifyDispatchBucket`, the latter deciding the `in_progress`/`radar` 7-day bucket boundary), and
`lib/dispatchDashboard.ts` had a third copy as its own local `daysUntilFrom()` helper (the 14-day
`DEEP_CHECK_WINDOW_DAYS` gate) - none of the three imported or called `lib/dates.ts`'s own
`daysUntil()`, which every card's own displayed `DeadlineChip` uses instead. The difference: the
inline copies measured from the exact current instant (`now.getTime()`); `daysUntil()` measures from
today's midnight, by design, "so the count is stable all day" (its own doc comment).

Concrete, reproducible failure: a tender closing `2026-11-04T09:00+02:00`, viewed at
`2026-10-28T15:00+02:00` (an ordinary afternoon) - `classifyDispatchBucket()`'s inline math computed
7 days left and placed the card in the **Urgent Actions & Blocked Items** lane (`in_progress`,
"closing within 7 days"), while the very same card's own `DeadlineChip` (driven by `daysUntil()`)
read **8 days left** right next to it. Since midnight-of-today is always earlier than "now", the
canonical `daysUntil()` is mathematically always ≥ the inline copies' answer - so this wasn't a rare
edge case, it fires every afternoon/evening for any tender sitting near the 7-day or 14-day boundary.

Fix: gave `daysUntil()` an optional injectable `now` param (defaults to `new Date()`, so every
existing single-arg call site is unaffected) and made it the one shared function; removed all three
duplicate copies, replacing them with calls to `daysUntil(dateStr, now)`.

- `app/lib/dates.ts`: `daysUntil(dateStr, now = new Date())`.
- `app/lib/dispatchTriage.ts`: both inline day-count computations replaced; now imports `daysUntil`.
- `app/lib/dispatchDashboard.ts`: local `daysUntilFrom()` deleted; now imports `daysUntil`.
- `app/lib/dispatchTriage.test.ts`: new regression test pins the exact `2026-11-04`/afternoon-viewing
  case above (reverted the fix first, confirmed the test fails - the old code put the card in
  `in_progress` while `daysUntil()` said 8 days - then restored the fix, confirmed it passes, same
  discipline as every other pass).

Verified: `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/*.test.ts` 178/178 passed (including the new
regression test and every other existing `dispatchTriage.test.ts`/`dates.test.ts` case, none of
which sit near the midnight-vs-now boundary, so none broke from the signature change); `tsc --noEmit`
and `eslint` on all four touched files clean. Pushed directly to `main` (small, fully verified, no
PR/self-merge involved, per this routine's standing guardrail).

still not applied to the live DB; the `narrative_documents` PostgREST schema-cache reload; the

**2026-10-28 ~16:15 UTC — `confirm_pack.py` was silently dropping a key person's incomplete
project citations with zero trace, anywhere, violating this gate's own "refuses loudly, not
silently" docstring; fixed.**

`confirm_pack.py` only requires a person's first 3 projects (raw profile order) to have every
field `sanral_fill.py`'s filler needs (`client_type`, `project_type`, `position_code`,
`contact_number`) - intentional, documented behaviour, since a position's 3 Form B1 rows don't
need every project a person has ever done. A 4th-or-later project missing a field was dropped via
a bare `continue` - no print, no note, nothing written to the generated `pack.yaml` at all. Found
because `sanral_fill.projects_for_block()` (the function that actually decides which of a
person's projects fill a given position's 3 rows) picks **by project_type matching that
position's own Book 1 matrix, not by raw list order** - so a project dropped here for a missing
field could easily have been the one a *later* position's block actually needed, and that drop
had no trace anywhere (contrast: the project-type-mismatch case in `projects_for_block()` itself
already generates a user-facing note, "surfaced on the contents page, never silent" per
`assemble_pack.py`'s own comment - this one bypassed that path entirely, before the project ever
reached it).

Fix: record each such drop (person, project, missing fields) into a new
`pack['_provenance']['dropped_incomplete_projects']` list - same place/convention the file
already uses for AI-suggestion overrides - and print it to stdout the same way overrides are
printed. Doesn't change what gets filled (a project still needs a complete profile to be cited;
that's correct and unchanged); only makes the drop visible instead of invisible.

Verified with the revert-confirm-fail-restore-confirm-pass discipline: reverted the fix, ran a
synthetic 4-project person through `confirm()` - the 4th project vanished with nothing printed and
no `dropped_incomplete_projects` key in the output at all (confirmed bug); restored the fix, same
input - printed "1 project(s) dropped..." and `pack.yaml`'s `_provenance.dropped_incomplete_projects`
named the person and the missing fields. `py_compile` clean; no dedicated test file exists for
`confirm_pack.py` (noted previously, still true) - not adding one now would be inconsistent with
this session's own "verify properly" discipline, but a full test file is a larger lift than this
pass's scope; flagging that `confirm_pack.py` having zero dedicated tests (unlike `suggest_pack.py`,
which got one on 2026-10-21) is itself worth a future pass, not just this one finding.

**2026-10-28 — standing review pass, real bug fixed: `ownPosition()` could show an impossible
"rank past the field size" when the company's own bid was itself an outlier
(`app/lib/marketPricing.ts`).**

Picked `app/lib/marketPricing.ts` (523 lines - money-adjacent bid/award analysis logic, only 105
lines of test coverage and zero tests for `ownPosition()` specifically, the function that computes
"Rank X of Y" for the Market Intelligence pages) as this pass's under-reviewed candidate.

The bug: `columnField()` excludes any bid more than `OUTLIER_FACTOR` (5x) off the field's median from
`amounts`/`low`/`median`/`high` - correct, it's how a register's own typing errors are kept out of the
aggregate. But `ownPosition()`'s `rank`/`of` were both read off that same outlier-filtered
`field.amounts` with no account taken of whether the company's *own* price was itself one of the
excluded values. When it was, `of` (the field size) silently dropped the company from its own count
while `rank` (counted by `1 + amounts below price`) did not - producing a result like **"Rank 4 of
3"**, a contradiction (rank can't exceed the field size) that would have read as broken or confusing
on the Market Intelligence page for any company whose own submitted price happened to be a genuine
(if unusual) 5x-off-median outlier - a real, if not everyday, scenario: a fat-fingered price, or a
company legitimately bidding far outside the pack on a complex scope.

Fixed by confirming whether the company's own `price` is present in `field.amounts` (`ownCounted`)
and, when it isn't, adding the company back into `of` (`field.amounts.length + 1`) so rank and field
size are always self-consistent in both directions - a high-outlier price now correctly reads "last
of N+1", a low-outlier price "first of N+1", not "Nth of N" or "1st of N" undercounting the company's
own presence in the field.

Verified with the full revert-confirm-restore-confirm discipline: wrote two new tests in
`app/lib/marketPricing.spec.ts` (`describe("ownPosition", ...)`) reproducing the exact "rank 4 of 3"
case and the symmetric low-outlier undercount, confirmed both failed against the unfixed code
(`expected 4 to be not greater than 3` / `expected 3 to be 4`), applied the fix, confirmed both pass,
then ran the full app test suite (`npx vitest run`, 291/291 passing, 31/31 files) and `tsc --noEmit`
(clean) with no regressions. Committed and pushed directly to `main` (self-contained logic fix inside
one file plus its own new tests, no schema/API/behavioural surface beyond this function - no PR, per
this routine's convention).

No other open items touched this pass. Open PRs #164, #165, #169 are all still correctly
draft/unmerged (checked via `git fetch origin main` + `list_pull_requests` before starting - no new
self-merge, no file overlap with this change).

**2026-10-28 — standing review pass, clean sweep: Form B7 (Targeted Enterprise subcontracting)
plan-mode handling in `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py` + `engine/sanral_b7.py`, no real bug found.**

Picked `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py` (543 lines, the central SANRAL submission-pack orchestrator -
no dedicated `test_assemble_pack.py` exists) as an under-reviewed area for this pass. Traced a
hypothesis that `b7_filled = (b7_plan or {}).get("mode") == "subcontract" or (bool(legacy_te) and not
b7_plan)` (line 243) could let a third, uncaught `subcontracting_plan.mode` value fall through both
the "included" branch and `sanral_b7.applicability()`'s checks, silently omitting a required Form B7
with no warning.

Ruled out, end to end:
- `app/lib/sanralB7.ts:187` normalizes `mode` to only ever `"waived_by_tender"`, `"subcontract"`, or
  `null` before a plan is ever written to `tender_subcontracting_plans` - no third mode can reach this
  code path from the app at all.
- `sanral_b7.check_plan()` (line 155) has its own catch-all for a corrupted/unexpected mode
  (`f"unknown plan type '{mode}'"` as a hard error), and `assemble_pack.py` calls `check_plan()` and
  raises before `b7_filled` is ever computed when `b7_plan` is a non-empty dict - so a bad mode refuses
  the pack rather than silently omitting the form.
- The one real precedent for this exact class of bug - an explicit plan losing to the legacy
  `targeted_enterprise` block - was already found and fixed in the 2026-10-26 QA pass
  (`engine/fill_conventional.py`/`fill_tender.py`: `elif te and not td.get("subcontracting_plan")`,
  covered by `engine/test_fill_b7_legacy_precedence.py`). `assemble_pack.py`'s own `b7_filled`
  computation mirrors that same precedence rule exactly (`bool(legacy_te) and not b7_plan`) - confirmed
  consistent, not re-drifted.
- `engine/test_sanral_b7.py` (ALL PASSED) and `engine/test_fill_b7_legacy_precedence.py` (0 failures)
  both re-run clean against current `main` as part of this pass.

No code change made - a thorough look turned up nothing real here, so documenting the clean sweep
rather than forcing a weak finding. Verified via `git fetch origin main`: only #164 (savings-counter
rework) and #165 (4 pre-demo defects) open, both still correctly unmerged drafts - no self-merge this

**2026-10-28 ~06:25 UTC — standing review pass: a real, reachable bug fixed in `app/lib/workflowRegistry.ts`'s
`cronIntervalMs()` - the new `/admin/telemetry` page (Phase 6) was falsely flagging the perfectly-healthy
`corrigendum_alerts` workflow as "stale" every single morning and every weekend.** Orientation: `git fetch
origin main` confirmed local HEAD already matched `origin/main` at `a987198` (the CV `completed_at` fix from
the prior pass) - no new commits to catch up on. Two open PRs (`#164`, `#165`), both still draft/unmerged,
re-confirmed via the GitHub API; neither overlapped the file this pass touched. Re-confirmed (did not
re-flag as new) the already-known impersonation token-refresh gap by tracing the actual installed
`@supabase/auth-js` SDK source, and ruled out the "submitted-tender nagging" gap extending to the newer
Phase 6 digest scripts (`corrigendumAlerts.ts`, `clarificationWindowReminders.ts`, `complianceDigestCandidates.ts`,
`discoveredTendersDigest.ts` all correctly handle or correctly don't need pipeline-stage filtering) - neither
produced a new finding.

**The finding**: of the 10 `WORKFLOW_REGISTRY` entries backing the admin Telemetry page's health badges,
`corrigendum_alerts` is the only one with BOTH an hour-range restriction and a day-of-week restriction in its
cron (`"0 5-17/2 * * 1-5"`, business hours only, Mon-Fri) - and `cronIntervalMs()` computed only the literal
step size (2h), ignoring that this cron goes quiet overnight and over the weekend BY DESIGN. Reproduced live
with a Node script calling the real `heartbeatStatusFor()`: a perfectly healthy last-completed timestamp
(Friday's last run, or any weekday's last run the evening before) read as `"stale"` the following Monday
morning or the following morning respectively - the existing `workflowRegistry.spec.ts` suite never caught
this because it only exercises `compliance_digest` (once-daily) and `scout_alerts` (every-10-minutes), neither
of which has this combination of restrictions.

**First fix attempt was wrong, caught by this same pass's own verification before it shipped**: widening the
allowed gap to the worst case (the Friday-to-Monday span) and applying that one flat number everywhere fixed
the reported false positive, but silently broke the opposite way - a genuine 3-day mid-week outage (no
weekend involved) then also read as `"healthy"`, because the threshold had been sized for the worst case and
applied uniformly regardless of when in the week the gap actually fell. Caught by testing a mid-week negative
control (`Monday 17:00 last run → Thursday 12:00 now`, which should read `"stale"`) before considering the fix
done, per this routine's own "verify properly" discipline - not shipped with that flaw.

**Actual fix**: replaced the flat-interval model with one that sums only the cron's own *eligible* elapsed
time between the last completion and now (`eligibleElapsedMs()`), rather than raw wall-clock elapsed time -
nights/weekends outside the cron's window contribute zero regardless of how many fall in the gap, while every
in-window hour (one missed firing or three straight days of them) counts fully and accumulates normally
against the step-size threshold. This correctly fixes both directions at once. `cronIntervalMs()` was renamed
to `cronStepMs()` (now just the per-firing step size, not a worst-case gap) to match what it actually returns;
confirmed via grep that nothing else in the repo referenced the old name.

**Verified properly**: live-reproduced both the original false positive (weekend + overnight) and the
mid-week false negative my own first attempt would have shipped, confirmed the final fix resolves all of them
plus two more within-window sanity checks (a normal gap stays healthy, a single missed firing goes stale) -
six scenarios total, all correct. Added 5 new permanent regression tests to `workflowRegistry.spec.ts`
covering `corrigendum_alerts` specifically (none existed before this pass). `git stash`'d the source fix,
confirmed the two bug-reproducing tests fail with exactly the predicted wrong result (`"stale"` instead of
`"healthy"`) against the old code, restored the fix, confirmed all 13 tests in the file pass. Ran the full
suite afterward: 289/289 passing across all 31 spec files, no regressions. `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` both
clean on the touched files.

**Pushed directly to `main` - no PR, per the standing guardrail**: a pure-logic fix in one `.ts` file with
its own new, passing regression coverage, no schema change, no UI change needing visual review, no live-DB
mutation.

three reminder/digest senders - none filter out a tender a company has already marked submitted -
not fixed, flagged for Sarel's own call given it spans multiple pre-existing scripts, not one.**
Orientation: `git fetch origin main` showed 1 new commit since this routine's own last pass
(`db06ad3`) - `Finding 88` from a sibling QA routine (`engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py`'s
idempotency-claim ordering), unrelated, no overlap. Two open PRs (`#164` savings-counter rework

**The finding**: `scripts/send-returnables-digest.ts` (Phase 6, landed in the prior pass) queries
`tenders` joined to `tender_packs!inner(company_id)` with no `pipeline_stage` filter at all, then
checks only the 3-5 BUSINESS day closing window. A company can mark a tender `submitted` at any
time via the Pipeline board's own "Mark submitted" button (not gated by closing date - physical
hand-delivery days ahead of the deadline is a normal, real workflow this app explicitly supports) -
and `pipeline_stage` moving to `submitted` doesn't retroactively mark the company's own vault
documents/CSD/COID etc. as "have" in the system. So a company that already physically submitted
their bid 4 business days before closing, with the system's own compliance tracking still showing a
document gap, would still receive this digest's "you're missing mandatory returnables for this
tender" nudge - confusing and wrong once a tender is genuinely out the door. **Confirmed this isn't
unique to the new script, not invented in isolation**: `scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts` (the
"closing in 3/24 hours" reminder, pre-existing) has the exact same gap - same
`tender_packs!inner(company_id)` join, no `pipeline_stage` selected or filtered anywhere in that
file either. The only sender in this codebase that DOES filter closed stages is
`send-operational-alerts.ts`'s print-cutoff path, which separately fetches `pipeline_stage` per
candidate and runs it through `printCutoffCandidates()`'s own `CLOSED_STAGES` check
(`lib/printCutoffReminders.ts`) - that one deliberate guard exists, the other two senders never got
it.

**Why this stays a judgment call rather than a quick patch**: it's not a one-line fix in one place -
it's the same missing guard in (at least) two pre-existing sender scripts plus the brand-new one,
and the right fix shape is itself a real design decision: filter in the SQL query (`tender_packs`
join on `pipeline_stage not in (...)`, cheapest, but duplicates the stage list in three places) vs.
a shared helper both the query-row type and the candidate functions import (more consistent, but
touches `returnablesWindowCandidates()`'s and `deadlineReminderCandidates()`'s own already-tested
signatures). Fixing only the newest script would leave the older, already-live
`send-deadline-reminders.ts` with the identical bug still unaddressed, which reads as worse than
flagging both honestly together. Not reproduced against a live database (no live Supabase
credentials in this sandbox) - reasoned from the actual query/candidate-function code directly, which
is sufficient to establish the gap is real without needing a live run.

**2026-10-27 ~22:17 UTC — standing review pass: a real reliability gap found and traced to the SDK
source in the brand-new "View Tenant Workspace" impersonation feature (Admin Command Center Phase 4) -
not fixed, flagged for Sarel's own call given the complexity and no live Supabase credentials in this
sandbox to verify an end-to-end fix against.** Orientation: `git fetch origin main` showed 10 new
commits since this routine's own last pass (`18ac558`) - fast-forwarded cleanly, no stale-checkout
risk. The bulk of it is the huge Admin Command Center Phase 4-7 build-out (impersonation, billing,
telemetry, tender catalog, returnables digest) plus a new standing rule (above, this file's own top)
after a real live-database-cleanup incident Sarel caught and corrected directly - not this routine's
own incident, nothing for this pass to add to it beyond reading and respecting the new rule going
forward. Three open PRs (`#164`, `#165`, `#166` - the last of these is in fact what just landed as
Phase 4-7, already merged by the time this pass checked) re-confirmed via the GitHub API, not assumed;
stayed clear of the self-merge incident PRs per the standing guardrail.

**The finding, traced to the actual installed `@supabase/auth-js` source rather than guessed at**:
`lib/impersonation.ts`'s own header documents a 4-hour ceiling
(`IMPERSONATION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`) as the intended maximum length of an impersonation session, enforced
via the cookie's own `maxAge`. In practice the underlying Supabase session dies far sooner than that,
silently, with no clean fallback:

- `lib/supabase/server.ts`'s `createClient()` rebuilds a fresh impersonated client on every single
  request by calling `setSession({ access_token, refresh_token })` with the SAME two tokens read back
  from the cookie - the cookie itself is written exactly once, at mint time
  (`impersonation-actions.ts`'s `startImpersonation()`), and never updated again anywhere in the
  codebase (confirmed via `grep` across `middleware.ts` too - zero mentions of the impersonation cookie
  there).
- Read `node_modules/@supabase/auth-js/dist/module/GoTrueClient.js`'s own `_setSession()` directly
  (lines ~3033-3081): when the access token has expired, it calls `_callRefreshToken()` internally and
  returns a **refreshed session with a new access/refresh token pair** - this part works, and is
  presumably why 1-hour-ish Supabase access-token lifetimes don't break the very first refresh.
  Supabase's own refresh tokens rotate by default on use (the standard, documented Supabase Auth
  behaviour) - the old refresh token becomes invalid the moment the new one is issued. Since nothing in
  this codebase captures that refreshed pair and re-persists it into the cookie, the **next** request
  after the first refresh presents the now-already-rotated, now-invalid refresh token, which
  `_callRefreshToken()` will reject.
- Net effect: an admin's impersonated session can silently stop working well inside the documented
  4-hour window (as early as shortly after the first natural access-token expiry, commonly ~1 hour by
  Supabase default), with no clear "your impersonation session has ended, please restart" message - the
  client simply falls back to an unauthenticated/anonymous Supabase client for that request, which
  could surface as a confusing broken page or an unexplained empty state rather than the deliberate,
  honest failure messages this feature's other paths (`mintTargetSession()`, `startImpersonation()`)
  were clearly built to give.

**Not fixed this pass, and not a quick patch**: the correct fix needs the refreshed token pair captured
from `setSession()`'s own return value and re-persisted via `setImpersonationCookie()` - straightforward
from a Server Action or Route Handler, but `createClient()` is also called from plain Server Components
(this file's own existing comment already notes cookie writes are rejected there, which is exactly why
`middleware.ts` exists to refresh the ADMIN's own `sb-*` session cookies today) - the impersonation
cookie would need the same middleware-level treatment to stay correctly refreshed across every request
shape this app makes, not just Server Actions. That is real surface area in a security-sensitive,
brand-new path, and this sandbox has no live Supabase credentials to verify an end-to-end fix actually
works (refresh-token rotation behaviour can also be a per-project Supabase Auth setting, not purely a
code question) - documented in full here rather than guessed at or rushed. **Worth Sarel's own look**,
not urgent in the sense that no privilege escalation results (a dead session just goes anonymous, it
never silently grants the admin's own elevated rights or another user's session), but real enough that
a genuine diagnostic session longer than ~1 hour will likely break without warning.

**QA tooling**: sound - `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean (0 errors, same 3 pre-existing warnings).
No application code touched this pass (investigation + SDK source reading only).

  existence) - confirmed by reading `sanralConventionalDocumentChecks()` that experience/financial-
  capture/briefing/role data feeds only NON-mandatory items this digest never reports, so none of that

**Real finding, not a bug to silently work around**: SANRAL's own Form of Offer (C1.1.1) item is
*always* `status: "check"` by construction - confirmed by reading `sanralConventionalDocumentChecks()`,
`formFillNote()` can only ever return `null` or `"check"`, and the outer code does
`fill.status ?? "check"` - so it can never read `"have"`, whatever the data. This means every SANRAL
tender a company tracks will show "C1.1.1 Form of Offer, completed and signed" in this digest at least
once, every time it enters the window - a real, always-true fact (it genuinely always needs a human
signature, the same "Verify: Sign the Form of Offer" the live compliance report already shows forever
until signed), not a defect this digest introduces. Worth knowing before expecting a SANRAL company's
digest to ever come back empty-missing.

**Pre-existing real bug fixed in passing**: `lib/generalTender.ts` imported `"./dates"` and
`"./tenderCompliance"` with no file extension - fine for Next.js's bundler, but Node's own
`--experimental-strip-types` (every standalone `scripts/*.ts` sender uses this, no bundler) can't
resolve an extensionless relative specifier at all. Confirmed by actually running
`node --experimental-strip-types -e "import('./lib/generalTender.ts')"` before, which failed
(`Cannot find module '.../lib/dates'`), and after the fix, which succeeded. This module had never
been imported by a direct-node script before this digest - only by Next.js-bundled pages - so the bug
was real but latent. Fixed with `.ts` extensions, matching every other lib file already written this
way (`lib/tenderCompliance.ts`'s own imports, `lib/deadlineReminders.ts`'s own header comment on
exactly this constraint).

**2026-10-27 ~21:05 UTC — Admin Command Center, Phase 4: "View Tenant Workspace" impersonation +
immutable audit log, built under Sarel's own 5 explicit guardrails. Live-verified the one genuinely
novel, highest-risk mechanism (real session minting) against the live project using Sarel's own
test account; the DB-dependent half (audit logging, the banner) cannot be live-tested until
migrations land - see the status note below, which also applies to Phases 1-3.**

Design, in one sentence: the admin's own real sign-in (the `sb-*-auth-token` cookie(s)
@supabase/ssr already manages) is NEVER touched; a single SEPARATE cookie carries the TARGET
user's own session tokens, and `lib/supabase/server.ts`'s `createClient()` - the one function
nearly every Server Component/Action in this app already calls - prefers that session when the
cookie is present. Every existing page therefore renders exactly as the impersonated member would
see it, with zero per-page changes, and "Exit" is just deleting that one cookie - nothing to
"restore" because nothing else was ever overwritten. This is the first time the deployed Next.js
app itself needs the service-role key (confirmed by grepping the whole `app/` tree before building
- every other service-role caller is a GitHub Actions workflow or standalone script) - isolated
entirely inside the new `lib/impersonation.ts`, which never returns the key itself, only a
short-lived target-user session.

**Built and verified this pass** (`tsc --noEmit`/`eslint .`/`vitest run` 274/274/`npm run build`
clean after every step):
- Migration `0102`: `impersonation_audit_logs` (admin_user_id, target_company_id, target_user_id,
  a DENORMALISED target_company_name/target_user_email captured once at start so the banner never
  needs a live join, reason, started_at, ended_at - immutable except ended_at, which only the same
  admin can set once), `platform_admin_start_impersonation()` (resolves the target - the company's
  owner, else earliest member - and opens the row), `platform_admin_end_impersonation()` (closes
  it, idempotent).
- `lib/impersonation.ts`: the session-mint (`admin.generateLink` + `verifyOtp` two-step Auth API
  dance - supabase-js has no direct "sign in as" call), cookie read/write/clear helpers, and
  `impersonationConfigured()` so the UI hides the action entirely rather than offering a button
  that would fail, when no service-role key exists in an environment yet.
- `lib/supabase/server.ts`: `createClient()` now checks the impersonation cookie first and returns
  a client hydrated with the target session when present; `{ bypassImpersonation: true }` always
  returns the real admin's own session (used by the banner and both impersonation Server Actions
  themselves, which are inherently "real admin" operations).
- `app/_components/ImpersonationBanner.tsx`: the sticky amber banner (guardrail 2's exact wording),
  reading the REAL admin's session, never the swapped one. **Caught a real site-wide regression
  before shipping**: mounting this in the root layout (`app/layout.tsx`) forced every page in the
  app - including every public marketing/tool page (`/login`, `/signup`, `/privacy`,
  `/tools/*`, `/_not-found`) - out of static prerendering, because `cookies()` access anywhere in
  the root layout taints the whole tree. Fixed by moving it into `AppShell.tsx` instead (outside
  `SidebarProvider`, for true full-width-above-everything placement) - the right mounting point
  architecturally too (same place `SubscriptionBanner`/`DemoBanner` already live, and the one
  already-dynamic component every signed-in page, and only signed-in pages, renders through).
  Confirmed by re-running the build: every public page is back to `○` static, matching the
  pre-Phase-4 baseline exactly; nothing changed for the already-dynamic authenticated pages.
- `/admin/customers`: "View Tenant Workspace" button (guardrail 5) on both the row and the expanded
  drawer, hidden when impersonation isn't configured. Exit redirects to `/admin/customers?company=
  <id>` (guardrail 4 asked for `/admin/customers/[id]`, which does not exist in this codebase - the
  company detail view is the expand panel on the one listing page, not a separate route; adapted to
  land on that exact company's own context via a query param that auto-expands its row, same intent
  as the brief, no fabricated route).
- **Live-verified the session-mint mechanism** against the real project (Sarel's own Clevapp test
  account, `sareljvr101@gmail.com` - confirmed as the account owner via the Auth Admin API before
  using it): `generateLink` + `verifyOtp` produced a real access/refresh token pair for exactly the

**2026-10-27 ~20:40 UTC — fixed the recurring "SANRAL page could not be read (404)"
system_alerts noise: root cause was a seeded DEMO/fixture tender, not a dead real tender,
a URL bug, or a SANRAL site-scheme change.** Diagnosed on Sarel's own direct request (SANRAL
is the company's primary launch wedge, so this got a real investigation, not a guess).

**Root cause, confirmed against the live database**: the pursued tender behind the alert
(`contract_no` `N.007-030-2026/1F`) has `slug` `demo-n7-section-3-2026-1f` and `source`
`sanral` - traced to `engine/seed_demo_company.py`'s own `TENDER_SLUGS` fixture list (one of
3 sales-demo tenders seeded for the shared "Mzansi Roads & Civils (Pty) Ltd" demo account).
Its slug was never a real page on `nra.co.za` - `detail.fetch_detail()` correctly 404s
fetching `https://www.nra.co.za/open-tenders/demo-n7-section-3-2026-1f`, because that page
never existed. `watch_tender_updates.py`'s "actively pursued" query has no exclusion for a
demo/fixture tender, so it retried this doomed fetch every 2 hours, forever, logging a real
`system_alerts` error indistinguishable from a genuine page-read failure on an actual pursued
tender each time.

**Fixed**: `engine/discovery/watch_tender_updates.py` - added `DEMO_SLUG_PREFIX = "demo-"`
(matching `seed_demo_company.py`'s own naming convention for every fixture slug it seeds,
confirmed none of SANRAL's real slugs use this prefix - they look like `r-343-020-2025-1f`,
per `detail.py`'s own docstring example) and an early guard in `check_tender()` that skips a
demo-slug tender with a clean, visible log line and `last_error = null` in
`tender_watch_state` - never a silent swallow, and never attempting the live fetch at all.
A genuine SANRAL page-read failure on a real tender still raises `system_alerts` exactly as
before - only the demo fixture is excluded. 4 new checks added to
`engine/discovery/test_tender_updates.py` (Part 0): the demo tender returns no updates and
never calls `fetch_sanral`, no alert is raised, its watch state records a clean check, and a
real (non-demo) SANRAL slug is still fetched normally. Full existing suite (Parts 1/2/2b) still
passes. Verified live: re-ran `watch_tender_updates.py` against the real Supabase project -
the 404 is gone, replaced by a clean one-line skip.

**Flagged, not fixed in this pass (a product call, not a bug)**: two REAL (non-test) companies
- "Tender Ready" and "Reviewer Civils & Consulting Pty Ltd" - are also pursuing this same demo
fixture tender via their own `tender_packs` rows (`is_test_company = false` on both), likely

**2026-10-27 ~18:16 UTC — standing review pass: Form B7's SETUP sheet carries two
disagreeing subcontracting signals, confirmed disagreeing on a real committed sample -
flagged for Sarel's own call, not fixed (compliance-critical, needs a reconciliation
decision, not a guess).** Orientation: `git fetch origin main` showed no new commits since
this routine's own last pass (`15f9e9c`) - local checkout already matched. Three open PRs
(`#164` savings-counter rework, `#165` four pre-demo defect fixes, `#166` notification
migration + Admin Command Center) read in full via the GitHub API - all correctly still
draft/unmerged, none overlapping `engine/sanral_b7.py` or anything this pass touched.
Stayed clear of the self-merge incident PRs, as directed.

**The finding.** `engine/sanral_b7.py`'s `read_setup()` reads two separate signals off the
Technical Submission workbook's own SETUP sheet: `L1` ("App. D Category of Tender") plus a
policy matrix (`J27:L35`) that together drive `applicability()`'s category+company-size
subcontracting answer, AND `L2` - labelled, in SANRAL's own template, literally
`"Subcontracting Compulsary:"` (their spelling) - a direct YES/NO the buyer states for that
specific tender. `read_setup()` already parses `L2` into a `compulsory` field on the dict it
returns (`str(wb.cached("SETUP", "L2") or "").strip().upper() or None`) - but nothing in this
file, or either of its two callers (`engine/pack/assemble_pack.py`,
`engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`), ever reads that field again. It's computed and
discarded. Confirmed this isn't a hypothetical edge case: read `SETUP!L2` directly off all 6
committed real samples (`templates/samples/*_ran.xlsm`) -

| Sample | Category (L1) | Matrix says, Generic tenderer | `SETUP!L2` "Subcontracting Compulsary" |
|---|---|---|---|
| R.334-030-2025.1F | 2 | **required** | **NO** |
| R.343-020-2025.1F | 3 | required | YES |
| R.352-020-2025.1F | 3 | required | YES |
| R.352-030-2025.1F | 3 | required | YES |
| R.394-010-2025.1F | 3 | required | YES |
| R.396-010-2025.1F | 3 | required | YES |

R.334 is a real, live disagreement: the category/matrix path (what the product actually
tells a Generic-sized company today) says B7 is **required**, while SANRAL's own template
states on the same sheet, in plain words, that subcontracting is **not compulsory** for this
exact tender. A company reading `applicability()`'s `"required"` reason today would be told
to complete a form SANRAL's own document says it doesn't need to - real wasted effort on a
compliance document, and the kind of "two writers that could disagree" shape this codebase
already treats as a hard rule to avoid elsewhere (0043's cross-tenant trigger, this same
file's own Book-1-waiver path for `R.396`).

**Why this isn't fixed in this pass, not just documented as a shortcut.** The right
reconciliation isn't obvious enough to guess at silently on a compliance gate that already
exists specifically to never guess (`applicability()`'s whole design is "ask, don't skip"
the moment anything is unknown). Candidates worth Sarel's own call, not mine: (a) treat `L2`
as authoritative over the matrix when they disagree - but it's unclear whether `L2` is
genuinely tender-specific or just echoes the category's own "Generic" row of the matrix
verbatim, which would make it redundant rather than an override in the 5 category-3 samples
and only meaningfully informative in the one category-2 sample where it disagrees; (b) treat
a disagreement as its own `"unknown"`-shaped outcome (same "required until you answer"
posture the module already uses for a missing category or company size), surfacing both
readings in the reason text; (c) leave the matrix as authoritative and treat `L2` as a
documented cross-check only shown to the user, never driving the actual required/not_required
split. Not picking one of these without Sarel's steer, given a wrong guess here either makes
a company jump through an unneeded hoop or - worse - tells them a required compliance form
isn't needed.

`ALL PASSED`; this pass made no code changes, so nothing to regress. `tsc`/`eslint` unaffected

narrower `fixCount`, built from `classifyComplianceItem()`/`bidTaskStatus === "fix"` specifically -

extraction doesn't change `DisqualificationGuard()`'s own rendered output, and wiring it into the

**2026-10-27 ~00:14 UTC — standing review pass: a real, already-occurring fingerprint blind spot
fixed in `engine/fingerprint.py`'s `named_ranges()` - confirmed in the real committed baseline, not
hypothetical.** Orientation: `git fetch origin main` showed no new commits since this routine's own
last pass (`023a8f7`) - local HEAD matched `origin/main` exactly. Two open PRs (`#164` savings-counter
rework, `#165` four pre-demo production defect fixes) read in full and confirmed correctly left as
unmerged drafts, neither touching anything this pass reviewed.

**The finding**: `named_ranges()` built its dict as `{d.get("name"): "".join(d.itertext()) for d in dn}`
over every `<definedName>` in the workbook. Excel auto-creates a SHEET-SCOPED defined name
(`localSheetId` attribute set) the moment any sheet ever has its own print area set - `_xlnm.Print_Area`
being the standard example - so a multi-sheet workbook very normally carries several entries that all
share the exact same `name` but genuinely different ranges, one per sheet. The plain-name-keyed dict
comprehension silently collapsed all of them down to whichever one iterated last, discarding every
other sheet's own value entirely before it ever reached the stored fingerprint - directly against this
module's own one stated job ("refuses to proceed silently on any mismatch," Sarel's own rule, quoted
in this file's own header). **Not hypothetical**: the real committed baseline
(`fingerprints/Conventional_Consultant_Tender.json`) already shows exactly one `_xlnm.Print_Area`
entry despite this being SANRAL's genuinely multi-sheet Conventional Consultant Tender workbook -
confirmed directly by reading that file, not assumed. Reproduced further with a minimal synthetic
`.xlsm` built in-memory (two sheets, each with its own `_xlnm.Print_Area`): `named_ranges()` returned
exactly 1 key instead of 2, and a `diff()` comparison with one sheet's print area changed and the
other's unchanged showed **no difference at all** under the old code - the exact silent-miss this
module exists to prevent.

**The fix**: a sheet-scoped name is now keyed as `"name#sheetN"` (using its own `localSheetId`), so
same-named entries from different sheets no longer collide; a workbook-scoped name (no `localSheetId`)
keeps its bare name, unchanged from before - confirmed the one other real entry in the committed
baseline (`MarkupCost`, workbook-scoped) round-trips identically. Verified properly: reverted the fix
first (`git stash`) and confirmed the new test fails with the exact predicted result (3 of 6 cases),
restored and confirmed all 6 pass. Grepped the rest of the codebase for any other reader of
`named_ranges()`'s output keyed by a specific name - none exists; it's only ever compared as a whole
dict inside `diff()`, so this is a safe, self-contained change.

**New test file added, since none existed for this module at all**: `engine/test_fingerprint.py` (6
cases - the collision reproduction, a workbook-scoped name staying unchanged, an empty
`<definedNames>`, and a direct `diff()` check that a single sheet's own change is now actually
caught). Registered as its own step in `bridge-worker-ci.yml`, matching this repo's existing
one-step-per-test-file convention - it was not previously discovered by anything automatic.

**Real, honest operational consequence - not silently absorbed**: the next real SANRAL Conventional
Consultant Tender processed will very likely show a `named_ranges` **mismatch** against the existing
committed baseline, purely because the baseline was computed with the old under-counting logic and
now genuinely carries fewer keys than a correct re-computation would. This is the fingerprint check
working as designed - Sarel's own rule is that any mismatch stops the pack run and needs a person to
check and update the baseline - but it's worth knowing in advance that this specific mismatch, when it
shows up, is this fix surfacing previously-hidden sheets' own print areas for the first time, not a
sign the real template itself changed. A fresh, correct baseline can be regenerated at that point by
deleting the stored file and letting the next run's "no baseline yet" path re-seed it (same as any
other legitimate baseline update) - **not done here**, since this sandbox has no live tender to
fingerprint against, and overwriting the one real committed baseline from a synthetic test would
replace real data with fabricated data.

**Pushed directly to `main`, no PR**: `engine/fingerprint.py`, `engine/test_fingerprint.py`,
`.github/workflows/bridge-worker-ci.yml`, this file.

**QA tooling**: sound - `py_compile` clean on both Python files touched, `engine/test_fingerprint.py`

floating widget built a broken link whenever the configured number had any formatting), QA sound,

**The bug**: the floating `WhatsAppContactButton` (`components/public/whatsapp-contact-button.tsx`,
landed via the self-merged PRs #160-162) and the home page's own footer WhatsApp link (`app/page.tsx`)
both read the same `NEXT_PUBLIC_WHATSAPP_NUMBER` env var, but only the footer link's code stripped
it to digits-only (`number.replace(/\D/g, "")`) before building the `wa.me/` URL - the floating
widget used the raw env-var string directly. A phone number typed into an env var with its natural
formatting ("+27 82 123 4567" - spaces and a leading "+", exactly how a person would type it) would

link to the *same number* worked correctly - confirmed directly (not assumed) by constructing both
URLs side by side with a realistic formatted value. Found by comparing the two call sites of the
same env var directly against each other, since neither one in isolation reads as wrong.

**Fix**: `whatsapp-contact-button.tsx` now strips to digits the same way `app/page.tsx` already
does - one source of sanitization logic duplicated correctly instead of one correct and one
missing, rather than extracting a shared helper for a two-line regex. Verified: `tsc --noEmit`/
`eslint` clean on the changed file, full `npx vitest run` 202/202 unchanged (no existing coverage of
this component to begin with - a real gap worth a future pass, not built here to stay scoped), and
the before/after URL construction demonstrated directly with a realistic formatted number.

(dashboard/onboarding fixes, draft), `#157` (pack bridge test-only additions, draft), `#118`

**The finding**: `app/lib/sanralScoring.ts` (341 lines) - the engine behind "does this bid clear
SANRAL's functionality threshold", shown live on `/tools/b6-estimator` and the tender workspace's
own compliance report (`compliance-data.ts`, `compliance-report.tsx`) - has **zero test coverage,
direct or indirect**. Confirmed by searching every actual caller (`compliance-data.ts`,
`compliance-report.tsx`, `B6EstimatorClient.tsx`, `tenderCompliance.ts`) and finding no test file
for any of them either. This is real money/bid-decision logic - a wrong `outlook` ("clears" /
"cannot_clear" / "depends") reaching a customer is a materially different risk than a cosmetic UI
bug, and nothing here would catch a regression.

Read the whole file looking for a concrete bug to fix rather than just reporting the coverage gap,
and found one genuine correctness question, but couldn't establish it's actually reachable: when
more than 6 key positions have an unknown SANRAL "managerial" flag (`estimateSanralConventional`'s
own `unknownIdx`), the code deliberately stops brute-forcing all `2^n` combinations and checks only
"all managerial" vs "all non-managerial" as the two bounds (`scenarios = ... <= 6 ? 1 << n : 2`).
Because making a position managerial changes both the numerator (adds `manPos`, which can be 0) and
the denominator (`managementMax` 15→30) together, the true min/max of the ratio isn't guaranteed to
sit at either all-same extreme - a mixed combination could in principle score more extreme than
both. **Not fixed**: `MAN_POSITION_COLUMNS` (PL/CE/RE/RM + toll equivalents, the only codes that can
even be managerial) means this needs more than 6 of specifically those position types on one
tender's Form B1 to ever engage the >6 branch at all - real SANRAL tenders this repo has templates
for run one PL plus a handful of DS-class (never-managerial) specialists, so this is very unlikely
to be reachable in practice. Noted here rather than built around a case I can't demonstrate actually
happens, and rather than silently left for the next pass to rediscover.

**Not acted on this pass**: writing the missing test suite itself - this needs real SANRAL matrix
fixtures (multiple positions, multiple projects, both managerial-known and -unknown cases) built
carefully against the actual Book 1 source the file's own header cites, not assembled quickly as a
light-touch pass's afterthought. A solid candidate for either a dedicated follow-up or the Edge-case
QA routine's own rotation.

**2026-10-26 ~14:33 UTC — standing review pass: fixed a false "Ready" claim in
`engine/general/submission_plan.py`'s `compile_plan()` for a CIDB grading requirement - scoped to
the Python module, verified NOT reachable from the deployed app, which already handles this
correctly.** Orientation: `git fetch origin main` showed 16 new commits since this routine's own
last pass (`af59b6d`) - the big one being PR #156 (Tender Workspace: RequirementRow wiring,
contradictory-badge fixes, confidence %, cover-page print, buyer pill), merged with zero reviews
(`get_reviews` returned `[]` - a further self-merge instance, not investigated or reverted per the
standing guardrail, same as every other one this file already documents). Also landed: Finding 80
(`build_world_bank()` printing the literal word "None"), and a System Admin Command Center feature
that was reverted once and reapplied as its own split PR. Three open PRs checked and avoided: `#159`
(dashboard/onboarding fixes, draft), `#157` (pack bridge test-only additions, draft), `#118`
(discovery scoring, draft, stale) - none collided with this pass's own work.

**The finding**: `compile_plan()`'s returnables loop produces a generic "CIDB registration /
grading" step for the `cidb` returnable (keyword match on the bare word "CIDB" anywhere in the
text) *in addition to* the dedicated `cidb_grading` step (triggered when a specific grading number,
e.g. "7GB", is actually found) - and in practice these fire together almost every time a specific
grading is named, since the grading sentence itself contains the word "CIDB". The generic step's
own status logic only ever asked "does the company have ANY grading on file at all", marking it
**"ready" the moment any grading exists - even one well below what's required**. Reproduced live
with the test suite's own existing SBD_BUNDLE fixture (company has 5GB on file, tender requires
7GB+): the dedicated step correctly showed `review - "confirm this actually meets or exceeds 7GB"`,
while the generic step simultaneously showed **`ready - "Company CIDB grading on file: 5GB."`** -
genuinely contradictory, false-confidence information about the exact same fact, sorted near the
bottom of the plan (where "ready" items sit) where a skimming user would read it as resolved.

**Important correction made before claiming user-facing impact, not assumed**: `compile_plan()` is
NOT reachable from the deployed Next.js app - confirmed by reading `submission-plan-logic.ts`'s own
header comment and the architecture decision it cites (2026-10-21, already recorded in this file):
every "read the manifest, classify it" screen computes fresh in TypeScript against the
already-stored manifest, never by calling this Python module live. The live TS port
(`submission-plan-data.ts` + `generalTender.ts`'s `checkReturnable()`) keeps the CIDB returnable
(**"is a document on file for this tender"**) and the CIDB grading-comparison step (**"does the
grading actually meet the requirement"**) as two *deliberately* separate concerns -
`checkReturnable()`'s own "cidb" case only ever says "CIDB grading X on file" / "attach the
certificate", never "meets the requirement" or "ready" in the misleading sense this Python bug
produced. Confirmed directly by reading both files, not inferred. So this is a real conflation bug
in the Python reference implementation (the one other code is explicitly documented as being
*ported from*, and the one a local CLI dry run exercises), not a live, user-facing one - worth
having fixed for that reason, but not reported as more impactful than it actually is.

**The fix**: the generic "cidb" returnable step is now skipped when `manifest.get("cidb")` is
truthy (a specific grading was found) - the dedicated step is strictly more informative in that
case (names the actual grading, never claims "ready" without a human confirming the comparison) and
wins; the generic step still shows on its own when only a bare "CIDB" mention exists with no
specific number to anchor a dedicated step. Two new regression cases added to
`test_submission_plan.py` (one per branch); reverted the fix first to confirm the new case fails
with the exact predicted result (16 steps, both present) before restoring it (15 steps, only the
dedicated one) - full suite re-run clean (`python3 engine/general/test_submission_plan.py`), plus
`test_requirements.py`, `test_process_general_jobs.py`, `test_general_bridge.py` (all unaffected,
confirmed clean) and `tsc`/`eslint` (no TypeScript touched).

**Pushed directly to `main`, no PR, no self-merge**: `engine/general/submission_plan.py`,
`engine/general/test_submission_plan.py`.

**Backlog re-confirmed, not re-verified live this pass** (unchanged from last pass): migration

**2026-10-26 ~12:00 UTC — PR #156: 6 of 7 targeted review fixes pushed (commit `7c8a21f`), re-tested
against real tenders GG12700238 and N.007-030-2026/1F; 1 fix explicitly not done, for a stated reason.**
A relayed review (claimed to be Sarel's own, against the Vercel preview of PR #156 - the tender-
workspace wire-up pass) listed 7 fixes to make before approval, with explicit constraints: no rewrite,
no splitting admin work out again, don't touch migration 0098. Verified the premise before acting on
it (per this file's own standing "weigh, don't blindly trust" rule for cross-session/relayed input) -
each of the 7 findings was independently re-derived from the actual code, not taken on faith:

1. **Cross-tab anchor links didn't switch tabs** - confirmed root cause: `next/link`'s `<Link href="#x">`
   navigates via `history.pushState`, which never fires the native `hashchange` event
   `workspace-tabs.tsx`'s `WorkspaceTabs` listens for to switch tabs (a real, well-known Next.js/browser
   quirk, not a guess - a plain `<a href="#x">` fires it correctly, and both styles already coexisted in
   this codebase). Found 2 same-page `<Link>` hash jumps in `general-workspace.tsx` and 3 more dynamic
   ones (`fixHref`/`changeHref`, which mix same-page hashes like `#tender-templates`/`#form-b7`/
   `#key-positions` with real cross-page paths like `/company#bee-cidb` in the same field) in
   `compliance-report.tsx`, `pack-review.tsx`, `general-pack-review.tsx`. Fixed with plain `<a>` for the
   first case and a new `HashAwareLink` helper (`app/app/tenders/[id]/hash-aware-link.tsx`) for the
   mixed case - picks `<a>` for a same-page hash, `<Link>` for a real route. Tested (`hash-aware-link.spec.ts`).
2. **Misleading blocked-document flow** - for a general-family tender with no manifest read yet, "Team &
   CVs" could render completely empty (`generalSections.people` was a bare `null`, and nothing else fills
   that tab for a general-family tender) - now explains why and points at Overview's read-documents
   action. Separately, a manifest where every document came back `unreadable` gave a dead-end "No
   supporting documents named in the readable text" with zero indication anything had gone wrong - now
   names the real reason and offers "Try reading the documents again" (+ an upload pointer for a shared
   tender).
3. **Deadline/countdown math wasn't actually shared** - `app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx` carried its own
   independently-drifted local copies of `lib/dates.ts`'s exported `closingCountdown()` (missing the
   remaining-hours breakdown the shared one has) and `daysUntil()` (as a locally-defined `taskDaysLeft()`,
   byte-for-byte the same logic under a different name) - both deleted in favour of the one shared,
   tested implementation. Added direct `daysUntil()` coverage (date-only/already-overdue matrix) to
   `lib/dates.test.ts`, which previously only tested `closingCountdown()`.
4. **No day-before physical-submission planning detail** - the print+transit buffer collapsed into one
   opaque "Hard target" number in `SubmissionModeBadge`. Added `departureDeadline()` to
   `lib/dispatchTriage.ts` (closing minus transit only, tested) so the badge can show 3 sequential,
   labelled steps instead of one. The 4h/2h hour defaults (`0090_submission_logistics.sql`'s own column
   defaults) are now explicitly labelled "editable planning defaults... not verified facts" in both the
   badge and the logistics form; a missing delivery address or courier contact now warns explicitly in
   both places too.
5. **Status vocabulary conflated unlike things** - real, provable bug:
   `0002_field_provenance.sql`'s own table comment defines `"confirmed"` as "a human entered/approved
   it" and `"computed"` as "derived mechanically... no judgment call" - opposites - but
   `pack-review-logic.ts`'s `PROVENANCE_STATUS_MAP` mapped both to the same ReviewStatus `"confirmed"`,
   silently feeding `tender-readiness.ts`'s "confirmed" count/score from mechanically-derived values
   nobody ever looked at, directly contradicting that file's own doc comment ("only true when the
   underlying ReviewStatus is literally confirmed"). Fixed: `"computed"` now maps to `"assumed_default"`
   (same Fix/Provide/Verify bucket, excluded from the confirmed count). Separately, removed "Attendance
   at the compulsory briefing session" as a document-style compliance chip in `tenderCompliance.ts` (an
   action, already tracked correctly as a real `tender_tasks` row with its own status/due date) -
   replaced with a one-line pointer to Tasks & milestones in `compliance-report.tsx`.
6. **Fake personnel matches shown as SUGGESTED** - `lib/positionSuggestions.ts`'s `suggestForPosition()`
   handed back the top-ranked candidate regardless of evidence; a person with no ECSA level, no years'
   experience and no matched keyword could be labelled "SUGGESTED" with its own reason reading "no
   matching or conflicting evidence on file" - a real name dressed up as a real match.
   `score_candidate()`'s score is an open-ended, no-floor integer, so 0/negative is a real, reachable
   case, not an edge case to dismiss. Fixed: such candidates are now excluded from
   `suggestion`/`alternatives` entirely (new `noSuitableCandidate: boolean`, tested in
   `positionSuggestions.spec.ts`); the UI shows "No suitable candidate identified" and manual selection
   stays available in the ordinary dropdown.

**Also done, not one of the 7 but the same pass**: trimmed one always-visible 3-sentence compliance
explainer (`compliance-report.tsx`) to a one-line summary + expandable `Tooltip`, matching

**Not done - methodology reference-document upload, and why.** The 7th finding asked for a reference-
document upload for the methodology-statement generator, "using the existing document/extraction

raw extracted document text anywhere a Next.js server action could read it back synchronously. Building
real AI-side consumption of an uploaded reference document would require either a new engine-side job
(Python, outside what this pass could safely write and test) or a new Next.js dependency (which is
itself a new mechanism, not "the existing one"). Did not ship a half-wired upload button that stores a
file the generation call never actually reads - flagged honestly in the PR body instead, with the
concrete reason, so it reads as a known gap rather than a silent drop.

**2026-10-26 ~10:20 UTC — standing review pass: a real dedupe bug fixed in `system_alerts.fingerprint()`
- two occurrences of the identical underlying failure, differing only by a Python object's
non-deterministic memory address, were silently filed as two separate open alerts instead of one.**
Orientation: `git fetch origin main` showed one new commit since the last pass (`5ea9dc6`, a sibling
QA routine's Finding 79 in `engine/general/submission_plan.py` - unrelated area, no overlap; note in
passing, not acted on: that pass's own `System-Status.md` entry landed mid-file rather than at the
top, breaking this file's own reverse-chronological convention - flagging for whoever runs that
routine next, not fixing someone else's file-editing habit myself). Three open PRs checked and
avoided entirely: `#157` (draft, test-only additions to `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py` - the
exact file this routine's own prior pass just edited, so deliberately steered clear of that file this
pass to avoid treading on it), `#156` (draft, notification-engine session's tender-workspace wire-up),
`#118` (draft, stale). Stayed clear of the self-merge incident PRs, per the standing guardrail.

**The finding**: `system_alerts.py`'s own `fingerprint()` function exists specifically so "ids, hex
strings and numbers [are] blanked out" before hashing, meaning two occurrences of the same
underlying failure collapse into one open alert with an incrementing occurrence count rather than
flooding `/admin` with duplicate rows. Read `_UUID`/`_HEX`/`_NUM`'s own regexes closely rather than
trusting the docstring's claim: `_HEX = re.compile(r"\b[0-9a-f]{12,}\b", re.I)` requires a word
boundary (`\b`) immediately before the first hex digit - but a Python object repr's own "0x..." memory
address (routinely the tail of a bridge's stdout/stderr when an exception's `str()` includes an object
repr, e.g. `<Workbook object at 0x7f8a3c2d1e40>`) has no such boundary: "x" and the hex digit that
follows it are both `\w` characters, so `\b` never matches between them. The hex run falls through
`_HEX` entirely and lands on `_NUM` instead, which only blanks the pure-digit substrings inside it
(`0`, `7`, `8`, `3`, `2`, `1`, `40` individually) and leaves every hex letter in place - a result that
differs from one process run to the next, since the memory address itself does. Reproduced directly
(not theorised): `fingerprint("pack", "...at 0x7f8a3c2d1e40...")` and the same message with
`0x55b19a001230` substituted in produced two different sha256 hashes, confirming two occurrences of
the exact same failure would file as two separate `system_alerts` rows rather than one row with
`occurrences: 2` - the opposite of this function's own stated purpose, and exactly the kind of alert-
noise problem Sarel's own recent asks (PR #151's anti-noise batching, PR #152's per-bridge source
tagging) were built to reduce.

**Fix**: added `\b0x[0-9a-f]+\b` as a first alternative in `_HEX`, ahead of the existing bare-hex
pattern - it matches the "0x" prefix as part of the hex run itself, so the match no longer needs a
word boundary between "x" and the digits after it. Verified: added a regression case to
`engine/alerts/test_system_alerts.py`'s own `fingerprint()` check block - confirmed it failed with the
exact predicted result before the fix (two different hashes for the same underlying message), then
confirmed it passes after. Full `python3 engine/alerts/test_system_alerts.py` (Part 1, the in-memory
Supabase stand-in - real bridges fed malformed jobs, the checker's new/still-occurring/resolved
lifecycle) re-run clean, 0 failures, every pre-existing case included - this fix touches only the
regex, nothing about dedup behaviour on UUIDs or plain numbers changed. `py_compile` clean on both
touched files.

**Pushed directly to main, no PR**: `engine/alerts/system_alerts.py`,
`engine/alerts/test_system_alerts.py` - commit (see `git log`).

entirely clear of the self-merge incident PRs, as directed.

**What was chased, and why it looked like a real bug at first:** `engine/general/fill_flat_pdf.py`
(the flat/non-fillable municipal MBD-form filler - 1002 lines, confirmed via grep to have zero
dedicated test file, unlike every other filler in this engine) writes a value into a form cell two
different ways depending on whether the buyer's own template already pre-prints the field's
"prefix" (`"MAAA"` for a CSD supplier number, `"R"` for the bid price): if the target cell is
genuinely blank, it writes the raw `value` straight in with no prefix logic at all; only when the
cell already shows the prefix printed does it strip a matching prefix off `value` first (so the
written text doesn't duplicate it, e.g. "MAAAMAAA0999999"). The blank-cell path writing a bare,
unprefixed `value` looked like a real bug on first read - MBD 1's CSD cell with no pre-printed
"MAAA" would then show just the bare number, missing the required "MAAA" prefix altogether.

**Confirmed NOT a bug, by checking how these values are actually stored**, not by assumption: grepped
every write site for `csd_supplier_number` (seed data, migration `0001`, test fixtures,
`fill_sbd_docx.py`, `fill_a_forms.py`) - every single one stores/passes it **with** "MAAA" already
baked into the string (`"MAAA0999999"`, `"MAAA0123456"`, never a bare digit string). Same for
`total_bid_price` (`tender_answers`, per migration `0077`'s own comment, and this engine's own test
fixtures: `"R 1 000 000.00"`, `"R 98 765.43"` - the user types the "R" themselves when answering).
So the blank-cell path writing `value` as-is is correct (the prefix is already part of the string),
and the pre-printed-prefix path's `value.upper().startswith(pre.upper())` strip is the one genuinely
needed to avoid a doubled prefix when the template already shows it. Also traced the phone-number
cell-splitting regex (`^\s*\(?(0\d{2})\)?[\s-]*(.+)$`, assumes a domestic `0XX` area code) - a stored
number not matching that shape (e.g. an international format) correctly falls back to writing the
whole value into one cell rather than crashing or writing a malformed split.

**Real gap flagged, not built this pass**: `fill_flat_pdf.py` and `fill_sbd_docx.py` (547 lines, the
SBD/MBD `.docx`-native equivalent) both have **zero dedicated test files** - confirmed via grep,
neither is imported by any `test_*.py` in this engine. Both are only exercised indirectly through
`test_general_bridge.py`'s end-to-end fixture runs, which cover the happy path but not the
prefix/phone-splitting edge cases traced above. A real candidate for the Edge-case QA routine's
rotation, alongside the already-flagged `confirm_pack.py`/`process_pack_jobs.py` coverage gap from
two passes ago.

**The finding, reproduced live before touching anything**: `boq_extraction.py`'s
`MIN_NUMERIC_QUANTITY_RATIO` sheet-acceptance check required a majority of a sheet's matched rows
to have a parseable numeric **quantity**, specifically, or the whole sheet (and everything in it)
was discarded with a note calling it a "coincidental header match." A real, extremely common SA
tender shape - a Preliminaries & General bill, or some smaller tenders' entire priced schedule,
made up of lump-sum lines ("Allow a lump sum for site establishment") with a real rand Amount and
no Quantity/Rate at all (quantity is implicitly 1, left blank in the buyer's own template) - fails
that check at 0% every time, even though every row carries a genuine, non-zero rand value.
Reproduced directly: a synthetic P&G sheet (4 lines, real descriptions, real amounts of
R85,000/R220,000/R45,000/R18,000, no quantity column populated) came back with **0 items** and a
note actively mischaracterising it as a coincidental match. This silently drops a genuine priced
schedule from `tender_scope_records.boq_summary` - the exact market-intelligence data this module
exists to surface.

**Fix, kept deliberately narrow**: the sheet-acceptance check now also passes when a majority of
matched rows have a real, **non-zero** rate or amount, even with no quantity. Deliberately NOT
widened to "any numeric field at all" - the sibling false-positive case this module already
protects against (a returnables checklist whose "Quantity" column reads Yes/No/Unclear) has a
literal `0` placed in its own Amount column for every row in the existing test fixture, and a
uniform zero is itself the signal that it isn't real pricing; checking non-zero specifically keeps
that protection intact. Verified properly, not just read: reverted the fix first, confirmed the new
test (`test_all_lump_sum_preliminaries_bill_is_not_rejected`) fails with the exact predicted `0
items` result; restored, confirmed the full `test_boq_extraction.py` suite green (16 checks, 0
failures) including every pre-existing false-positive-rejection test unchanged; `test_tender_
enrichment.py` (the one real caller) also still clean.

date-shaped field (`expiry_date`, `letter_date`, `completion_date`) through `normalise_date()`. When
that function can't parse the value at all (returns `iso=None` - as opposed to a low-precision but
parseable year/month-only value, which is already handled and tested), the field falls through to
the generic "drop it if the value is None" branch at the bottom of the loop - silently discarding not
just the field, but the warning `normalise_date()` itself generated explaining *why* ("isn't a date
that could be read; enter it by hand"). Reproduced directly: a CIDB registration whose expiry field
read "see addendum" (a real, plausible value an AI extraction could return for a document that
defers its own expiry to an attached addendum) came back with `expiry_date` simply absent from
`fields` and **zero warnings anywhere, document-level included** - indistinguishable, from the
reviewer's side, from the document never mentioning an expiry date at all. Every *other* "couldn't
determine X" case in this same function (the id_document "no valid SA ID number found" branch) already
surfaces through `overall` (the document-level warnings list shown in the review UI); this one
silently didn't.

**Fix**: when `iso is None`, append a plain-English note to `overall` naming the field and the raw
value that couldn't be parsed, before the field still correctly drops out of `fields` (it never had a
usable value, so it shouldn't be proposed as one - that part of the existing behaviour was right).
Verified properly, not just read: reverted the fix, confirmed the new regression test fails with
exactly the predicted "field present, zero warnings anywhere" result, restored, confirmed it now
surfaces `"expiry date was mentioned in the document but couldn't be read as a date ('see addendum') -
check it and enter it by hand if needed."` at the document level. Added as a permanent regression test
in `test_classify_documents.py` (next to the existing year-only-placeholder-date test, same function).
Full `engine/onboarding/test_classify_documents.py` suite and `engine/cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py`
(shares the same `normalise_date()` helper via `cvx`) both clean before and after.

before starting, per the standing habit this routine adopted after getting burned by a stale
